title.rendered: OBASANJO GIVES RECIPE FOR AGING GRACEFULLY

content.rendered:
NIGERIA’S former President, Olusegun Obasanjo, says ageing is a natural process that cannot be reversed with drugs but could be attained gracefully by eating right, adequate rest, regular medical checkups, mental exercises, maintaining good social interaction and regular exercising.
Chief Obasanjo, in a lecture he delivered at the Elders’ Forum Meeting of the Chief Tony Anenih Geriatric Centre, University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, stated that ageing is inevitable, and so elderly people should not let anyone scare them with the issue of death.
According to him, “ageing does not mean that you must lose your tooth; even the graying hair is dignifying. Prepare for ageing; have savings for old age. Things are changing; our culture is changing so plan your old age, including having a well thought-out house that is safe to stay. Many aged people die, for instance, due to home accidents such as a fall in the bathroom.”
He added that as good as food is, if diet is not carefully planned, it can become poisonous. “The type of food, how we eat it and the combination we eat are as important as the amount taken. Intake of fruits and vegetables daily is also important,” he said.
He stressed the need for medical checkups to be conducted twice a year since the body is ageing, and detection and prompt treatment of any disease discovered will prevent complications and boost the quality of life.
“I was diagnosed with diabetes almost 40 years ago; some with the disease had died within five years because there is no drug for diabetes. It cannot be cured but diabetes can be managed. There is no disease that cannot be managed but you must know it early before it is advanced and so, the need for medical checkups,” he added.
Obasanjo reiterated the need for the elderly to have a first aid box at home, ensure that they get involved regularly in activities that will task their brains, maintain a healthy weight and good social interactions with friends, family and community members that will not pose stress to them.
Chief Obasanjo, declaring that he boosts his immunity with medicinal herbs, said the elderly could use medicinal herbs after talking with their doctors.
According to him, “bitter kola and kola nut are stimulants and have medicinal values. The herbal concoction (agbo) for boosting my immunity contains neem, pawpaw leaf, lime, ginger, garlic, turmeric, and so on. These are boiled for about 15 minutes in water and stored in the fridge. When I am ready to drink it, I warm it and sweeten it with honey.”
Earlier, UCH’s Chief Medical Director, Professor Jesse Otegbayo stated that the event is about the lifestyle and health of the elderly, just as he admonished them on how to keep fit even at very old age.
Otegbayo, speaking through the hospital’s chairman, Medical Advisory Committee, Dr Abiodun Adeoye, said it is expected that the event would provide the elderly with the impetus to continue to live healthier lives.
According to him, Chief Obasanjo is the most eminently qualified person to make his presentation on helpful tips to age gracefully.
“I have always believed that our former President has both the physical health and the mental capacity to tell us how to live a useful, elderly life,” he said.

title.rendered: Medical traditional practices and indigenous knowledge -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
It’s unfortunate that many medical traditional practices and indigenous knowledge are often overlooked or undervalued. By recognising and building upon our existing ingenuity, refining our methods, and combining them with modern research and training, we can unlock new opportunities for innovation and progress. Traditional medicine, for instance, is gaining attention for its potential to integrate evidence-based practices with modern healthcare, preserving cultural heritage while ensuring safety and efficacy.
Research and adoption are crucial steps in preserving and modernising traditional practices. Thorough research can help identify the most effective and sustainable aspects of traditional knowledge, which can then be integrated with modern innovations. This approach is particularly valuable in areas like traditional medicine, agriculture, and environmental conservation, where local knowledge and practices have been developed over centuries.
In health and medication, traditional knowledge can be particularly valuable. Many traditional remedies and practices have been used for centuries, and some have shown promising results. By researching and modernising these approaches, we can potentially discover new treatments or therapies that are effective, affordable, and accessible to more people. For example, some traditional African remedies have been found to have potent anti-malarial or anti-inflammatory properties.
When integrating traditional medicine with modern healthcare systems, ensuring safety and efficacy is a challenge. A nuanced approach is needed, respecting the value of traditional knowledge while applying rigorous scientific standards. By harnessing traditional opportunities, we can create more affordable and accessible solutions. However, this requires a pragmatic approach to governance and economic management, which is currently lacking. Without political goodwill and a people-centered approach, alternative solutions may struggle to gain traction.

title.rendered: Basic Sign Language 2.0

content.rendered:
The second edition of the Basic Sign Language Class was successfully held on Friday, 6th February, 2026, at the Palace of the Olowu of Owu, Abeokuta, under the theme “True Inclusive Communication: Leaving No One Behind.
The programme was organized by the Association of Sign Language Interpreters of Nigeria (ASLIN) in collaboration with the Olowu Hope Initiative (OHI) and aimed to promote inclusive communication and foster a society where no individual is excluded due to communication barriers.
Participants were provided with foundational sign language knowledge and trained on the importance of inclusive communication. The programme significantly contributed to raising awareness on accessible education and advancing the principles of inclusivity in Ogun State, reinforcing the commitment of OHI and ASLIN to leaving no one behind.
The event hosted ten pupils each from Peace Foundation International College, Gateway Secondary School, Anglican College, African Church Grammar School, Methodist High School, Unity High School, Landmark College, and Full Moon Academy.
Distinguished participants included Olori Ameenah Adeleye Matemilola, the Wife of Olowu of Owu, Abeokuta and the Matron ASLIN Ogun State Chapter, ASLIN Ogun State Chairman, Mr Seyi Ogunbayo,  representatives from the Ministry of Education, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Education – Alhaja Mrs. M. Oloko, the Director of SUBEB, the Director of Special Education, and the Honourable Commissioner for Education represented by Ms. Deborah Ogundimu.

title.rendered: SixthSense SmartWords – Do what needs to be done when it needs to be done, because doing it at another time may not be the right time

content.rendered:
With the above, I’m emphasising the importance of timing and taking action when it’s needed. Doing something at the right moment can make all the difference in achieving success or resolving issues. Delaying or doing it at a different time might not yield the same results.
This reminds me of the concept of “kairos” in Greek, which refers to the opportune moment or the right time to do something.
There are many issues associated with inappropriateness, the most challenging part of taking action at the right time is the sense of timing.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
-The SixthSense Initiative outreach.

title.rendered: ANA OGUN, ROCKCITY FM PARTNER TO PROMOTE LITERACY, READING

content.rendered:
The Association of Nigerian Authors, ANA, Ogun State Chapter has entered into a bilateral agreement with the authorities of Rockcity FM to promote literacy and reading.

The decision was taken on Wednesday when Executive Members of Ogun ANA led by the State Chairman, Chief Abiodun Lasile, paid a courtesy call on the Chief Executive Officer of Rockcity F.M., Dr. Niran Malaolu.
Chief Lasile, who is also the Orunto of Owu Kingdom, congratulated Rockcity FM for being the first private radio station in Abeokuta which also pioneered the first newspaper.
He commended the station for promptly informing, educating, entertaining and enlightening citizens through innovative programmes as well as giving citizens the platform to express their feelings.
Welcoming the Ogun ANA executives, Dr. Niran Malaolu, informed them of his plan to establish a writers’ hub at the Broadcasting House of Rockcity FM where transformative ideas for development would be incubated.
He confessed that since his mother introduced him to reading he had always had passion for writers adding that though he had only published one book, he had many unwritten books in his head.
He opined that the Nigerian society was not doing enough to encourage young people to read and recommended the Sweden Nokia example as recipe for boosting reading and development.
He challenged members of Ogun ANA to design a programme that would encourage and inspire young ones to think, write and make the society better than they met it.
Quoting Graham Greene’s book The Man Within, Dr. Malaolu said everybody had one or two books unwritten in the course of navigating the vagaries of life.

title.rendered: My Voice: Ogun @ 50 Story 1976 #2

content.rendered:
I was born in Ibadan, but my journey with Ogun State began in 1975 after my primary education when I moved to Akure. 
A year after the state creation, in 1977, we returned to Abeokuta, the state capital, just after the state creation. I was filled with enthusiasm and curiosity, eager to explore this new city. During my secondary school days, I got to know the nooks and crannies of Abeokuta, traversing the Egba townships and listening to the rich history of the land. These experiences have been invaluable to me.
In June 1980, I landed my first job through the Deputy Governor, Chief Sesan Soluade, at the old Governor’s Office in Oke Ilewo, Abeokuta. I was part of the Ogun State Civil Service, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, led by Commissioner Dr. Akinola.
At this juncture I must acknowledge Aiyekoto the first civilian governor, late Chief Olabisi Onabanjo under the Unity Party of Nigeria and ably led by the sage himself, another Ogun state personality, Chief Obafemi Awolowo of sweet political memories.
The ministry of home affairs was vast, with departments that would later become standalone ministries, including Information, Community Development, Fire Service, Forestry, Social Welfare, Arts and Culture, Government Press, and the Ten Local Government Areas. Most are fulfledged ministries with many departments under them.
After just six months in the civil service, I joined NTV Abeokuta at Ogbe in 1980 as one of its pioneer staff. The station was founded in 1979 and was a testament to the state’s growth and development.
I’m proud to celebrate Ogun State’s 50th birthday, and I’m grateful for the experiences that have shaped me into who I am today.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: “My Voice; Ogun @ 50 Story 1976”

content.rendered:
I was in secondary school in Akure, Ondo State, when states were created in Western Nigeria.
Our electrical shop was a hub for Egbas, Ijebus, and other Ogun indigenes, who gathered to play the game of Draughts and to discuss life. When the announcement came, excitement erupted, and applause filled the air. Even bystanders from nearby houses and Ondo State indigenes joined in, creating a joyful atmosphere. I was thrilled to hear Abeokuta mentioned, and I paid close attention to the optimistic discussions.
However, a seasoned draught player, Baba Ijebu, threw a spanner in the works, saying, “Ijebu Ode should have been the capital, not Abeokuta.” This sparked a heated debate, with camps forming and arguments flying to left and right.
 Unfortunately for Baba Ijebu, there were more Egbas present that day, and other Akure natives supported Abeokuta. As a teenager, I was elated that our town was supported to win the argument. Many people mentioned above as attendees at our game centre were soldiers and Yorubas, they said fingered Obasanjo’s connection, and his contributions to the state creation. The connection to our Owu indigene roots in Abeokuta was crystal clear.
The next day, I proudly announced to my school friends that our town, Abeokuta, was now a state capital, armed with knowledge gathered from the previous night’s discussions.
Happy 50th birthday, Ogun State, with Abeokuta as its capital!
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: TRIBUTE TO FELA ANIKULAPO KUTI, AS “HE WINS A DESERVED POSTHUMOUS GRAMMY AWARD”, FOR CREATING THE UNIQUE GENRE OF AFRO BEAT MUSIC TO THE WORLD IN 1962, AND FOR ALSO   USING MUSIC AS A WEAPON FOR OUR COLLECTIVE FIGHT AGAINST INJUSTICE  WORLDWIDE

content.rendered:
Fela’s Legacy Is Not About Wealth Or Money
Like Eric Donaldson sang in his irreplaceable classic, Land of My Birth to wit:
“The progress you make in life , is not always how rich you are”
Greatness is not measured by riches,but by immortal footprints in the sands of time relating to how one has impacted the society, nay the world.
Fela Improved The Positive Imaging Of The Blackman
Fela was an epitome of our collective struggles for world citizenship, black consciousness, negrito aspirations,fighting neo colonialism and deliberate miseducation.
He was a graduate of musicology from the prestigious Trinity College of Music in London
Afrobeats Is From Fela’s Afrobeat
And Fela was the undisputed founder of the  Afrobeat genre of music in 1962. The word Afrobeat was as coined by Fela’ s  English manager in 1962. This alone seamlessly makes Fela unbeatable. What Whiz Kid is now playing is Afrobeats which is a child of Afrobeat.
Afrobeats is a fusion of multiple beats to rhyme his jams. Whilst Fela is just the fusion of jazz and our native rhythm (kpangolo) according to Majek
With the latter version as a conveyor for black consciousness and freedom from mental slavery .And whilst also using same as a weapon for our emancipation
The Real And Original Wiz Kid Emerged From Great Uniben 36 Years Ago In 1990 Vide The Quill Magazine Naming Him De Whizzle
Even the name Wiz Kid is debatable as the Original “Whiz” is from the greatest of the greatest Uniben.
The full name na the”, Whizzle ‘ and so added the Wizard” cos as the guy dey groove and baff up, na so e dey pass him  exam like Wizard.
So the school shorten am to the,Wiz “( used interchangeably as the “whiz”) So if Fela spirit vex, I go sue for stolen alias in law.
Interestingly, in the Nigerian home video titled “Rampage”, shot inside Uniben, Francis Duru as the main character, when e baff up  come out for the film, dem hail am as “De Whiz”
Fela Founded Afro Beat In 1962 Ahead of Reggae In 1969 By Hibbert Maytal ( See Guinness Book of Records)
So if Fela founded Afrobeat 64 years ago,even ahead of Reggae in 1969, Fela cannot have a match locally or internationally
Fela Performed Globally And In The Americas Too
More significantly in the international scene, not only in France or Berlin, Fela also performed in the UK and particularly in the USA very well, with Sandra who introduced him to the teachings of Malcolm X
They later sang the hit track” Upside Down “
 I remember my dad bought from UK in mid 70s, the first Fela album in our house titled” Fela live in London”
As a diehard musical collector, I have that  CD in my archive I bought in 1995 during my post grad at the LSE
Fela Was Backed Up By Two Of The World ‘s Best Drummers To Wit:
Ginger Baker of the Legendary Rare Earth And Sly Dumbar ( just deceased) Of Taxi Promotions.
In his illuminating career, Fela had the exceptional privilege to be backed up by two of the world’s best drummers. The first is Ginger Baker of the legendary Rare Earth..Get Ready until I come. Baker was on the drums as they both played the scintillating “Yeye Dey Smell” in the 1974 Fela in London concert.
The second was Sly Dumbar of the Taxi Promotions
Sly before his passing last week was currently the world’s best drummer
And he has played with musical heavy weights like, Jimmy Cliff, Peter Tosh, Grace Jones, Black Uhuru etc. Sly played the drums for Fela in France on his master piece “Army Arrangement” using electric drums for the first time in Fela’ music
Fela Played All Musical Instruments Except The Guitar
Instructively, Fela plays all musical instruments apart from the guitar. Mr Ayodele Balogun, aka Wizkid, Which instrument you dey play?
See flavour on guitar and  Timaya on drums as well as Majek on acoustic lead  guitar  and even kpankolo sef; and see Emma Grey Afrik Wadada canning the drums
Dem don Born him  house before? For fighting for us?
Fela Voted Amongst 100 Most Influential People In The World By The Influential Time Magazine
And for the record, the world recognition which our kid bloodline is yet to ever receive, is Fela being listed in TIME MAGAZINE as one of The World’s Most Influential People in the year he passed
Only two Nigerians hitherto had been in the front of the prestigious Time Magazine, to wit: General Yakubu Gowon during the civil war, and Sade Adu in the mid 80s for winning Grammys vide her evergreen “Smooth Operator” album; and
Fela followed up in classic succession
Fela Winning Posthumous Grammy Award?
This is a well thought out and deserved honour to an unbeatable African irredentist and global revolutionary.
Fela’s music till date, like that of his equally formidable counterpart,the great Robert Nesta Marley, continues to lift the spirit of our collective struggles for all freedoms of mankind,and also  for global equality of all race in the comity of nations
“Me I No Go Gree Make My Brother Hungry ,Make I No Talk”
That is Compassion XD rate Fela for you ,as “Asset” to the” Collective”
Indeed,Fela was A BORN FREEDOM FIGHTER FOR THE OPPRESSED PEOPLE OF THIS “WILD” WORLD, as coined by the iconic, James Chambers aka Jimmy Cliff
Congratulations Ebami Eda.
Outstanding, Grandstanding ,Standing Ovation !!!
Dissemination by:
Dr Akpo Mudiaga Odje 
Constitutional Lawyer 
The Maiden And Original “Whiz”

Fela Voted Amongst 100 Most Influential People In The World By The Influential Time Magazine And for the record, the world recognition which our kid bloodline is yet to ever receive, is Fela being listed in TIME MAGAZINE as one of The World’s Most Influential People in the year he passed Only two Nigerians hitherto had been in the front of the prestigious Time Magazine, to wit: General Yakubu Gowon during the civil war, and Sade Adu in the mid 80s for winning Grammys vide her evergreen “Smooth Operator” album; and Fela followed up in classic succession Fela Winning Posthumous Grammy Award? This is a well thought out and deserved honour to an unbeatable African irredentist and global revolutionary. Fela’s music till date, like that of his equally formidable counterpart,the great Robert Nesta Marley, continues to lift the spirit of our collective struggles for all freedoms of mankind,and also  for global equality of all race in the comity of nations “Me I No Go Gree Make My Brother Hungry ,Make I No Talk” That is Compassion XD rate Fela for you ,as “Asset” to the” Collective” Indeed,Fela was A BORN FREEDOM FIGHTER FOR THE OPPRESSED PEOPLE OF THIS “WILD” WORLD, as coined by the iconic, James Chambers aka Jimmy Cliff Congratulations Ebami Eda. Outstanding, Grandstanding ,Standing Ovation !!! Dissemination by: Dr Akpo Mudiaga Odje  Constitutional Lawyer  The Maiden And Original “Whiz”

title.rendered: CHRISLAND UNIVERSITY PLEDGES SUPPORT FOR OGUN ANA

content.rendered:
The Vice Chancellor of Chrisland University, Professor Oyedunnisola Arulogun, has pledged to partner the Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) Ogun State Chapter in the area of capacity building  for staff and students of the University.

Professor Arulogun who stated this while receiving the Executive Members of Ogun ANA in her office said publication was a given for academicians who cannot progress without publishing.
She urged ANA to partner Chrisland University to improve the communication skills of students and assist them to discover their hidden creative skills which they can harness for wealth.
Speaking earlier, the Chairman of Ogun ANA and Orunto of Owu Kingdom, Dr. Abiodun Lasile asked for support to promote the flagging literacy and reading culture in the society through various activations on and off the university campus.
Also contributing, the Librarian of Chrisland University, Dr. Good luck Ifijeh urged writers to produce current books and stop the culture of reprinting old books adding that writers should use technology like the “turn-it-in” software to reduce plagiarism in books.
The Registrar of the University, Mr. Samuel Omotoso, in his own remarks underscored the importance of documentation and asked Ogun ANA to create a student wing of the Association to coordinate creative activities on campus.

title.rendered: WRITE BOOKS TO LIVE FOREVER – GM, PARAMOUNT FM

content.rendered:
Nigerians have been urged to write books to ensure their lives and times are recorded for posterity.
The General Manager, Paramount FM, Abeokuta, Mrs Oluremi Olugbenro, gave the advice while receiving the Executive Members of the Association of Nigerian Authors, ANA, Ogun State Chapter  in her office.
She said she would have created a special programme for ANA to propagate its activities but for the daunting challenge of power currently being faced by Paramount FM, Abeokuta.
She pledged continued support for the Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) and its activities on regular basis.
Also speaking, the station’s Head of Programmes, Pastor Oladapo Oyekanmi said ANA was not a stranger to Paramount FM adding that “having ANA as a partner is an asset”.
Speaking earlier, the Chairman of Ogun ANA, Dr. Abiodun Lasile, promised to enrich the library of Paramount FM with sundry books in order to further promote literacy and the reading culture in the society.
Dr. Lasile who is also the Orunto of Owu Kingdom asked for mutually beneficial partnerships that would boost literacy by enthroning knowledge in this fast paced, technologically driven world.

title.rendered: The Significance of Respect in Yoruba Tradition -Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
In Yoruba culture, tradition plays a vital role in shaping the values and behaviours of individuals, particularly children. One of the most important values that is deeply ingrained in Yoruba tradition is respect. Respect is not just a virtue, but a fundamental aspect of Yoruba identity that is expected to be upheld in all aspects of life. As the saying goes, “Tradition holds respect in high expectations in personality and it’s particularly necessary in the upbringing of a child.”
The Importance of Respect in Child Rearing
In Yoruba culture, children are taught from a young age to respect their elders, and this respect is not limited to just family members. Children are expected to show deference to older individuals in the community, using appropriate titles and greetings, and behaving in a manner that is respectful and obedient. This emphasis on respect is not just about teaching children to be subservient, but about instilling in them a sense of humility, empathy, and understanding of their place in the community.
The Consequences of Disrespect
In Yoruba society, disrespect towards elders is not taken lightly. Children who are disobedient or disrespectful are often chastised and taught the importance of respecting their elders. This approach may seem strict, but it is rooted in the understanding that respect is a fundamental value that is essential for building strong, harmonious relationships within the community. In fact, a child who is disrespectful to their elders is often viewed as an outcast, and this can have serious consequences for their social and emotional well-being.
The Virtue of Respect
Respect is a virtue that is highly valued in Yorubaland, and it is expected to be demonstrated in all aspects of life. Whether it’s within the family, compound, group, association, or in the streets, respect is seen as an essential component of social interaction. Children are taught to show respect to their elders, using titles such as Baba or Mama, and to at least greet them with a bow or a curtsy. This emphasis on respect helps to create a sense of community and social cohesion, where individuals understand their roles and responsibilities towards one another.
The Impact on Children
The emphasis on respect in Yoruba culture has a profound impact on children. From a young age, children are taught to prioritise respect and to understand the importance of treating others with dignity and respect. This helps to shape their worldview and informs their interactions with others. By instilling respect in children, Yoruba culture helps to create a sense of responsibility and accountability, which is essential for building strong, healthy relationships and achieving success in life.
In conclusion, respect is a fundamental value in Yoruba culture that is essential for building strong, harmonious relationships within the community. The emphasis on respect in child rearing helps to instill in children a sense of humility, empathy, and understanding of their place in the community. By prioritising respect, Yoruba culture helps to create a sense of social cohesion and responsibility, which is essential for achieving success and living a fulfilling life. As the Yoruba saying goes, A kii se ohun ti o ba agba je, which means “One does not do what would offend the elders.”
– Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Embracing Cultural Identity: A Message of Pride -Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

content.rendered:
In a world where cultural identity is often compromised in the name of modernity and innovation, Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta stands out as a beacon of cultural pride. His statement, “I’d rather proudly identify as Yoruba and intentionally celebrate my Owu heritage than adopt a foreign identity in the name of fashion or innovation,” is a powerful declaration of self-awareness, confidence, and cultural loyalty.

The Importance of Cultural Identity
Cultural identity is an essential part of who we are. It shapes our values, influences our worldview, and connects us to our heritage. For the Yoruba people, cultural identity is particularly significant, as it is deeply rooted in tradition, history, and community. By proudly identifying as Yoruba and celebrating his Owu heritage, Chief Abiodun Lasile is not only affirming his own identity but also promoting a sense of cultural awareness and appreciation.
The Dangers of Cultural Imitation
In contrast, the adoption of foreign identities in the name of fashion or innovation can be seen as a form of cultural imitation. When we abandon our cultural heritage in favor of something foreign, we risk losing our sense of identity and cultural continuity. This can lead to a form of cultural dissonance, where individuals are caught between two cultures, unsure of where they truly belong.
The Value of Cultural Preservation
Chief Abiodun Lasile’s statement highlights the importance of cultural preservation. By celebrating his Owu heritage, he is helping to preserve the cultural traditions and values of his community. This is particularly significant in today’s world, where cultural homogenisation is a growing concern. By embracing and celebrating our cultural differences, we can promote a more diverse and inclusive society.
A Call to Action
Chief Abiodun Lasile’s statement is not just a declaration of cultural pride; it’s also a call to action. It’s a
reminder
that we should be proud of our cultural heritage and actively work to preserve it. By doing so, we can promote a sense of cultural awareness and appreciation, and help to create a more diverse and inclusive society.

In conclusion, Chief Abiodun Lasile’s statement is a powerful reminder of the importance of cultural identity and the need to preserve our cultural heritage. By proudly identifying as Yoruba and celebrating his Owu heritage, he is setting an example for others to follow. As we navigate the complexities of modernity and innovation, it’s essential that we don’t forget the value of our cultural roots. By embracing and celebrating our cultural differences, we can promote a more diverse and inclusive society, and create a brighter future for generations to come.

-The SixthSense Initiative outreach

title.rendered: The Enduring Value of Traditional Politics -Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

content.rendered:
In a world where partisan politics often dominates the landscape, it’s refreshing to see traditional politics emerge as a beacon of hope. This form of politics is not about winning elections or gaining power, but about serving the people with integrity, wisdom, and a deep understanding of the community’s values and traditions. As Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta so aptly puts it, “Among the various forms of politics, traditional politics stands out as a refreshing alternative. It’s not about partisan maneuvering, empty promises, or deceit, but about speaking truth to the people, rooted in tradition, custom, and culture.”
The Essence of Traditional Politics
Traditional politics is about more than just governance; it’s about stewardship, community, and the preservation of cultural heritage. It’s a politics that is deeply rooted in the values and traditions of the community, and one that seeks to promote the common good above personal or partisan interests. This approach to politics recognises that the well-being of the community is paramount, and that leaders should be guided by a sense of responsibility to their people, rather than personal ambition.
The Importance of Cultural Context
One of the key strengths of traditional politics is its ability to tap into the cultural context of the community. By understanding and respecting the traditions, customs, and values of the people, leaders can build trust and foster a sense of unity and purpose. This approach also recognises that cultural identity is an essential part of who we are, and that it should be celebrated and preserved, rather than suppressed or ignored.
The Challenges of Modern Politics
In contrast, modern politics often seems to prioritise partisan interests over the needs of the community. The emphasis on winning elections and gaining power can lead to a focus on short-term gains, rather than long-term solutions. The use of deceit, manipulation, and empty promises can erode trust and create divisions within the community. In this context, traditional politics offers a refreshing alternative, one that prioritises integrity, wisdom, and a deep understanding of the community’s values and traditions.
The Benefits of Traditional Politics
So, what are the benefits of traditional politics? For one, it offers a more authentic and meaningful form of governance, one that is rooted in the values and traditions of the community. It also provides a sense of stability and continuity, as leaders are guided by a deep understanding of the community’s history and cultural heritage. Additionally, traditional politics can help to promote a sense of community and shared purpose, as leaders and citizens work together to address common challenges and achieve shared goals.
In conclusion, traditional politics offers a powerful alternative to the partisan politics that often dominates our

discourse. By prioritising integrity, wisdom, and a deep understanding of the community’s values and traditions, we can build a more just, equitable, and prosperous society. As Chief Abiodun Lasile so aptly puts it, traditional politics is about “speaking truth to the people, rooted in tradition, custom, and culture.” By embracing this approach, we can create a brighter future for ourselves and for generations to come.

-The SixthSense Initiative outreach

title.rendered: Before the Flames: Fela Kuti’s Original Afrika Shrine in Mushin, Lagos

content.rendered:
Long before it became a legend spoken of in hushed reverence, the Afrika Shrine in Mushin, Lagos, stood as a living monument to resistance, music, and radical thought.

  Established by Fela Anikulapo Kuti, the Shrine     was  far more than a performance venue. It was a    cultural headquarters, a political classroom, a          recording space, and a bold challenge to         Nigeria’s military establishment.
  The photograph taken before 18 February 1977       preserves a moment in time before the Shrine was     violently erased during one of the most infamous military    raids in Nigeria’s cultural history.
  The Birth of the Afrika Shrine
  The original Afrika Shrine was founded in the early           1970s in Mushin, a densely populated

 

   working-class area of Lagos. Fela deliberately situated     the Shrine outside elite spaces, aligning it with the people whose struggles he chronicled through Afrobeat.
At the time, Mushin was a melting pot of street life, commerce, and political agitation. The Shrine naturally became a gathering place for artists, students, activists, and everyday Lagosians seeking expression beyond state-controlled narratives.
A Home, Not Just a Stage
Unlike conventional music venues, the Shrine functioned as Fela’s home and a communal living space. Members of his band, family, and associates lived and worked there. This communal structure mirrored Fela’s rejection of Western individualism and reflected his embrace of African communal values.
The space blurred the lines between private life and public performance. Music, conversation, ideology, and daily life flowed into one another without separation.
Nightly Rituals and Musical Revolution
Performances at the Afrika Shrine typically began around midnight, often stretching into the early hours of the morning. These sessions were not just concerts. They were rituals.
Fela used the stage to dissect Nigerian politics, military authoritarianism, colonial legacies, and social hypocrisy. Songs were introduced with lengthy monologues delivered in Pidgin English, ensuring accessibility across class and educational boundaries.
The Shrine also doubled as a recording space, where experimental arrangements were tested live before audiences, shaping the raw, extended compositions that defined Afrobeat.
Symbol of Defiance
By the mid-1970s, the Afrika Shrine had become a visible symbol of artistic and political rebellion. Its influence extended beyond music into social consciousness.
Military authorities increasingly viewed the Shrine as a threat. Fela’s criticism of government corruption, police brutality, and military excesses directly challenged Nigeria’s ruling elite during an era of authoritarian rule.
The Military Invasion of 18 February 1977
On 18 February 1977, Nigerian soldiers launched a coordinated assault on the Kalakuta Republic, Fela’s nearby commune, and the Afrika Shrine. The invasion followed years of escalating hostility between Fela and the military government.
The original Shrine in Mushin was destroyed during this attack. Buildings were razed, property was destroyed, and the cultural centre that had housed one of Africa’s most powerful artistic movements was wiped out.
The invasion marked a turning point in Nigeria’s cultural history and solidified Fela’s global image as an uncompromising voice against oppression.
Aftermath and Legacy
Although the original Afrika Shrine was destroyed, its spirit survived. Fela later established new versions of the Shrine, ensuring continuity of performance and resistance.
Today, the original Shrine is remembered not as a lost building but as a foundational chapter in African musical and political history. It remains a symbol of what happens when art refuses to be silenced by power.
Historical Significance
The image of the Shrine before its destruction captures more than architecture. It documents a space where African music, political thought, and communal life converged in defiance of authoritarian rule.
The Mushin Afrika Shrine stands as evidence that cultural spaces can become sites of resistance, capable of unsettling governments and inspiring generations.
Sources
Nigerian national archives and documented histories of the 1977 Kalakuta invasion
Published biographies of Fela Anikulapo Kuti
The Punch historical features on Fela and the Afrika Shrine

title.rendered: The Pursuit of Wisdom -Orunto Owu Kingdom

content.rendered:
In a world where knowledge is abundant and information is readily available, it’s easy to overlook the value of wisdom. Wisdom is not just about knowing facts or figures;

 it’s about understanding the world and its complexities. It’s about making informed decisions, navigating life’s challenges, and finding meaning and purpose. According to Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR, “Wisdom is from God, and association with elders adds practical experience; sensible elders are indeed friends.” This profound quote highlights the importance of seeking wisdom from a higher power and gaining practical experience through interactions with elders.
The Divine Source of Wisdom
The quote begins by acknowledging that wisdom comes from God. This perspective recognises that there is a higher power at work in the universe, guiding and directing us towards wisdom. It’s a reminder that wisdom is not solely the product of human ingenuity or intelligence, but rather a gift from a divine source. By acknowledging this, we can approach wisdom with humility and reverence, recognising that it’s a treasure to be cherished and respected.
The Value of Practical Experience
The second part of the quote emphasises the importance of association with elders in gaining practical experience. Elders have lived through various experiences, faced challenges, and made decisions that have shaped their lives. By interacting with them, we can gain valuable insights into how to navigate life’s complexities, make informed decisions, and avoid pitfalls. Practical experience is a powerful teacher, and learning from those who have gone before us can save us time, energy, and heartache.
The Role of Sensible Elders
The quote also highlights the importance of associating with sensible elders. Not all elders are created equal, and it’s essential to seek out those who possess wisdom, integrity, and a deep understanding of the world. Sensible elders are not just knowledgeable; they are also wise, compassionate, and discerning. They can offer guidance, support, and encouragement, helping us to navigate life’s challenges with confidence and clarity.
The Friendship of Elders
The quote concludes by noting that sensible elders are indeed friends. This is a beautiful perspective on the relationship between younger and older individuals. When we associate with elders, we can form meaningful bonds that transcend age and generational differences. Elders can become mentors, coaches, and friends, offering us a unique perspective on life and helping us to grow and develop as individuals.
In conclusion, the quote “Wisdom is from God, and association with elders adds practical experience; sensible elders are indeed friends” offers valuable insights into the pursuit of wisdom. By recognising the divine source of wisdom, gaining practical experience through interactions with elders, and associating with sensible individuals, we can cultivate wisdom and live more meaningful lives. As we navigate the complexities of the world, let us seek wisdom from those who have gone before us, and let us cherish the relationships we form with elders who can guide and support us on our journey.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

title.rendered: The Art of Crafting One’s Personality

content.rendered:
In a world where conformity often seems like the easiest path, it’s refreshing to see individuals who dare to be different. I love the beauty of creating when it comes to personality, and it’s a journey that requires immense courage and self-awareness. To be able to stand out and be known for who you truly are is a remarkable feat. It’s not just about living like any other person, blending in with the crowd, and following the status quo. No, it’s about embracing your individuality and declaring to the world, “This is me, irrespective of the path I’ve chosen.
The Paradox of Uniqueness
What’s fascinating is that while people claim to love distinct personalities, they often struggle with envy and insecurity when confronted with someone who embodies those qualities. They may admire the confidence, creativity, and charisma of others, but when faced with someone who possesses these traits, they can’t help but feel threatened. Uniqueness becomes their grouse, and they may try to tear down the very thing they claim to admire.
The Deliberate Craft of Personality Creation
Personality creation is not a happenstance; it’s a deliberate consciousness of practices, perseverance, prices, courage, and focus, among other behavioral patterns. It requires a deep understanding of oneself, a willingness to take risks, and the resilience to overcome obstacles. When you set out to create a personality that’s authentic and meaningful, you’re not just building a persona; you’re crafting a work of art that reflects your values, passions, and experiences.
The Courage to Be Yourself
It takes guts to be able to be known for who you are, without apology or pretension. It means embracing your strengths and weaknesses, your quirks and flaws, and being willing to share them with the world. When you’re confident in your own skin, you’re unstoppable. You’re no longer held back by the opinions of others, and you’re free to pursue your passions with reckless abandon.
The Reward of Authenticity
The journey of personality creation is not without its challenges, but the reward is well worth the effort. When you’re true to yourself, you exude a sense of confidence and authenticity that’s hard to ignore. You’re no longer just a face in the crowd; you’re a beacon of hope, inspiration, and creativity. You’re a reminder to others that they too can be bold, take risks, and forge their own path.
No Pain, No Gain
As the saying goes, “No pain, no gain.” The process of creating a personality that’s authentic and meaningful requires hard work, dedication, and perseverance. There will be times when you’ll face criticism, rejection, and self-doubt, but it’s in those moments that you’ll discover your true strength. By embracing the challenges and learning from your experiences, you’ll emerge stronger, wiser, and more confident. So, if you’re ready to embark on the journey of personality creation, be prepared to face the challenges head-on, and remember, the reward is well worth the effort.
Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta.
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative and Sixth Sense Series Publications.
Chairman Association of Nigerian Authors (Ogun Chapter)

title.rendered: The Power of Being Driven: Unleashing Potential for Humanity’s Service -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
As individuals, we all possess unique qualities that set us apart and drive us towards achieving our goals. For some, it’s the pursuit of excellence, while for others, it’s the desire to make a difference. When we tap into our inner drive, we unlock our full potential and become unstoppable forces for change.
The Driving Force
Being driven is more than just a personality trait; it’s a mindset that propels us forward, even in the face of adversity. It’s the spark that ignites the flame of passion, motivating us to work tirelessly towards our objectives. For those who are driven, there’s no obstacle too great, no challenge too insurmountable. We’re fueled by an insatiable desire to succeed, to innovate, and to push beyond the boundaries of what’s possible.
Passion towards Humanity’s Service
What drives Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR is a passion towards humanity’s service. This noble pursuit is a testament to the human spirit’s capacity for empathy, compassion, and kindness. When we’re driven by a desire to serve others, we tap into a deep well of motivation that goes beyond personal gain or recognition. We’re motivated by the knowledge that our actions can positively impact the lives of others, making the world a better place.
The Benefits of Being Driven
Being driven has numerous benefits, both for the individual and society as a whole. When we’re driven, we’re more focused, more productive, and more resilient. We’re better equipped to overcome obstacles, and we’re more likely to achieve our goals. Moreover, our drive can inspire others, creating a ripple effect that can lead to positive change.
Unleashing Potential
When we combine being driven with a passion for humanity’s service, we unleash a powerful force for good. We become agents of change, working towards creating a world that’s more just, equitable, and compassionate. By harnessing our inner drive, we can make a meaningful difference in the lives of others, leaving a lasting legacy that transcends our own lifetimes.
Conclusion
In conclusion, being driven is a powerful motivator that can help us achieve our goals and pursue our passions. When combined with a passion for humanity’s service, it can be a game-changer. As Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR so eloquently puts it, “What drives me is passion towards humanity’s service.” May we all find our driving force and use it to make a positive impact on the world.
-The SixthSense Initiative outreach

The Benefits of Being Driven Being driven has numerous benefits, both for the individual and society as a whole. When we’re driven, we’re more focused, more productive, and more resilient. We’re better equipped to overcome obstacles, and we’re more likely to achieve our goals. Moreover, our drive can inspire others, creating a ripple effect that can lead to positive change. Unleashing Potential When we combine being driven with a passion for humanity’s service, we unleash a powerful force for good. We become agents of change, working towards creating a world that’s more just, equitable, and compassionate. By harnessing our inner drive, we can make a meaningful difference in the lives of others, leaving a lasting legacy that transcends our own lifetimes. Conclusion In conclusion, being driven is a powerful motivator that can help us achieve our goals and pursue our passions. When combined with a passion for humanity’s service, it can be a game-changer. As Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR so eloquently puts it, “What drives me is passion towards humanity’s service.” May we all find our driving force and use it to make a positive impact on the world. -The SixthSense Initiative outreach

title.rendered: 60TH ANNIVERSARY OF  NIGERA’S FIRST MILITARY COUP DETAT

content.rendered:
On Saturday, 15th January,1966, Nigerians woke up to the cold sound of martial music on radio. It was an eerie announcement of the country’s first  military coup.
Among the many casualties of that coup were the country’s Prime Minister, Finance Minister, the Premiers of the now-defunct Western Region of Nigeria and Northern Region of Nigeria, top senior military officers, civilians etc.
Photograph shows Dr Abimbola Akintola, the 87-year old medical doctor younger daughter of  Premier Akintola who was a two-time Federal Minister of Finance presenting me with the portrait of her late father at the 2024 SLA MEMORIAL LECTURE/AWARD HELD AT the House of Chiefs, Secretariat, Agodi Ibadan, Oyo State
I chaired the ceremony.
-Oloye Lekan Alabi 
Abese Olubadan ti ile Ibadan

title.rendered: Leadership Boundaries and Merit-Based Decision Making: The Foundation of Good Governance -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
As we navigate the complexities of modern leadership, it’s essential to recognise the importance of boundaries and merit-based decision making in ensuring good governance. In a democratic system, decisions should be guided by standards and principles, rather than personal relationships or nepotism. The need for leadership that prioritises merit, transparency, and accountability has never been more pressing.
The Dangers of Nepotism and Favouritism
Favouring family members or friends in leadership positions can have far-reaching consequences. It can undermine the integrity of institutions, create unequal opportunities, and breed corruption. When leaders prioritise personal relationships over merit, they compromise the effectiveness and legitimacy of their institutions. This can lead to a lack of trust, decreased morale, and reduced productivity among employees or citizens.
The Importance of Merit-Based Decision Making
Merit-based decision making is a fundamental principle of good governance. It ensures that decisions are based on objective criteria, such as qualifications, skills, and experience. This approach promotes fairness, equality, and justice, and enables institutions to attract and retain the best talent. When leaders prioritise merit, they demonstrate their commitment to excellence and accountability.
The Role of Leadership Boundaries
Leadership boundaries are essential in maintaining the integrity of institutions. Boundaries help leaders to distinguish between their personal and professional roles, and prevent the abuse of power. When leaders establish clear boundaries, they demonstrate their commitment to transparency, accountability, and good governance. Boundaries also help to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure that decisions are made in the best interest of the institution or community.
The Benefits of Good Governance
Good governance is not just a moral imperative; it’s also essential for economic growth, stability, and prosperity. When institutions are guided by merit-based decision making and strong leadership boundaries, they are more likely to attract investment, promote innovation, and deliver public services effectively. Good governance also promotes trust and confidence in institutions, which is essential for social cohesion and stability.
Promoting Leadership that Prioritises Merit and Accountability
So, what can we do to promote leadership that prioritises merit and accountability? First, we need to recognise the importance of leadership boundaries and merit-based decision making. We need to encourage leaders to prioritise transparency, accountability, and fairness in their decision-making processes. We also need to support institutions that promote good governance, such as independent judiciaries, free press, and civil society organizations.
Conclusion
In conclusion, leadership boundaries and merit-based decision making are essential components of good governance. By prioritising merit, transparency, and accountability, leaders can promote fairness, equality, and justice. We need to recognise the dangers of nepotism and favouritism, and promote leadership that is guided by principles and standards. Let’s work together to build institutions that are strong, effective, and accountable to the people they serve.
Chief Abiodun Lasile’s Vision
As Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta and Chairman Association of Nigerian Authors (Ogun Chapter), I am committed to promoting leadership that prioritises merit, transparency, and accountability. I believe that good governance is essential for the development and prosperity of our communities. Let’s work together to build a brighter future for ourselves and future generations.

title.rendered: APENA EGBA: Chief Suarau Alani Bankole

content.rendered:
Chief Suarau Olayiwola Alani Bankole (born September 17, 1941) is a distinguished Egba businessman, industrialist, and traditional chieftain from Ogun State, Nigeria. Widely respected in both the corporate and traditional spheres, he has played a significant role in Nigeria’s private-sector development while also occupying highly regarded positions within the Egba traditional hierarchy.
Early Life and Education
Chief Bankole was born into an Egba family in Abeokuta, a city renowned for producing many of Nigeria’s foremost intellectuals, entrepreneurs, and national leaders. He received his secondary education at the prestigious Baptist Boys’ High School (BBHS), Abeokuta, one of the oldest and most influential secondary schools in Nigeria. The discipline, leadership training, and strong alumni culture of BBHS helped shape his outlook on enterprise, service, and community responsibility.
Business Career and Entrepreneurship
Chief Bankole built a formidable reputation in Nigerian business through decades of entrepreneurial activity and corporate leadership. He is best known for his association with the manufacturing and industrial sector, having served as Chairman of West African Aluminum Products Plc (WAPCO/WAAPCO), a company that became prominent in the aluminum and building materials industry. Under his leadership, the company strengthened its corporate governance profile and expanded its relevance within Nigeria’s industrial landscape.
In addition to his role in manufacturing, Chief Bankole is the founder of Freight Agencies Nigeria Ltd, an indigenous freight forwarding and logistics company established at a time when the sector was largely dominated by foreign interests. The company is often regarded as one of the pioneering Nigerian-owned freight agencies, contributing to the growth of local capacity in shipping, customs clearing, and international trade facilitation.
Through these ventures, Chief Bankole became known for encouraging indigenous participation in commerce, mentoring younger entrepreneurs, and demonstrating that Nigerian-owned companies could compete effectively in complex and capital-intensive sectors.
Traditional Titles and Cultural Role
Beyond business, Chief Bankole occupies an eminent place in Egba traditional society. He holds the respected titles of Oluwo of Iporo Ake and Apena of Egbaland, positions that place him close to the heart of Egba traditional governance and cultural life. These titles are not merely honorary; they come with responsibilities related to community leadership, conflict resolution, cultural preservation, and advisory roles within the Egba traditional council.
His standing as a traditional chief reflects the trust reposed in him by the Egba people and underscores the long-standing Yoruba tradition of recognizing individuals who have achieved distinction and rendered service to their communities.
Personal Life and Family
Chief Bankole was married to Chief (Mrs.) Atinuke Bankole, who held the prestigious title of Ekerin Iyalode of Egbaland, a significant position within the women’s traditional leadership structure. Their union further reinforced the family’s prominence within Egba society.
He is the father of Dimeji Bankole, who served as Speaker of the House of Representatives of Nigeria (2007–2011), one of the highest legislative offices in the country. Through his family, Chief Bankole’s influence has extended into national political life, complementing his achievements in business and tradition.
Legacy and Significance
Chief Suarau Olayiwola Alani Bankole represents a generation of Nigerian businessmen who combined entrepreneurship with cultural rootedness and public relevance. His legacy lies in:
-Advancing indigenous participation in industry and logistics
-Providing corporate leadership in Nigeria’s manufacturing sector
-Upholding and strengthening Egba traditional institutions
-Raising a family that has contributed to national public life
He remains a notable example of the intersection between commerce, culture, and leadership in modern Nigerian history.

title.rendered: The Imperative of Respect and Restraint: A Kingmaker’s Perspective  -Orunto Owu

content.rendered:
As a kingmaker, I believe that monarchs and crown heads must prioritise mutual respect and restraint, particularly in public. These leaders are human beings first, and their ascension to traditional stools or thrones does not exempt them from the fundamental principles of decency and respect. In fact, their exalted positions demand even higher standards of behaviour, attitude, and character.
The Weight of Tradition and Expectation
Kings and monarchs are expected to embody the values and traditions of their heritage, and their behaviour is often seen as a reflection of their people and culture. As such, they must be mindful of their actions and words, lest they be perceived as unbecoming or unbefitting of their office. The assumption that spirits guide them and their ways only adds to the weight of expectation, and they must be careful not to desecrate their position through petty squabbles or acrimonious sentiments.
The Challenges of Modern Times
In today’s fast-paced world, monarchs face unique challenges that require a high level of tolerance and perseverance. The speed of transmission and the scrutiny of the public eye can be overwhelming, and it’s essential that they exercise restraint and accommodation to avoid public embarrassment. The fact that their followers and subjects may take things beyond boundaries only adds to the complexity of their role.
A Call to Action:
As a kingmaker, I’m compelled to urge monarchs and their custodians to take heed of these challenges and to prioritise respect, restraint, and wisdom in their words and actions. The throne is not just a symbol of power, but also a symbol of responsibility and accountability. In this era of rapid change and technological advancements, it’s more important than ever that our kings and monarchs remain steadfast in their commitment to tradition, values, and the well-being of their people.
A Voice at the Corridor of the Palace
I offer this perspective as a kingmaker, with the utmost respect and concern for the dignity and integrity of the throne. I believe that by working together, we can ensure that our monarchs and crown heads continue to inspire and uplift their people, while also upholding the values and traditions that have been passed down through generations.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Preventing Fractures in the Elderly: Crucial Advice from an Orthopaedic Doctor

content.rendered:
As we age, our bones naturally lose density, making us more prone to fractures. According to Dr. Shrujal Shah, an Orthopaedic and Joint Replacement Surgeon, the key to preventing fractures in the elderly is to prevent accidental injuries. Dr. Shah emphasizes that “one fall can cost ten years of life,” highlighting the importance of taking proactive measures to ensure safety.
The Three Golden Rules
Dr. Shah’s advice can be summed up in three simple yet crucial rules: “Be careful, be careful, be careful again.” These rules may seem straightforward, but they are essential in preventing accidents and fractures. By being mindful of our surroundings and taking necessary precautions, we can significantly reduce the risk of falls and injuries.
Specific Measures to Prevent Accidental Injuries
To reduce the risk of accidental injuries, Dr. Shah recommends the following specific measures:
1. Avoid standing on chairs or stools: Never stand on a chair or stool to get something, even if it’s a low stool. Instead, use a step stool or ask for help.
2. Stay indoors on rainy days: Try to avoid going out on rainy days to minimize the risk of slipping and falling.
3. Take care when bathing or using the toilet: Be cautious when bathing or using the toilet, and ensure that the floor is dry and non-slippery. Use handrails and grab bars for support.
4. Wear underwear safely: When putting on underwear, sit comfortably on a chair or bed to avoid slipping and falling.
5. Ensure a safe bathroom environment: Clean up clutter on the floor, use a commode with handrails, and fix a hand rest to hold onto while getting up from the commode seat.
6. Be mindful of wet floors: Take extra care when walking on wet floors, and ensure that they are cleaned up promptly.
7. Get up slowly: When getting up from bed or a chair, sit for a few minutes before standing up, and turn on the light first.
8. Have a safety system in place: Consider installing an alarm bell in the toilet or keeping the door unlocked in case of emergencies.
9. Sit while dressing: Seniors should sit on a chair or bed while dressing to avoid falling.
10. Fall safely: If you do fall, try to stretch out your hands to break your fall and avoid fracturing your hip or spine.
Additional Tips for Bone Health
In addition to preventing accidental injuries, Dr. Shah emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong bones through:
1. Exercise: Engage in regular exercise, such as walking, to improve bone density and overall health.
2. Dietary supplements: Consume dietary supplements like dairy products, soy products, and bananas that are rich in calcium.
3. Sun exposure: Spend time outdoors to get vitamin D from sunlight, which helps promote calcium absorption and bone health.
4. Weight management: Maintain a healthy weight through a balanced diet and regular exercise to reduce the risk of osteoporosis and fractures.
Conclusion
By following these simple yet crucial tips, seniors can significantly reduce their risk of fractures and maintain their independence. Dr. Shah’s advice is clear: be careful, take necessary precautions, and prioritize bone health. By doing so, we can prevent fractures and ensure a healthier, happier life in our golden years.
-The SixthSense Initiative outreach

Avoid standing on chairs or stools: Never stand on a chair or stool to get something, even if it’s a low stool. Instead, use a step stool or ask for help. 2. Stay indoors on rainy days: Try to avoid going out on rainy days to minimize the risk of slipping and falling. 3. Take care when bathing or using the toilet: Be cautious when bathing or using the toilet, and ensure that the floor is dry and non-slippery. Use handrails and grab bars for support. 4. Wear underwear safely: When putting on underwear, sit comfortably on a chair or bed to avoid slipping and falling. 5. Ensure a safe bathroom environment: Clean up clutter on the floor, use a commode with handrails, and fix a hand rest to hold onto while getting up from the commode seat. 6. Be mindful of wet floors: Take extra care when walking on wet floors, and ensure that they are cleaned up promptly. 7. Get up slowly: When getting up from bed or a chair, sit for a few minutes before standing up, and turn on the light first. 8. Have a safety system in place: Consider installing an alarm bell in the toilet or keeping the door unlocked in case of emergencies. 9. Sit while dressing: Seniors should sit on a chair or bed while dressing to avoid falling. 10. Fall safely: If you do fall, try to stretch out your hands to break your fall and avoid fracturing your hip or spine. Additional Tips for Bone Health In addition to preventing accidental injuries, Dr. Shah emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong bones through: 1. Exercise: Engage in regular exercise, such as walking, to improve bone density and overall health. 2. Dietary supplements: Consume dietary supplements like dairy products, soy products, and bananas that are rich in calcium. 3. Sun exposure: Spend time outdoors to get vitamin D from sunlight, which helps promote calcium absorption and bone health. 4. Weight management: Maintain a healthy weight through a balanced diet and regular exercise to reduce the risk of osteoporosis and fractures. Conclusion By following these simple yet crucial tips, seniors can significantly reduce their risk of fractures and maintain their independence. Dr. Shah’s advice is clear: be careful, take necessary precautions, and prioritize bone health. By doing so, we can prevent fractures and ensure a healthier, happier life in our golden years. -The SixthSense Initiative outreach

title.rendered: The Power of Knowing One’s History and Identity: A Perspective from a Traditional Leader* -Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
As the Orunto of Owu Kingdom, I have come to realise the immense value of understanding one’s history and identity. It is a conviction that has guided my actions and decisions as a traditional leader, and one that I believe can benefit individuals and communities alike. Knowing one’s history and identity can profoundly shape our lives, and it is a responsibility that we must take seriously.
The Significance of History and Identity
Our history and identity are the foundation upon which our communities are built. They define who we are, where we come from, and what we stand for. By understanding our history, we can learn from the triumphs and mistakes of our ancestors, and use those lessons to build a better future for ourselves and future generations.
As a traditional leader, I have seen firsthand the impact that a strong sense of history and identity can have on a community. When individuals understand their roots and cultural heritage, they are more likely to feel a sense of belonging and purpose. This, in turn, can lead to greater community cohesion, social stability, and economic prosperity.
The Responsibility that Comes with Knowing One’s History and Identity
Knowing one’s history and identity is not just a privilege, but also a responsibility. It is our duty to preserve and promote our cultural heritage, and to ensure that the lessons of the past are not lost to the sands of time. This responsibility extends not just to individuals, but also to communities and future generations.
As the Orunto of Owu Kingdom, I have made it my mission to promote the cultural heritage of my kingdom and to ensure that our history is preserved for generations to come. This includes supporting initiatives that document and celebrate our customs, traditions, and history, as well as encouraging young people to learn about and appreciate their cultural heritage.
The Benefits of Knowing One’s History and Identity
The benefits of knowing one’s history and identity are numerous. It can help individuals develop a sense of pride and self-worth, and provide a framework for understanding their place in the world. It can also foster greater empathy and understanding between different cultures and communities, and promote tolerance and respect for diversity.
In my own life, knowing my history and identity has been a source of strength and inspiration. It has helped me navigate the complexities of traditional leadership and has given me a sense of purpose and direction. I believe that it can do the same for others, and I encourage individuals and communities to explore their history and identity with pride.
Conclusion
In conclusion, knowing one’s history and identity is a powerful tool that can shape our lives in profound ways. It is a responsibility that we must take seriously, and one that requires effort and dedication. As a traditional leader, I am committed to promoting the cultural heritage of my kingdom and to ensuring that our history is preserved for generations to come. I hope that others will join me in this endeavor, and that together, we can build a brighter future for ourselves and for our communities.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom

title.rendered: 2026 Special Service

content.rendered:
The Armed Forces celebration and remembrance day in Nigeria is a week-long event, marked with various activities, including the launch of an emblem and special services for Christians, Muslims, and other faiths.
The main programme takes place on January 15th, where the government of Nigeria honours the nation’s fallen heroes and heroines alongside the Legion. It is all inclusive, the veterans and their families.
This year’s celebration serves as a poignant reminder of the call to peace and the importance of unity.
A special service was held at the Cathedral of St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Ake, Abeokuta, where I represented HRM Oba Prof. Saka Adelola Matemilola, FNSE Otileta VII, Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, with Osupori Owu in paying tribute to our brave heroes.
Let’s hope all is well with everyone in this nation without greed!
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR, Orunto Baalufe Owu

title.rendered: Ability of Oneself and Understanding History -Orunto Owu

content.rendered:
Knowing oneself and understanding history are crucial to maintaining one’s identity. By understanding our past, culture, and heritage, we gain a sense of belonging and purpose. This knowledge helps us navigate life’s complexities and make informed decisions about our future. The saying ‘Those who do not learn from history are doomed to repeat it’ underscores the importance of studying history to learn from our ancestors’ triumphs and mistakes. This self-awareness and historical knowledge foster a deeper understanding of ourselves and others, allowing us to appreciate our unique experiences, traditions, and perspectives.
Knowing one’s history and identity can profoundly impact our lives in several ways:
– Sense of Belonging: Connecting with our roots and community through our history and cultural heritage provides a sense of belonging and purpose.
– Self-Awareness: Understanding our past and cultural context helps us understand who we are, what we value, and where we’re going, driving personal growth and development.
– Informed Decision-Making: Learning from our ancestors’ experiences and mistakes enables us to make informed decisions and avoid past errors.
– Cultural Appreciation: Studying our history and culture promotes appreciation for our traditions, customs, and values, leading to greater pride and respect for our heritage.
– Empowerment: Knowing our history and identity empowers us to take control of our narrative, shape our destiny, and make positive contributions to our communities.
– Intergenerational Connection: Understanding our history connects us with our ancestors and future generations, providing a sense of continuity and responsibility to preserve our legacy.
– Personal and Collective Growth: Learning from our past helps us identify areas for improvement, driving personal and collective growth and leading to a more fulfilling life.
In essence, knowing one’s history and identity is vital for building a strong sense of self, fostering community connections, and navigating life’s complexities with purpose and direction.”
–Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: The Cordiality between Oba Gbadebo and Oba Matemilola

content.rendered:
HRM Oba Dr Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo CFR Okukenu IV, the revered Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, and HRM Oba Prof Saka Matemilola FNSE, the esteemed Olowu of Owu Kingdom in Abeokuta, share a remarkable bond characterised by mutual respect, trust, and cordiality. Their relationship is a shining example of the power of unity and cooperation among traditional leaders in the Egbaland.
Oba Gbadebo has publicly expressed his deep appreciation for Oba Matemilola’s efforts in injecting love and harmony among traditional rulers in Egbaland and beyond. This gesture speaks volumes about the strong bond between the two monarchs and their commitment to promoting peace and stability in their kingdoms.
Their collaboration extends beyond mere protocol, as they have worked together on various occasions to address pressing issues affecting their communities. One notable example is their joint effort to resolve inter-clan disputes between Egba and Ota indigenes. In a remarkable display of leadership and diplomacy, Oba Matemilola, along with another respected traditional ruler, initiated interlocutory mediation to bring an end to the disputes between the two groups.
This exemplary display of collaboration and unity underscores the strong relationship between Oba Gbadebo and Oba Matemilola. By working together, they demonstrate their commitment to maintaining peace and stability in their kingdom, and their efforts serve as a model for other traditional leaders to follow.
Through their joint initiatives and unwavering support for one another, Oba Gbadebo and Oba Matemilola have fostered a sense of unity and cooperation that transcends traditional boundaries. Their partnership is a testament to the enduring power of traditional leadership and the important role that monarchs play in promoting peace, stability, and development in their communities.
As respected leaders, Oba Gbadebo and Oba Matemilola continue to inspire their subjects and promote a culture of peace, love, and understanding. Their legacy serves as a reminder of the importance of unity, cooperation, and strong leadership in building a prosperous and harmonious society.
The photo represents their cordiality at the Abeokuta Polo Club festival in December 2025

title.rendered: Oba Oyebade Lipede: The Ninth Alake of Egbaland and Architect of Modern Egba Unity

content.rendered:
Oba Oyebade Lipede was the ninth Alake of Egbaland, one of the most influential Yoruba traditional stools in southwestern Nigeria. His reign, which lasted from August 1972 until his death in February 2005, remains one of the longest and most consequential in Egba history. Beyond kingship, Lipede was a seasoned civil servant whose administrative experience significantly shaped his leadership style as monarch.
A rare photograph taken in 1941, when he was just 26 years old, captures him as a young officer in the Nigerian Customs Department, years before destiny placed him on the throne of Egbaland.
Birth, Family Background, and Education.
Oba Oyebade Lipede was born on January 26, 1915, in Abeokuta, the heartland of Egbaland in present-day Ogun State. He was born into a royal lineage eligible for the Alake stool, although, like many Egba princes of his era, he pursued a professional career before ascending the throne.
His early education reflected the elite missionary schooling of the period. He attended:
St. Peter’s School, Abeokuta, Abeokuta Grammar School and CMS Grammar School, Lagos.
These institutions were among the most prestigious educational centres in colonial Nigeria and produced many future national leaders.
Civil Service Career Before Kingship
Lipede began his career in 1937, joining the Nigerian Customs Department, where he served diligently for several years. By 1941, the year of the widely circulated photograph, he was already an established customs officer.
He later worked with the Nigerian Produce Marketing Company, gaining further experience in administration, trade regulation, and public service. His years in government service gave him a deep understanding of bureaucracy, negotiation, and governance—skills that would later define his reign as Alake.
Ascension to the Throne
Following the death of his predecessor, Oba Oyebade Lipede was installed as the Alake of Egbaland on August 5, 1972. His coronation marked a new era for Egba traditional leadership at a time when Nigeria was navigating military rule, state creation, and rapid social change.
He reigned for 33 years, making him one of the longest-serving Alakes in history.
Reign and Political Influence
Oba Lipede’s reign coincided with one of the most transformative periods in Nigerian history. One of his most notable achievements was his active lobbying for the creation of Ogun State in 1976.
He played a decisive role in:
Advocating for Abeokuta as the capital of Ogun State
Representing Egba interests during negotiations with the federal military government
Acting as a unifying figure among the Ake, Owu, Gbagura, and Oke-Ona Egba groups
Known for his centrist, diplomatic leadership style, Lipede avoided extreme political alignments and instead focused on consensus-building, cultural preservation, and peaceful coexistence.
Personality and Leadership Style
Oba Oyebade Lipede was widely regarded as:
Calm and methodical
Deeply traditional yet politically pragmatic
A bridge-builder among rival factions within Egbaland
His civil service background strongly influenced his approach to kingship, emphasizing order, consultation, and institutional continuity.
Death and Age
Oba Oyebade Lipede passed away in February 2005 at the age of 90, bringing to an end a reign that had spanned over three decades. His death marked the close of a significant chapter in Egba traditional history.
Legacy
Today, Oba Oyebade Lipede is remembered as:
A stabilising monarch during decades of national uncertainty
A key traditional figure in the creation and consolidation of Ogun State
One of the longest-reigning Alakes of Egbaland
A ruler who successfully blended modern governance experience with ancient Yoruba kingship
His legacy continues to influence traditional leadership and political identity in Egbaland.

title.rendered: Embracing self-pride and self-worth is empowering -tssi

content.rendered:
In the profound words of Chief Dr. Abiodun Lasile, “SixthSense SmartWords” echo with timeless wisdom, illuminating the path to self-discovery and empowerment. To truly embrace one’s inner strength, it is essential to recognise and celebrate personal achievements, not for the validation of others, but as a testament to one’s own worth. This profound self-awareness is the cornerstone of confidence, allowing individuals to stand tall, unshaken by the whims of external opinions.
For those who dare to be different, who refuse to be swayed by the doubters and naysayers, Chief Dr. Lasile offers a powerful mantra: set boundaries, assert your self-respect, and own your narrative. By doing so, you cultivate a mindset that is both empowered and empowering, one that fosters growth, learning, and self-expression.
The beauty of autonomy lies in its ability to allow individuals to make choices that align with their values and goals, to chart their own course, and to navigate the complexities of life with purpose and direction. And yet, this autonomy is not about isolation; rather, it is about being open to advice, to guidance, and to the wisdom of others.
As Chief Dr. Lasile so eloquently puts it, embracing autonomy and remaining open to advice is a powerful mindset that enables individuals to maintain their personal agency while continuing to learn and grow. It is a delicate balance, one that requires self-awareness, confidence, and a deep understanding of one’s own worth.
To those who have chosen to walk this path, Chief Dr. Lasile offers a simple yet profound message: keep shining. Your light is a beacon of hope and inspiration to others, a reminder that self-pride and self-worth are the greatest assets we can possess. May we all continue to shine brightly, illuminating the world around us with our unique talents, our passion, and our unwavering commitment to our values and goals.
-The SixthSense Initiative outreach
