title.rendered: Tribal Marks

content.rendered:
Let’s embark on a journey to explore the rich and complex world of tribal marks, a realm where art, identity, and culture converge. Tribal marks have been an integral part of human expression for centuries, serving as a visual representation of one’s heritage, status, and spiritual affiliation. As we delve deeper into the world of tribal marks, we discover that these markings are not just aesthetically pleasing but also carry significant cultural and spiritual meaning.
There are various types of tribal marks, each with its unique characteristics and significance. One type of tribal mark that stands out is the keloid tribal mark. These are raised scars that are created by cutting or burning the skin, and they are often considered a sign of beauty and strength in some African cultures. The keloid mark is a testament to the individual’s endurance and resilience, and it is often worn with pride.
Another type of tribal mark is the scarification mark. These scars are created by cutting or scratching the skin, and they can be used to signify status, identity, or spiritual affiliation. title.rendered: Luxury of quality, and the timeless sophistication that I hold dear

content.rendered:
As I navigate the complexities of life, I find solace in the embodiment of understated elegance. Guided by a discerning eye for quality that transcends the superficial, I approach life with a quiet confidence that is both captivating and unassuming. This confidence is not born out of loud declarations or ostentatious displays, but rather from a deep-seated understanding of what truly matters.

For me, life is about appreciating the finer things, not just in material possessions, but in the beauty of human connections, the richness of experiences, and the depth of knowledge. I am committed to timeless sophistication, a quality that is not bound by the whims of fleeting trends or the dictates of external validation. Instead, it is rooted in a profound sense of self-awareness, a clear understanding of my values, and a commitment to living a life that reflects those values.

In a world that often prioritises spectacle over substance, I choose to take a different path. I prioritise the essence of life, the things that bring true fulfillment and joy. My refined sensibilities are reflected in the choices I make, from the clothes I wear to the company I keep. I surround myself with people who share my values, who appreciate the beauty of simplicity, and who understand the luxury of quality.

With a keen sense of discernment, I curate my life with intention. I am deliberate about how I spend my time, the opportunities I pursue, and the relationships I nurture. I believe that life is a masterpiece in the making, and I strive to create a work of art that is authentic, meaningful, and beautiful.

As I move through the world, I am reminded of the power of understated elegance. It is not about seeking to impress others or to draw attention to oneself. Rather, it is about living a life that is true to oneself, a life that is marked by quiet confidence, deep appreciation, and a commitment to timeless sophistication.

In the end, it is not the loud or the flashy that leaves a lasting impression, but the quiet, confident, and elegant individuals who move through the world with purpose and intention. I am humbled to be counted among their number, and I look forward to continuing to live a life that reflects the beauty of simplicity, the luxury of quality, and the timeless sophistication that I hold dear.

-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta 
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative and Sixth Sense Series Publications 
Chairman, Association of Nigerian Authors (Ogun Chapter)

title.rendered: The Power of Keeping Promises

content.rendered:
As we step into the new year, adopting the habit of keeping promises can be a transformative resolution. According to the dictionary, a promise is “a declaration or assurance that one will do something or that a particular thing will happen.” In Yoruba, it’s known as “ílẹ̀rí” or “adehun.”
Keeping promises is simple: show up on time for appointments, follow through on commitments, and honour your word. By doing so, you build trust, credibility, and strengthen your relationships with others. When you make a promise to yourself, it’s a commitment to personal growth and self-improvement. Fulfilling your promises to yourself builds self-discipline and trust.
When you make a promise to someone else, it’s even more critical to keep it. Your reputation and relationships are at stake. Failing to fulfill a promise can damage your credibility and erode trust. Prioritise keeping your promises, and communicate openly and honestly if exceptional circumstances arise.
By keeping your promises, you demonstrate reliability, responsibility, and commitment to your word. This builds trust, credibility, and respect from others. Strive to be a person of your word, and may we all build strong relationships and credibility through our actions and commitments.
Some key takeaways:

– Be reliable: Show up on time and follow through on commitments.

– Communicate openly: If you can’t keep a promise, communicate honestly with the affected parties.
– Prioritise promises: Make keeping promises a habit, and exceptions should be rare.
By incorporating these habits into your daily life, you can build stronger relationships and a reputation for being trustworthy and reliable.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom 
Chairman, Association of Nigerian Authors (Ogun Chapter)

title.rendered: The Enduring Legacy of Tradition: Navigating the Tides of Modernisation -Orunto Owu Kingdom

content.rendered:
As the tides of modernisation ebb and flow, traditional institutions stand as sentinels, guarding the sacred trust of their heritage and values. Like ancient trees weathering the storms, they must flex and adapt, yet remain rooted in the rich soil of their history, preserving the essence of their identity and the integrity of their time-honored traditions.
The challenge lies not in resisting change, but in discerning which aspects of modernity can be embraced without sacrificing the core tenets that define their existence. This delicate balance requires wisdom, resilience, and a deep understanding of the past, present, and future. It demands a nuanced approach, one that honors the legacy of the ancestors while embracing the opportunities and challenges of the modern world.
As Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR, Orunto Baalufe of the Owu Kingdom in Abeokuta, I am acutely aware of the importance of preserving our cultural heritage. For generations, our people have thrived in the face of adversity, drawing strength from their traditions and values. As we navigate the complexities of modernisation, we must remain vigilant, ensuring that our institutions continue to reflect the wisdom and knowledge of our ancestors.
The tides of modernisation can be unforgiving, threatening to erode the very foundations of our traditional institutions. Yet, it is in these moments of uncertainty that we discover our greatest opportunities for growth, innovation, and renewal. By embracing the best of modernity while remaining true to our heritage, we can create a brighter future for ourselves and for generations to come.
As we move forward, we must do so with a sense of purpose, pride, and responsibility. We must honor the legacy of our ancestors, while also embracing the possibilities of the future. We must be mindful of the delicate balance between tradition and modernity, ensuring that our institutions remain relevant, effective, and true to their core values.
In the Owu Kingdom, we are committed to preserving our cultural heritage, while also embracing the opportunities and challenges of the modern world. We believe that our traditional institutions have a vital role to play in shaping the future of our community, and we are dedicated to ensuring that they continue to thrive and flourish.
As I reflect on the importance of tradition in our rapidly changing world, I am reminded of the wisdom of our ancestors. They knew that the strength of a people lies not in their ability to resist change, but in their capacity to adapt, innovate, and thrive. May we draw inspiration from their example, as we navigate the complexities of modernization and work towards a brighter future for all.
The Power of Tradition
In the end, it is not the institutions that are fragile, but our understanding of them. We must approach our traditions with humility, recognising that they are not static, but dynamic and evolving. By embracing this perspective, we can unlock the true power of tradition, harnessing its potential to inspire, motivate, and guide us as we navigate the challenges of the modern world.
As we look to the future, let us do so with hope, confidence, and a deep commitment to our heritage. Let us honor the legacy of our ancestors, while also embracing the possibilities of the future. Together, we can create a brighter tomorrow, one that is rooted in the wisdom of the past, yet open to the opportunities of the future.
-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom

title.rendered: Bullies Are Only Tough When They Are Winning   -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
Bullying often involves an imbalance of power, where the bully seeks to assert dominance over others. When bullies are challenged or faced with opposition, they may back down or become less aggressive. This quote highlights the importance of standing up against bullying behaviour and not giving in to their tactics.
Let’s dive into some strategies for handling bullying or supporting those who are being bullied. Here are some potential approaches:

-Stay calm and assertive: When dealing with a bully, try to remain calm and composed. Speak up for yourself or others in a clear and firm tone, without escalating the situation.

-Seek help and support*: Don’t hesitate to reach out to trusted friends, family members, or authority figures for support and guidance. Talking to someone can help you feel less isolated and more empowered.
-Document incidents*: Keep a record of any bullying incidents, including dates, times, locations, and the specific behaviors or actions involved. This can be helpful in case you need to report the bullying.
-Practice self-care: Take care of yourself physically, emotionally, and mentally. Engage in activities that bring you joy and help you relax, such as exercise, hobbies, or spending time with loved ones.
-Foster empathy and kindness: Encourage a culture of kindness and empathy in your community or school. Promote positive relationships and inclusivity, and stand up for those who are being bullied.

–The SixthSense Initiative outreach

title.rendered: Don’t Write People’s History in Absentia -Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
The notion that People’s history isn’t written in absentia; if attempted, it won’t stand the  test  of    time underscores the importance of authentic representation and agency in shaping one’s own narrative. History, as we know it, is often recorded and interpreted by those in positions of power, which can lead to skewed perspectives and the marginalisation of certain groups. However, when people are given the opportunity to tell their own stories, their histories gain authenticity, depth, and resilience.
Writing history in absentia—without the direct involvement of the people it concerns—risks reducing complex realities to oversimplified narratives. These narratives might serve the interests of those in power or usurpers but fail to capture the true essence of the lived experiences they purport to represent. Such histories are often susceptible to biases, misconceptions, intentional destruction, and omissions, which can distort the collective memory and identity of a people.
On the other hand, when people take control of their own historical narrative, they bring forth a richness and accuracy that might otherwise be unattainable. Their stories, struggles, and triumphs are conveyed in their own words, with their own emphasis, and from their own perspectives. This not only ensures a more accurate representation but also empowers communities to preserve their heritage and pass it on to future generations.
Moreover, history written by the people themselves is more likely to stand the test of time. It isn’t merely a reflection of a particular moment or ideology but a living testament to the resilience, creativity, and strength of a people. Such histories are not easily erased or altered; they are embedded in the collective memory and consciousness of the community.
In conclusion, the importance of people writing their own history cannot be overstated. It is a matter of authenticity, empowerment, and the preservation of cultural heritage. When people are given the opportunity to tell their own stories, they create a legacy that is true to their experiences and capable of enduring through generations.

title.rendered: Polo Players Renew Commitment to Strengthening Game at Maiden Festival

content.rendered:
Polo players and enthusiasts in Ogun State have renewed commitment to strengthening the game as stakeholders stage the maiden polo festival in Abeokuta the state capital.
A massive turnout greeted the berth of the sport popularly called the “game of kings” in Abeokuta, as affirmed by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo who encouraged people of the state to embrace Polo game.
Oba Gbadebo described Polo as a game of skills, passion and love for the benefit of all age groups, urging the host communities to support the stakeholders in the interest of social development and economic growth.
Also, the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta, Professor Saka Matemilola, said the polo festival was not only about sports expansion but also serving as a platform to promote culture, preserve tradition and foster unity among communities.
In a remark, Former Governor of Ogun state, Senator Ibikunle Amosun expressed the conviction that Abeokuta Polo Club was a catalyst for development across the state and  pledged his commitment to assisting the club in every way
necessary.
Earlier, the President of the Abeokuta Polo Club, Dr. Sheriff Abdulrahman, had explained that the maiden festival, tagged “The Bold Step,” was the beginning of a new dawn for polo in Abeokuta, promising that the initiative would be sustained and enhanced to further stimulate economic activities in the area.
Dr. Abdul Rahman gave the assurance that the apart from sports, the initiative would equally enhance tourism, infrastructure, youth programmes, cultural showcase and real estate, with a view to positioning Abeokuta as a leading hub for polo and equestrian sports in Nigeria and West Africa.
Dignitaries at the festival included the Commissioner for Sports, Mr Wasiu Isiaka that of Culture and Tourism, Mr Sesan Fagbayi, Mrs Bola Obasanjo and Mrs Olufunso Amosun while the ceremony featured the display of horse riding, musical performances, bonfire and lots of entertainments.

title.rendered: Prayers are the Tonic that Energise the king on the Stool

content.rendered:
This sounds like describing a cultural or traditional practice of showing respect and support for a monarch. As kingmakers, we play a significant role in upholding the dignity and authority of the royal stool. Our role is not only to advise and counsel the king but also to protect and preserve the traditions and heritage of the kingdom.
We offer prayers, eulogies, and reverence to the king, not in worship, but to uplift his spirit and fortify the energies that surround him, that he may reign with wisdom, strength, and justice.
Long may the king reign.
Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Greed and selfishness don’t help intelligence.

content.rendered:
In the grand tapestry of human endeavour, the twin specters of greed and selfishness loom large, threatening to ensnare the unwary and stifle the very engines of progress. These pernicious forces, born of a myopic focus on personal gain, serve to constrict the vistas of the mind, shutting out the illuminating light of diverse perspectives and novel ideas. As the aperture of our vision narrows, our capacity for genuine intellectual growth and advancement becomes correspondingly diminished, trapped as we are in the sterile echo chamber of our own self-interest.

And yet, true intelligence – that most mercurial and multifaceted of qualities – is often found in the fertile crescent of curiosity, empathy, and a willingness to learn. It is in embracing the humility that comes from acknowledging the vast expanse of our collective ignorance, and in opening ourselves to the rich tapestry of human experience, that we create an environment conducive to the cross-pollination of ideas and the collaborative pursuit of solutions to the complex problems that beset us.

The notion that true intelligence is not about personal aggrandisement or the fleeting plaudits of others, but rather about contributing to the greater good and advancing the sum of human knowledge, is a profound one. It speaks to the very heart of what it means to be human, and to the transformative power of generosity, cooperation, and mutual support in the pursuit of a shared vision of the possible.

In this light, the cultivation of a culture of openness, empathy, and cooperation becomes not merely a desideratum, but a categorical imperative – one that holds the promise of unlocking the full potential of human intelligence, and of propelling us towards a brighter, more enlightened future, where the boundaries of what is possible are expanded, and the collective wisdom of humanity is allowed to flourish.

-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

title.rendered: ANTI-CORRUPTION COALITION INDUCTS OGUN YOUTH CHAIRMAN AS AMBASSADOR, PRESENTS AWARD FOR EXEMPLARY LEADERSHIP AND ANTI-CORRUPTION DRIVE.

content.rendered:
The State Chairman of the National Youth Council of Nigeria, Olóyè Akolawole Shoremi, has been conferred with two prestigious awards in recognition of his unwavering commitment to good governance, anti-corruption advocacy, and youth development in Ogun State.

The dual recognition of excellence and induction as an Anti-Corruption Ambassador of Nigeria was an initiative of the Organization of People’s Voice — a member of the ICPC-National Anti-Corruption Coalition (ICPC-NACC).

Presenting the awards on Monday, December 15, 2025, at Oke-Ilewo, Abeokuta, the State Programmes Coordinator of the ICPC-NACC, Mr. Idris Abu, eulogized the youth Chairman as a public servant with astute leadership qualities and remarkable commitment to youth development in Ogun State and Nigeria. “Today, we reflect on your remarkable contributions to the fight against corruption across our tertiary institutions in Ogun State over a decade ago,” he recalled.

“The coalition is pleased to see you sustain a lifestyle of transparency, decency, and honesty. These awards serve as a testament to your tireless service and enviable commitment to a fair and progressive society.

“I urge all members of the youth constituency to continue emulating your principles of integrity. We are proud to identify with you,” Abu concluded.

In his acceptance speech, the youth Chairman extended his heartfelt appreciation to the Organizers for the kind reflection and acknowledgement of his past and present endeavors. He reiterated his commitment to a just society being edged on a relentless drive for humanity.

The award was originally scheduled for presentation at the three-day Anti-Corruption programme organized by the Coalition, tagged “Your Right, Your Roles,” and held at the NUJ Hall, Oke-Ilewo, Abeokuta on Friday, November 14, 2025. The youth Chairman’s entourage included the State Deputy Secretary of the Youth Council, Com. Kehinde Ademuyiwa; and his Chief Protocol Officer, Com. Samsideen Bakare.

title.rendered: ROYAL BLESSING TO ORUNTO.

content.rendered:
Congratulations on your new position as Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Authors (Ogun Chapter)!

That’s exciting news! I’m sure your leadership will help promote and celebrate Nigerian literature, supporting authors and fostering a vibrant literary community.”

-HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE Otileta Vll Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: The Extraordinary Gift of Authors.

content.rendered:
Authors are the masterful weavers of the written word, possessing a unique perspective, creativity, and skill that sets them apart. With their pens or keyboards, they craft worlds, characters, and ideas that transport us to new dimensions, challenge our assumptions, and inspire us to see the world in new and exciting ways.

The Art of Storytelling

Authors have the remarkable ability to weave words into powerful stories that captivate and inspire. They share their insights and experiences, offering new perspectives that broaden our understanding of the world and ourselves. Through their writing, they distill complex ideas into accessible and engaging language, making the intricate seem simple and the obscure seem clear.

A Special Gift

Authors possess a special gift for communicating their thoughts, emotions, and ideas in a way that resonates with others. Their work can educate and enlighten, entertaining and inspiring us in the process. They challenge societal norms and spark meaningful conversations, leaving a lasting impact on readers and the world.

The Impact of Authors

The work of authors can have a profound impact on our lives. It can:
-Transport us to new worlds*, expanding our horizons and broadening our perspectives
-Inspire us to action*, motivating us to make a difference in the world
-Challenge our assumptions*, forcing us to think critically and question our beliefs
-Comfort and console us*, providing solace and support in times of need

As we celebrate the authors who enrich our lives with their words, let us acknowledge the immense talent, dedication, and passion that goes into crafting a work of literature. Let us recognize the power of their stories to shape our understanding of the world and ourselves.

In the words of authors past and present, we find reflections of ourselves, our hopes, and our fears. Their stories have the power to transform us, to make us see the world in a new light, and to inspire us to be better versions of ourselves.

So let us cherish the authors who weave their magic with words, and let us continue to be inspired by the extraordinary gift of their writing.

-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

title.rendered: NEW OGUN ANA EXCO TAKES OVER ON SATURDAY

content.rendered:
The Handover and swearing ceremony for a new set of Executives of the Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) in Ogun State held on Saturday at the Palace of Olowu of Owu on Oke Ago Owu in Abeokuta.
The three-in-one ceremony was attended by eminent authors and leaders including the Olowu of Owu, Oba (Professor) Saka Matemilola who served as the Chairman of the inauguration ceremony.
The new officers, elected at the Association’s monthly meeting in November,  formally took-over at the ceremony, which commenced  promptly at noon.
The officers included Orunto of Owu Kingdom, Chief Abiodun Lasile, Who was elected  Chairman,
Pastor Dare Folarin as Vice Chairman; and Mr. Matthew Simpa as General Secretary.
Others were Mr. Gbenga Ogunsola as Treasurer, Mr. Akinyemi Makinde as Assistant Secretary and Mr.Samuel Ogunyinka as Public Relations Officer.
Members of the Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) and the  South West Authors Forum (SWAF) were Present at the event.

title.rendered: Perspective on Traditional sacrifices and appeasement -Orunto Owu

content.rendered:
For centuries, the rituals of traditional sacrifices and appeasement have been woven into the fabric of human culture, rooted in the deepest wellsprings of spiritual belief and ancestral heritage. These ancient practices have served as a bridge between the mortal realm and the divine, offering solace in times of turmoil and uncertainty.

On one hand, these rituals can be a powerful means of connecting with the past, honouring the traditions that have shaped our identities and communities. They can provide a sense of belonging and continuity, a reassuring rhythm that echoes through the ages. In times of crisis or doubt, the familiar cadence of ritual and sacrifice can offer comfort, a sense of security that comes from knowing that our ancestors have walked this path before us.

Moreover, these practices can serve as a means of expressing gratitude, of acknowledging the mysteries that lie beyond our mortal comprehension. They can be a gesture of humility, a recognition of the limits of our knowledge and power. In the stillness of ritual, we may find guidance, a whispered wisdom that speaks to the deepest longings of our hearts.

Yet, there is also a shadow side to these practices. When ritual becomes rote, and sacrifice becomes a mere spectacle, we risk losing sight of the deeper truths that lie beneath. We may find ourselves trapped in a cycle of superstition and fear, bound by the chains of dogma and tradition. We may divert our attention from the tangible, practical solutions that lie within our grasp, instead pinning our hopes on divine intervention or magical thinking.

Furthermore, these practices can be exploited by those who would seek to wield power over others. They can be used to manipulate and control, to reinforce systems of oppression and injustice. When we prioritise the rituals of sacrifice and appeasement over the needs and dignity of human beings, we risk losing our way, forgetting the fundamental principles of compassion, empathy, and justice.

title.rendered: Ooni installs First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu as Yeye Asiwaju of Ile-Oodua

content.rendered:
We are delighted to join the entire Yoruba nation in celebrating Her Excellency, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, OON, CON, on her installation today as Yeye Asiwaju Gbogbo Ile Oodua by His Royal Majesty, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, Ojaja II, the Ooni of Ife.
The installation ceremony, held at Afewonro Park in Enuwa Square within the Ooni’s Palace, marked the grand finale of events commemorating the monarch’s 10th coronation anniversary.
Traditional rites were performed by palace chiefs in line with established Yoruba customs.
You have stood as a steadfast pillar beside our leader and President, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, offering strength, wisdom and support in ways that have shaped both his journey and the destiny of our country.
Congratulations.

title.rendered: Owu National Convention at Owu Gbawojo.

content.rendered:
Date: 5th Friday, 2025
A beautiful moment of heritage, unity, and tradition as Oba Marufdeen Adelani Adegbajo, the Adegbaajo of Owu Kingdom, warmly welcomed Alayeluwa Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola, Oluyalo Otileta VII, the Olowu of Owu, Abeokuta to this year’s Owu National Convention.

 

As part of the symbolic opening, Kabiyesi Oba Marufdeen Adelani Adegbajo led Alayeluwa Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola to the historic Abaa Tree a sacred symbol of peace, unity, and continuity for the Owu people. Standing beneath the Abaa signifies togetherness and the enduring bond that holds the kingdom strong.

Stay tuned for highlights from this year’s memorable gathering of the Owu kingdom…

title.rendered: Every Contribution Matters in Volunteerism…

content.rendered:
The 2025 World Volunteer Day theme, “Every Contribution Matters”, shines bright, reminding us that every act, no matter how small, counts. Collective efforts transform individual actions into powerful forces for change. This theme inspires inclusivity, encourages active participation, and celebrates the transformative impact of volunteering in shaping vibrant communities.

We urge a national outlook that positions volunteering as a cornerstone of development, service to humanity, and opportunity for growth.

Let’s harness the spirit of selfless service, recognising that personal contributions are investments in our nation’s growth and individual development. By inculcating volunteerism, we can shape responsible leaders and foster a culture of service.

Let’s inspire others to lend their time and talents to support those around them. Your dedication, solidarity, and compassion are crafting a better world. As Secretary-General António Guterres aptly puts it, “Together, we can grow a global movement of volunteers, and build a brighter, more caring future for all.”

Today, December 5, we commemorate the power of selfless service and celebrate the volunteers who make a difference. We celebrate doing something for nothing to humanity!

Press Release Signed by.
Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative

title.rendered: The Paradox of Selfless Giving.

content.rendered:
“Volunteering means giving without expecting anything in return”, yet it’s in this act of selflessness that we often discover our greatest rewards. For Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR, humanitarian efforts aren’t just about giving; they’re about finding purpose and fulfillment.

This paradox lies at the heart of true altruism. While others may see it as merely giving, those who volunteer know that it’s a transformative act that changes both the giver and the receiver. The act of giving without expectation awakens a sense of connection and community, reminding us that our actions have the power to impact lives.

Abiodun’s words resonate deeply: “My humanitarian efforts may seem selfless to some, but they bring me fulfillment”. This fulfillment isn’t just a byproduct; it’s a driving force. It fuels passion, ignites compassion, and inspires others to follow suit.

In a world where transactions often come with strings attached, volunteering stands out as a beacon of hope. It shows us that some things in life are priceless, that some actions are worth more than any reward.

As Abiodun so eloquently puts it, “even if others find it hard to understand”. True giving doesn’t seek validation; it stems from a place of empathy, kindness, and love. It’s a reminder that the value of our actions isn’t measured by external recognition but by the positive impact we create.

In the end, volunteering isn’t just about giving; it’s about living a life that matters. It’s about leaving a mark that says, “I was here, and I made a difference”. For Abiodun and countless others, this is the greatest reward of all.

“Volunteering means giving without expecting anything in return. While my humanitarian efforts may seem selfless to some, they bring me fulfillment, even if others find it hard to understand”. –Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

-SixthSense Outreach

title.rendered: Culture and Community in a child.

content.rendered:
The fabric of a child’s upbringing is intricately woven from the threads of culture and community. These twin pillars shape the contours of their growth, influencing every aspect of their development.

Cultural values impart a sense of identity, guiding parents in their approach to discipline, expectations, and nurturing. Whether it’s the emphasis on respect for elders or the encouragement of independence, these values form the bedrock of a child’s worldview.

A strong community envelops the child in a network of support, providing emotional solace, practical assistance, and positive role models. Extended family, neighbours, and community organisations all play a vital role in fostering a sense of belonging.

Through socialisation, children learn the nuances of human interaction, absorbing the norms, behaviours, and customs that define their community. This process molds their identity, helping them navigate the complexities of relationships and societal expectations.

Cultural traditions and practices breathe life into a child’s experiences, connecting them to their heritage and instilling a deep sense of roots. As they participate in rituals, celebrations, and daily practices, they develop a profound appreciation for the richness of their cultural legacy.

In this way, culture and community converge to shape the trajectory of a child’s life, influencing their growth, identity, and place in the world. It is encouraging to make people of the world to preserve cultures in their communities as they grow their new lives and values.

The SixthSense Initiative invites global communities to preserve their cultural heritage, fostering growth, values, and community enrichment.

-Chief Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: WACSW 2025: OGUN YOUTH CHAIRMAN LOBBIES AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK, SECURES STRATEGIC PATHWAYS FOR YOUTH EMPOWERMENT FUNDING.

content.rendered:
The State Chairman of the National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), Olóyè Akolawole Shoremi, was an invited Guest at the highly strategic 2025 West Africa Civil Society Week (WACSW 2025) recently held in Accra, Ghana, between November 18-22, 2025.
The event themed “Redefining Civil Society and the Future of Democratic Resilience in West Africa” had as its participants civil society actors, including activists, policy experts, youth leaders, media, civic-tech actors, and development partners from more than 10 West African countries.
The week-long event offered a critical platform for strategic reflection, peer-learning, and co-creating solutions to the challenges facing democratic governance and civic space in the sub-region.
During the week, the Chairman engaged with young leaders from across the West African sub-region, exchanging developmental ideas on youth engagement and entrepreneurship. The key highlight was a significant meeting with Mr. Emile Bela, the Programs Officer of the African Development Bank (AfDB). Discussions focused intently on leveraging existing AfDB financial mechanisms to open pathways for funding opportunities for young people in Ogun State and Nigeria.
In acknowledgement of Shoremi’s advocacy efforts, Mr. Bela developed a clear, five-point strategic roadmap for action detailing how the youth constituency of Nigeria can proactively submit winning proposals and gain access to AfDB funding and technical support under the Jobs for Youth in Africa (JfYA) Strategy.

The AfDB official further encouraged the Youth Council to focus on submitting targeted innovation proposals, advocate for ENABLE Youth Expansion and Co-Management, Negotiate a Youth Employment Compact to guarantee accelerated youth employment interventions through the AfDB, and convene a Youth Employment Coalition, among others.
According to the West African Civil Society Institute, the overarching goal of the WACSW 2025 is to provide a safe and broad based platform to assess the state of civil society in West Africa and redefine its purpose — conceptually and operationally, with specific objectives including the mapping of the ecosystem for new actors on youth and social movements, informal networks, cultural collectives among others.

-OGUN YOUTH HOUSE MEDIA TEAM

title.rendered: Self Pride is self worth. -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR

content.rendered:
Self-pride is the melody that resonates deep within our souls, a symphony of self-love and acceptance.

It is the gentle breeze that nourishes our spirit, the warm sunlight that illuminates our path, and the safe haven where we can be ourselves, without apology or pretension.

When we pride ourselves, we become the architects of our destiny, crafting a life that reflects our values, our passions, and our highest potential.

We rise above the whispers of doubt, the shadows of fear, and the limitations of others, and we emerge as the radiant, resilient, and triumphant beings we were meant to be.

title.rendered: Oba Alake’s 20th Anniversary

content.rendered:
The Alake of Egbaland, HRM Oba Dr. Michael Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo CFR Okukenu IV, marked his 20th anniversary on the throne of his forefathers on November 19, 2025. The week-long celebrations drew distinguished guests, including Egba Obas, titled chiefs, government officials, politicians, and business leaders.

 

The Orunto Owu, Chief Dr. Abiodun Lasile, was among the dignitaries who joined in the festivities, extending warm felicitations to the paramount ruler. On behalf of his family and kingdom, he prayerfully wished the monarch a long and healthy reign.

title.rendered: FACES AT 2025 ODUN OMO OLOWU

content.rendered:
Traditions, customs, and cultures are indeed valuable aspects of human identity, carrying significant historical, social, and emotional importance.

Preserving these aspects is crucial for Owu Kingdom Abeokuta:

– Maintaining cultural diversity and heritage
– Understanding historical context and evolution
– Fostering community cohesion and identity
– Promoting cross-cultural understanding and appreciation

By embracing and respecting diverse traditions, customs, and cultures, we can celebrate festivals:

– Learn from one another’s experiences and perspectives
– Enrich our lives through cultural exchange and exploration
– Build bridges of understanding between communities
– Preserve the collective heritage of humanity

 

 
 
Here are faces at the 2025 Odun Omo
 Olowu festival

title.rendered: OLUBADAN TO PROMOTE SEVEN SENIOR CHIEFS

content.rendered:
Seven senior chiefs in Otun Olubadan line would benefit from the promotion exercise slated for this Friday.

   The promotion exercise to be presided over by the Olubadan of Ibadanland,       Oba Rashidi Ladoja will take place at the Olubadan Palace, Oke Aremo,               Ibadan.
   As Senior Chief Lekan Alabi would be promoted to Abese Olubadan from           Maye Olubadan, so also will Senior Chief Akin Fijabi become Maye                         Olubadan  from Ekefa Olubadan.
   Senior Chief Saka Fola Lapade would become the Ekefa Olubadan while             former Senate Leader, Senior Chief Teslim Folarin, now Aare Alaasa                     Olubadan would be promoted to Agbaakin Olubadan.
Senior Chief Muibi Adewuyi is expected to become Aare Alasa Olubadan from Ikolaba Olubadan while Chief Raufu Delesolu will become Ikolaba Olubadan. Chief Hammed Lanihun would become Asaju Olubadan from Ayingun Olubadan.

It will be recalled that a fortnight ago, the promotion exercise to fill the vacant title created by the emergence of Oba Rashidi Ladoja as the 44th Olubadan began with the promotion of five Olubadan-in-council members from Otun Olubadan down to Ekarun. Next fortnight will afford the remaining nine other chiefs the opportunity to participate from the gale of promotion exercise sweeping through the Otun Olubadan line. 
E-signed: 
Adeola Oloko,
Media Aide 
His Imperial Majesty, Olubadan of Ibadanland.

title.rendered: ANA Ogun Elects New Excos

content.rendered:
Orunto Abiodun Lasile bags Chairmanship, Dare Folarin emerges Vice Chairman
New set of Executive Members have been elected to steer the ship of Association of Nigerian Authors (ANA) in Ogun State for the next two years.
The Orunto of Owu Kingdom, Chief Abiodun Lasile was elected as the Chairman while Pastor Dare Folarin was elected Vice Chairman.
Others include Mr. Matthew Simpa who was elected as General Secretary at the November monthly meeting held at Simeon Adebo Library, Abeokuta.
Mr. Gbenga Ogunsola was elected Treasurer, Samuel Ogunyinka Public Relations Officer and Akinyemi Makinde as Assistant Secretary.
The newly elected members would be sworn-in during the December monthly meeting scheduled to hold at the Olowu Palace in Abeokuta.
-SixthSense Media Outreach

content.rendered:

Dedicated to serving humanity and contributing to the greater good.”
-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Odun Omo Olowu 2025: A Festival Beyond Music, Colour, and Tradition, A Call to Cultural Responsibility

content.rendered:
The grand finale of the Odun Omo Olowu 2025, held at Oba Odeleye Park, Sokori Ori-Omi, Abeokuta, was marked by cultural splendour, royal dignity, and a powerful message from His Excellency, Chief Olusegun Aremu Obasanjo, GCFR, the Balogun of Owu Kingdom and former President of Nigeria.
In his address during the celebration, Chief Obasanjo delivered a heartfelt charge to Nigerians living abroad, urging them to ensure that their children learn and uphold the Yoruba language, values, and traditions so they do not lose their identity in foreign lands. He emphasized that culture is not merely a symbol of heritage but the foundation of self-awareness and communal pride.
Chief Obasanjo illustrated his point with a story about a Yoruba family abroad whose children, though highly educated, could not communicate in their native language. He expressed concern that many parents in the diaspora prioritize foreign assimilation over cultural preservation, leading to a gradual erosion of indigenous identity.
His message resonated deeply with the theme of the 2025 Odun Omo Olowu Festival, “Awaken the Owu Spirit.” The festival, which brings together sons and daughters of Owu from across the world, is not only a celebration of heritage but also a reminder of the enduring values of unity, respect, and cultural pride that define the Owu people.
Chief Obasanjo’s remarks reflected the festival’s vision, to reconnect generations of Owu descendants, both at home and abroad, with their roots. By urging parents to consciously teach their children Yoruba culture and traditions, he aligned with the festival’s broader call to revive the Owu spirit and strengthen the cultural continuity that binds the community.
Chief Obasanjo’s timeless message remains clear: “Our culture is our identity; without it, we are lost among nations.”

title.rendered: Olowu of Owu Confers Chieftaincy Titles on Distinguished Sons and Daughters During Odun Omo Olowu 2025

content.rendered:
On Friday, October 24, 2025, at the Palace of Olowu of Owu Abeokuta, Alayeluwa Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola, Oluyalo Otileta VII, conferred chieftaincy titles on distinguished sons and daughters of Owu in recognition of their outstanding contributions to the growth and development of the community.
The colorful conferment ceremony took place during the Odun Omo Olowu 2025 Festival, a grand celebration of Owu heritage, unity, and excellence.

Among the newly installed chiefs were:
Princess Grace Oluwafunmilayo Jimoh as Erelu Oluyalo
Mr. Oluwatoyin Wasiu Jimoh as Aare Akinrogun
Chief Mrs. Remilekun Mulikat Opere as Sarumi Iyalode
Mr. Akingbade John Adewale as Akinlagun
Mrs. Akingbade Folashade Medenat as Yeye Akinlagun
Sir John Olufunsho Aiku as Omogbadewa
Lady Princess Matilda Olufemi Aiku as Erelu Omogbadewa
The atmosphere was filled with joy and pride as family members, friends, dignitaries, and well-wishers gathered to celebrate the new chiefs. The conferment ceremony was a testament to the Olowu’s continued commitment to recognizing excellence and service within the Owu community.
Olowu commended the new chiefs for their dedication and urged them to continue being exemplary ambassadors of Owu Kingdom in all their endeavors.

title.rendered: Royal Unity and Cultural Pride as Egba Obas Grace Odun Omo Olowu 2025 Grand Finale

content.rendered:
The Grand Finale of Odun Omo Olowu 2025 was a majestic convergence of royal fathers, dignitaries, and guests from across Egbaland and beyond. The festival, which celebrates the rich cultural heritage of the Owu Kingdom, once again showcased the unity, dignity, and shared history of the Egba people.
In his goodwill message, His Royal Majesty, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, CFR, Okukenu IV, the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, commended Alayeluwa, Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola, Oluyalo Otileta VII, the Olowu of Owu Abeokuta, for his visionary leadership and for hosting such a culturally vibrant and unifying festival.
Alake of Egbaland urged other monarchs and community leaders to emulate the Olowu’s commitment to cultural preservation, youth empowerment, and communal development.
“The Olowu has set an example for all traditional rulers by promoting unity, investing in the welfare of his people, and upholding our shared heritage with pride,” Oba Alake stated. “I encourage other royal fathers to take similar steps that bridge divides and strengthen our cultural bonds across Egbaland and Yorubaland.”
Oba Gbadebo further emphasized that Odun Omo Olowu should serve not only as an annual celebration but also as a platform for promoting education, development, and social harmony among the Egba people.
He called on the youth to uphold their culture with innovation and pride, while the elders continue to guide with wisdom and humility.
In attendance were His Royal Majesty, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, CFR, Okukenu IV, the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland; His Royal Majesty, Oba Dr. Adedapo Adewale Tejuoso, CON, Karunwi III, the Osile of Oke-Ona Egba; and High Chief Ayodele Koleade, the Balogun of Iddo Township, Gbagura, among other prominent Egba chiefs and traditional leaders.
The Odun Omo Olowu Festival continues to stand as a testament to the Owu Kingdom’s enduring legacy, a celebration where royalty, culture, and community converge to reaffirm the strength of identity and tradition.

title.rendered: 2025 National Youth Day Summit and Award Presentation in Ogun State

content.rendered:
Thursday, 30th October, 2025

At Abeokuta Club 2025 National Youth Day Summit and Award Presentation in Ogun State, held under the auspices of youths and stakeholders of Egbaland, comprising the six local government areas of the central district. 

I was honoured to serve as a keynote speaker at the event, alongside Chief Tunde Delu, Special Senior Assistant to the Governor, at Abeokuta Club.
I was also distinguished as an award winner of the “Custodian of Youth”

title.rendered: Omo Olowu Oduru, Ajifepesere

content.rendered: “We gather to celebrate our shared humanity, development, and the storied history of our great Owu heritage (people). As the foremost descendants of Oduduwa, the revered founder of the Yoruba nation, we honour our distinct culture and character. Our reputation for dependability and trustworthiness is well-deserved, and we are proud to uphold these values.”

title.rendered: Kingmakers….Perspective of Senior Chiefs

content.rendered:
Introduction:

In traditional Yoruba culture, kingmakers hold a revered position, selecting and crowning monarchs who embody wisdom, leadership, and community values. While royal lineage plays a role, kingmakers ensure the chosen candidate possesses the necessary qualities to lead effectively, balancing birthright with merit and community consensus. This ancient institution underscores the importance of collective involvement in leadership selection.
In the context of traditional Yoruba culture, the phrase “Kingmaker” refers to individuals or groups who play a significant role in selecting and crowning monarchs, such as Obas. The kingmakers often comprise influential chiefs, elders, or other high-ranking members of the community who possess the authority to nominate or install a new king.
It also depends on the declaration of one town to the other or customs of tribes and history.
The statement “Kingmaker makes Obas though they are born princely” highlights the complex interplay between birthright and selection in traditional Yoruba monarchies. While Obas are typically born into royal lineages and are considered princes by birth, their ascension to the throne often depends on the approval and selection by the kingmakers.
This dynamic reflects the balance between hereditary privilege and merit or suitability, where being born into a royal family is a necessary but not sufficient condition for becoming an Oba. The kingmakers’ role is crucial in ensuring that the selected candidate possesses the necessary qualities, wisdom, and support to lead the community effectively.
The kingmakers’ role serves as a check on royal power, ensuring that the selected candidate possesses the necessary qualities, wisdom, and support to lead the community effectively. This system underscores the importance of community involvement and consensus in the selection of leaders.
In essence, the kingmakers serve as a check on royal power, ensuring that the monarch is not solely determined by birthright but also by their ability to lead and serve the community. This system underscores the importance of community involvement and consensus in the selection of leaders in traditional Yoruba society.
The Yoruba traditional institution is a complex system with a rich history and culture. The role of kingmakers is crucial in selecting and crowning monarchs, ensuring that the chosen candidate has the necessary qualities and support to lead the community effectively.
Some key aspects of the Yoruba traditional institution include:
1. Hierarchical structure: The institution is organized in a hierarchical manner, with the Oba (king) at the apex.
2. Council of chiefs: Kingmakers and other chiefs advise the Oba and play important roles in decision-making.
3. Community involvement: The selection of leaders often involves community participation and consensus.
4. Cultural significance: The institution is deeply rooted in Yoruba culture and tradition.

The Yoruba traditional institution has played a significant role in maintaining social order, promoting cultural heritage, and providing spiritual guidance.
Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta.

title.rendered: Owu Intricate Leadership in Perspectives

content.rendered:
The Owu people and culture are indeed distinct, with a notable characteristic being their strong values and high standards. The saying ‘Owu is difficult to serve and to lead’ underscores this notion, suggesting that their commitment to their principles can make it challenging for others to work with or lead them.
This trait can be attributed to their desire for individuality and uniqueness. The fact that older generations have observed and acknowledged this aspect of Owu culture lends credibility to its significance. While this strong sense of independence can pose a challenge for leaders aiming to achieve specific objectives, it’s fascinating that transparency often prompts a reaction from a vocal minority, which can sometimes be a distraction.
On the other hand, the strategic inclusion of outliers to maintain balance and achieve collective goals speaks to the community’s ability to problem-solve and work together. Ultimately, the Owu people are known for being trustworthy and dependable, qualities that are essential for building strong relationships and fostering trust within a community.

title.rendered: African Followership Resilience and Helplessness

content.rendered:
The weight of our collective destiny rests on the shoulders of every individual who possesses the power to shape the future. Yet, a pervasive malaise seems to have taken hold, a phenomenon aptly described as the African followership syndrome of resilience and helplessness. This paradoxical blend of endurance and hopelessness has become a defining characteristic of our collective psyche, hindering our progress and stifling our potential.

As we navigate the complexities of our modern world, we find ourselves at a crossroads, where the path forward demands a renewed sense of purpose and agency. It’s time to confront the status quo and challenge the norms that have held us back for far too long. We must recognise that our liberation lies not in the hands of a select few, but in the collective actions of the many.
At the heart of this issue lies our electoral responsibilities – the fundamental right to choose our leaders, shape our policies, and determine the course of our nations. Yet, all too often, we approach this sacred duty with a sense of apathy, detachment, or even desperation. We need to awaken to the reality that our franchise is not a privilege, but a potent tool that can be leveraged to transform our societies.
To exercise our franchise effectively means to take ownership of our democratic processes, to engage in informed decision-making, and to hold our leaders accountable for their actions. It demands that we move beyond the comfort of mere spectatorship and assume the role of active participants, working tirelessly to build a future that reflects our collective aspirations.
This is a call to action, a clarion call to every individual to recognise the power that lies within them. We must shed the cloak of helplessness and don the mantle of responsible citizenship. By doing so, we can create a groundswell of change that will resonate across our continent, inspiring a new generation of leaders and citizens to rise up and shape their own destiny.
As Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR so eloquently puts it, “It’s about addressing the African followership syndrome of resilience and helplessness. We need to be more responsive to our electoral responsibilities and exercise our franchise effectively.” Let us heed this call to action, and together, let us forge a brighter future for ourselves, our communities, and our nations.
Together, we can lead ourselves.
-SixthSense Outreach

title.rendered: Opinion: The Aspect of Cultural Preservation and Heritage in Festival Celebration

content.rendered:
Festivals are vibrant tapestries woven from the threads of cultural heritage, preserving the essence of community traditions. They burst forth with the rhythmic beats of traditional music, the whirl of colorful dances, and the intricate patterns of art and crafts. These joyous celebrations safeguard historical customs and rituals, passing down the treasured stories and values to younger generations.
As communities come together, festivals become a platform for cultural exchange, fostering appreciation and understanding among diverse groups. Participants strengthen their sense of identity and belonging, while sharing their unique heritage with others. The experience is reciprocal, allowing individuals to learn from and admire the richness of other cultures.
Moreover, festivals breathe new life into traditional practices, supporting local artisans and cultural practitioners. They forge unbreakable bonds within the community, nurturing social cohesion and a sense of togetherness. In preserving cultural heritage, festivals ensure that the community’s history, customs, and values are safeguarded for generations to come.
The SixthSense Initiative is a registered nonprofit outfit hugely promoting children reading culture and human capacity.

title.rendered: Volunteering: An Act of Service to Humanity

content.rendered:
Volunteering is a transformative journey where selflessness converges with profound personal enrichment. As Abiodun Lasile aptly puts it, “Doing something for nothing with a lot of gain.” This beautiful perspective highlights the intrinsic rewards that emerge from dedicating time and effort without expectation of material reward.
The multifaceted benefits of volunteering include:

– Personal Growth and Development: Nurturing self-awareness, resilience and emotional intelligence.

– New Skills and Experiences: Acquiring diverse expertise, perspectives and insights.
– Networking Opportunities: Fostering meaningful connections, collaborations and community.
– Sense of Purpose and Fulfillment: Discovering significance, contribution and impact.
– Positive Impact on the Community: Creating lasting change, driving progress and uplifting lives.
By embracing volunteering, individuals can unlock a wealth of rewards that transcend tangible compensation, yielding a profound sense of fulfillment and purpose.
The SixthSense Initiative is a registered nonprofit outfit hugely promoting children reading culture and human capacity development.

title.rendered: Relating Custom to Tradition and Development

content.rendered:
In the intricate dance between tradition and progress, lies a profound relationship that shapes the destiny of societies. Customs and traditions form the bedrock of cultural identity, providing a sense of belonging and continuity that defines community values and practices. These time-honoured rituals and heritage sites are not mere relics of the past, but vibrant expressions of a community’s history, art, and philosophy.

As development accelerates, it can bring about changes in customs and traditions. However, this evolution doesn’t necessarily imply a complete abandonment of cultural heritage. Instead, communities can innovate and adapt their traditions to fit modern contexts, striking a delicate balance between preservation and progress. By integrating traditional knowledge and practices into development initiatives, we can foster sustainable outcomes that not only respect cultural diversity but also promote environmentally conscious practices.
The key to successful cultural preservation lies in respectful innovation, where development initiatives are designed in tandem with local customs and traditions. Community engagement is crucial in this process, ensuring that the voices of local communities are heard and their values are integrated into development planning. This collaborative approach allows for a dynamic cultural exchange, where communities can learn from each other, share ideas, and preserve their unique customs in the face of globalisation and technological advancements.
Ultimately, understanding the interplay between custom, tradition, and development is essential for promoting culturally sensitive progress. By embracing this holistic approach, we can create a future where community heritage is respected, preserved, and celebrated, while still allowing for positive change and growth.
The SixthSense Initiative is a registered nonprofit organisation hugely promoting children reading culture and human capacity development.

title.rendered: Let’s Celebrate Indigenous Festivals

content.rendered:
The celebration of indigenous festivals serves as a powerful catalyst for community unity and social cohesion, bridging the gaps between individuals and fostering a sense of shared identity. By embracing these time-honored traditions, communities can preserve their cultural heritage, allowing the rich tapestry of their history and customs to thrive.

Moreover, indigenous festivals offer a unique opportunity for cultural exchange and appreciation, allowing people from diverse backgrounds to come together and experience the vibrant traditions of the host community. This cross-cultural dialogue not only enriches the minds of those involved but also paves the way for greater understanding and empathy.
Furthermore, the promotion of indigenous festivals can have a tangible impact on local economies, as tourism and cultural events bring in revenue and create opportunities for local artisans and entrepreneurs. Ultimately, the celebration of indigenous festivals is a joyous occasion that strengthens community bonds, promotes cultural understanding, and contributes to the overall development of society.
I rejoice with the entire family of Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta and Omo Olowu Oduru in general on the celebration of 2025 Odun Omo Olowu. festival.
Happy celebration to HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE Otileta Vll Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom Abeokuta.

title.rendered: Oba is a King

content.rendered:
The title of Oba in Yoruba culture is indeed rich in significance, symbolising leadership, spiritual guidance, and custodianship of tradition. The Oba’s role as a bridge between the human and divine realms underscores the deep spiritual connection and reverence embedded in the culture. It’s fascinating how such titles and roles are passed down through generations, maintaining continuity and cultural heritage.

For instance, Olowu, as an ancient title holder, carries the weight of these responsibilities, ensuring the well-being of their people and the preservation of customs. Today, Oba Olowu Oluyalo superintends over the entire Owu Kingdom Abeokuta. From Oke Ago-Owu to part of Aworiland where we have people of Owu cultural affinity.
In Yorubaland, the routes to the throne vary significantly from one town to another, reflecting the unique history and traditions of each stool.
These variations reflect the diversity and complexity of Yoruba traditions and history. Each throne has its own distinct customs, rituals, and power structures, shaped by the unique experiences and cultural heritage of its people.
For emphasis, “Oba is a king”

title.rendered: Orunto: Substance Over Title

content.rendered:
In the heart of Owu Kingdom, a visionary leader has emerged, dedicated to shaping the minds and futures of the younger generation. Orunto Baalufe, also known as Chief Dr Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile, is a revered kingmaker and the founder of The SixthSense Initiative, a registered nonprofit organisation that has been making waves in promoting a culture of reading and intellectual curiosity among youths. With a deep understanding of the challenges that young people face, Orunto has devoted his life to creating opportunities that foster positive development and steer them away from the pitfalls of crime and anti-social behaviour.

At the core of Orunto’s initiatives is a profound belief in the transformative power of reading. He recognises that the minds of young people are like fertile soil, ready to be nurtured and cultivated, and that reading can be a potent tool in shaping their thoughts, values, and aspirations. By promoting a culture of reading, Orunto aims to engage young people in a meaningful way, diverting them from negative influences and empowering them to reach their full potential. His vision is simple yet profound: to create a community where young people are encouraged to read, learn, and grow, and where the love of knowledge becomes a guiding principle in their lives.
Orunto’s work with The SixthSense Initiative is multifaceted, addressing some of the most pressing issues that affect young people today. By instilling a love for reading, he seeks to combat the scourge of youth crime, including cultism, drug abuse, and other anti-social behaviours that can derail the lives of promising young individuals. Through his initiatives, Orunto is not only promoting literacy but also fostering a sense of purpose and direction among young people, helping them to navigate the challenges of adolescence and beyond.
One of the hallmarks of Orunto’s approach is his commitment to collaboration and partnership. He has engaged with various stakeholders, including government agencies and community leaders, to develop programs that promote reading as a fundamental aspect of youth development. By working together with those in authority, Orunto is able to leverage resources and expertise, amplifying the impact of his initiatives and creating a ripple effect that can be felt throughout the community.
The SixthSense Initiative is more than just a nonprofit organisation; it is a beacon of hope for the young people of Owu Kingdom. Through its programs and activities, the initiative provides a safe and supportive environment where young people can explore their interests, develop their talents, and build their confidence. By empowering youths with the knowledge and skills they need to succeed, Orunto’s work with The SixthSense Initiative is helping to create a brighter future for the community, one that is filled with promise and possibility.
Orunto Baalufe’s dedication to promoting positive change in his community is a testament to his character and leadership. As a kingmaker and a visionary leader, he has demonstrated a deep commitment to the welfare and development of young people, and his work with The SixthSense Initiative is a shining example of his passion and expertise. Through his initiatives, Orunto is not only shaping the minds of the next generation but also inspiring a sense of hope and optimism that will resonate throughout the community for years to come.
-SixthSense Outreach

title.rendered: Preserving Cultural Heritage In A Modern World: How Can We Balance Tradition and Innovation?

content.rendered:
In the pursuit of preserving cultural heritage, we find ourselves at the crossroads of tradition and innovation. As the world evolves at an unprecedented pace, it is imperative that we strike a delicate balance between honouring our roots and embracing the future. This harmonious blend of old and new is not merely a desirable outcome but a necessary endeavour to ensure the vitality and relevance of our cultural legacy.

To preserve the essence of our traditions, we must first document the stories, practices, and histories that define us. Through the lens of various media—videos, books, and digital archives—we can safeguard the memories and experiences of generations past. Education plays a pivotal role in this endeavour, as it is through both formal and informal programmes that we can impart the significance of our cultural heritage to younger generations. Moreover, engaging local communities in preservation efforts is crucial, as their voices and perspectives are the authentic echoes of our shared history.
Yet, as we honour the past, we must also embrace the innovations that can breathe new life into our cultural heritage. Digital preservation, through tools like 3D scanning and virtual reality, offers unprecedented opportunities to protect and showcase our cultural treasures. Creative reinterpretation by artists and innovators can infuse traditional elements with modern sensibilities, making them resonate with contemporary audiences. Sustainable tourism, when developed with care and respect, can support local economies while promoting cultural understanding.
The key to successfully navigating this balance lies in contextualisation, collaboration, and adaptation. We must consider the cultural context in which modern technologies and innovations are applied, ensuring that they serve to enhance rather than dilute our heritage. By fostering dialogue between traditional practitioners, innovators, and policymakers, we can cultivate a mutual understanding that respects both the past and the future. Finally, the adaptive reuse of cultural heritage sites and artifacts, when done thoughtfully, can meet modern needs without sacrificing the essence of what we cherish.
In embracing both tradition and innovation, we not only preserve our cultural heritage but also make it a living, breathing part of our modern world. It is through this synthesis that we can ensure our cultural legacy remains vibrant, relevant, and accessible to generations to come.
-Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Reminiscing Ibadan…We go Dey Dia!

content.rendered:
I was born in Ibadan, at the Sodeinde area (Race Course) and grew up at NW4/70 Salvation Army Road, Ekotedo, Ibadan (Ile Baba HM Suberu)
Ni Ibadan ni won bi mi si emi won Baba won loni ile…
All my arena of childhood eregele was Ekotedo Iyaolobe, Idi Oro, Oke Padi, Dugbe Alawowo, Cooperative Corner, Omitowoju, Inalende, Adamasigba, Sabo and other dangerous horo-si-horo.
My knowledge of Ibadanland was following the popular King of Boys and Egungun. With these two escapades I knew many areas of Ibadan.
As Omo soja, awa Omo lile! I went to Army Children School, Eleyeye and Mokola, Ibadan. This was my other training ground including Race Course and Golf Field. We go waka from Sabo to Layipo through Dandaru to Igbo Agala.
It’s great fun that I have fond memories of my childhood and the places that shaped my experiences. Nostalgically, sweet!
iFelicitate HIM Oba Rashid Ladoja, Olubadan to ilu Ibadan. Kabiyesi o!
– Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Nigeria: What an old age

content.rendered:
As Nigeria celebrates 65 years of independence on October 1, 2025, the nation pauses to reflect on its journey, acknowledging both progress and challenges. Despite being blessed with vast natural resources, Nigeria faces complex issues that hinder its growth and development.
The country’s economic struggles are deeply rooted in its heavy reliance on oil revenues, which has stifled diversification efforts and exposed the nation to the unpredictable nature of global markets. This vulnerability has far-reaching consequences, affecting the lives of millions.
Insecurity is another pressing concern, with terrorism, banditry, and kidnapping plaguing various parts of the country. These threats not only undermine peace and stability but also impact agricultural productivity and food security, leaving many vulnerable to hunger and poverty.
The statistics are stark: over half of Nigerians live below the poverty line, and approximately 33 million people are projected to face acute food insecurity in 2025. Corruption and weak institutions exacerbate these challenges, hindering Nigeria’s development and eroding trust in its systems.
However, amidst these challenges lie opportunities for growth and renewal. Diversifying the economy, for instance, could reduce Nigeria’s dependence on oil and unlock new avenues for job creation and economic progress. Investing in sectors like agriculture, manufacturing, technology, and renewable energy could be a game-changer.
With over 60% of its population under 30, Nigeria’s youth represent a powerful force for change. By investing in education, job creation, and entrepreneurship programmes, the nation could harness the energy and creativity of its young people to drive growth and development.
Strengthening institutions, promoting transparency, and enforcing accountability are also crucial steps toward building trust and stimulating economic progress. As Nigeria celebrates its 65th anniversary, the theme “Nigeria at 65: All Hands on Deck for a Greater Nation” serves as a rallying cry for collective action. Leaders and citizens alike are calling for a renewed commitment to unity, peace, and progress, recognising that a stronger, more prosperous Nigeria is within reach if all stakeholders work together toward a common goal.
Nigeria at 65 is a good old age!
-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta 
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative and Sixth Sense Series Publications

title.rendered: History Reintroduced Into School Curriculum: Experts Weigh In

content.rendered:
Abeokuta  Nigeria – The reintroduction of history into the school academic curriculum has been welcomed by experts, who believe it will help shape the direction of the country. Chief Abiodun Lasile, a proponent of the reading culture, has emphasized the importance of knowing one’s past and heroes.
According to Chief Lasile, “A people without history can go into extinction, and history plays a major role in the direction of man.” He noted that most leaders do not know their heroes and their thoughts, and that this lack of knowledge can have far-reaching consequences. “A people needs to know their past and heroes,” he stressed.
Chief Lasile expressed gladness that the controversy over the issue has been laid to rest, and that history will now be reintroduced into the school curriculum. He believes that this will afford people the opportunity to connect with their past and chart a better course for the future.
The expert also emphasized the importance of teaching history to kindergarten students, so that they can grow up with a sense of their heritage. “We must let our kindergarten know our history,” he said. He also stressed the need to prepare new teachers for this role, so that they can play it very well.
Chief Lasile’s comments come as a welcome relief to many who have been advocating for the reintroduction of history into the school curriculum. He noted that a decade or two decades is a long time in a people’s life, and that it is essential to learn about recent past events, rather than just focusing on old history.
The reintroduction of history into the school curriculum is expected to have a positive impact on the country, by helping to shape the direction of the youth and promoting a sense of national identity. As Chief Lasile noted, history has the propensity to direct the youths, and it is essential that they are taught about their past and heroes.
-SixthSense Outreach

title.rendered: Peace Is Untapped Abundant Blessing

content.rendered:
In the heart of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, Chief Abiodun Lasile, the Orunto of Owu Kingdom, stood as a beacon of peace and tranquility. He believed that peace is a precious commodity, essential for daily life, and a state of mind that fosters overall well-being. According to him, peaceful families are the building blocks of a harmonious society, and collective peace is the foundation upon which stable and prosperous communities are built.

In a world plagued by conflict, corruption, and social unrest, Chief Lasile’s message resonated deeply. He emphasised that peace is not just the absence of conflict but a profound sense of calm, understanding, and respect for one another. As a kingmaker and traditional chief, he worked tirelessly to promote peace and unity in his community, inspiring others to do the same ¹.
One day, Chief Lasile joined forces with the Olowu ADR Committee to host the Society for Peace Studies and Practice. Together, they shared stories, experiences, and challenges, highlighting the crucial role of mediation sessions in promoting peace. This collective effort underscored the importance of collaboration in achieving a more peaceful society.
As Chief Lasile reflected on his journey, he realized that peace is not a destination but a continuous journey. It requires effort, dedication, and a commitment to understanding and empathy. Through his leadership, he demonstrated that even in the face of adversity, peace can prevail.
Key Elements of Peace
– State of Mind: Peace begins within, fostering a sense of calm and well-being.
– Family Unity: Peaceful families form the foundation of a harmonious society.
– Collective Action: Community-wide efforts promote peace and stability.
– Education and Empowerment: Access to quality education and empowerment are crucial in promoting peace and combating corruption.
Chief Lasile’s story serves as a testament to the power of peace and the impact one person can have on their community. His leadership philosophy, rooted in compassion, inspiration, and responsibility, continues to inspire others to strive for peace.
As we reflect on Chief Lasile’s words, we are reminded that peace is indeed a vital component of our daily lives. By working together and promoting understanding, empathy, and unity, we can build a more peaceful and prosperous world.

title.rendered: International Peace Day with Olowu ADR

content.rendered:
In commemoration of International Peace Day, the Olowu ADR Committee hosted the Society for Peace Studies and Practice, led by Chairman Simiat Abaru.

On behalf of the Olowu ADR Committee, Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile (Orunto Owu Abeokuta) shared our history, experiences, challenges, and successes with the group. The engagement was fruitful, highlighting the impactful role of mediation sessions in promoting peace within our community.
And, presentation of award to HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE Otileta Vll Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom Abeokuta
Wishing peace and harmony to people worldwide on this special day.

title.rendered: Olowu of Owu, Abeokuta at the Nordic-Africa Business Forum & Awards 2025

content.rendered:
Alayeluwa Oba Saka Matemilola, Oluyalo Otileta VII, delivered a powerful keynote on “Legacy of Change”, emphasising legacy, vision, change, and lasting impact as drivers of transformation.
Kabiyesi shared his inspiring vision and impactful initiatives including the Meal-A-Day Program, Women Empowerment Fund, Youth Skill Acquisition, Free Healthcare Insurance, and Scholarships.
Kabiyesi urged all to drive positive change that makes the world a better place.

#OwuKingdom #OlowuOfOwu #LegacyOfChange #NordicAfricaSummit #LeadershipWithImpact #GlobalChangeMakers

title.rendered: SixthSense SmartWords…Traditional Fallacy

content.rendered:
Traditional issues require thoughtful consideration, not off-the-cuff remarks, as they can easily lead to misrepresentation. Given the historical significance and cultural importance of these matters, it’s crucial to approach them with responsibility and accuracy, especially in public or among knowledgeable individuals.
Misrepresentation isn’t just an oversight; it’s a disservice to the traditional roles and custodians.
Not all dramatis personae in tradition are ignoramus or listeners to non factual statements at falsehood are accomplices. Many lobesidedness is what they traditional circle is battling with cum half knowledge.
Not all individuals involved in traditional matters are ignorant or passive recipients of misinformation. Rather, some may be complicit in spreading falsehoods. The traditional circle often struggles with imbalance and half-knowledge, which can be detrimental.
I’m highlighting the importance of critical thinking, accountability, and informed decision-making within traditional context.
What is fallacy? It is an error in reasoning that makes an argument unsound or invalid, even if it appears convincing. Fallacies can be unintentional mistakes or intentional attempts to deceive or manipulate, and they fundamentally weaken an argument’s logical foundation. Recognizing fallacies helps you avoid being misled and strengthens your own ability to construct persuasive, logically sound arguments.
These are standard statements of definition of fact, not postulation and conjecture. We must not lead ourselves into shame or create lack of knowledge to presume knowledgeable beings have slept through silence.
The traditional institution is cultivating wisdom and discernment to promote serenity, drive meaningful reformation, and preserve the richness of our refined cultures and traditions.

title.rendered: Loyalty in Traditional Followership

content.rendered:
Loyalty is more than just blindly following a leader; it requires a genuine commitment to their vision and goals. According to Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR, a respected figure from Owu Kingdom, true loyalty stems from a deep-seated dedication to the leader’s objectives, rather than mere obedience. This perspective highlights the significance of shared values, trust, and mutual respect in building strong relationships and achieving collective success.

In essence, loyalty involves a sincere commitment to a leader’s goals and vision, fostering a sense of unity and cooperation. When leaders and followers share common values, it strengthens their bond and promotes a sense of belonging. Trust and respect are also crucial components of loyalty, serving as the foundation for effective leadership and collaboration.
Key Elements of Loyalty
– Sincere Commitment: A genuine dedication to the leader’s goals and vision, driving individuals to work towards a common purpose.
– Shared Values: Common values between leaders and followers promote unity, strengthening their relationship and fostering a sense of cooperation.
– Trust and Respect: Essential for effective leadership and collaboration, trust and respect build loyalty and encourage collective success.
In the context of traditional leadership, loyalty is not about blind obedience but about working together towards a shared purpose. By being committed to a leader’s vision, individuals can contribute to achieving shared goals and creating a positive impact. Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR’s insights emphasize the importance of loyalty in leadership, highlighting its role in building strong relationships and driving collective success.
-SixthSense Outreach
