title.rendered: Two Sides to a Coin and the Edge

content.rendered:
I am a multifaceted individual, and through this write-up, you’re catching a glimpse of another dimension of my being – a journey of self-revelation that knows no bounds, unfolding endlessly as we explore the depths of my thoughts and experiences.
“I am Abiodun Lasile, and my philosophy is rooted in the profound belief that collective responsibility is the cornerstone of a stronger, more equitable, and prosperous nation. I firmly believe that when individuals come together to actively participate in national development, civic engagement, social cohesion, economic empowerment, environmental stewardship, accountability, education, and community development, we can create a brighter future for all.
At the heart of my philosophy lies a deep commitment to promoting integrity and transparency. I advocate for a multifaceted approach to overcome corruption, one that weaves a fabric of accountability and trust. By emphasizing the importance of quality education and empowerment, I believe we can equip citizens with the tools they need to demand their rights, needs, and basic necessities, ultimately bridging the inequalities that plague our society.
For me, education and empowerment are essential pillars of a thriving society. By ensuring access to quality education for all, we can empower citizens to become active participants in the development of our nation. I also highlight the significance of traditional values such as discipline, hospitality, respect for elders, and communal living in sustaining community harmony.
Furthermore, I encourage individuals to embrace unity and selflessness through volunteering, promoting a society driven by genuine leadership committed to humanity. My philosophy is built on several key pillars, including civic engagement, social cohesion, economic empowerment, environmental stewardship, accountability, education, and community development.
Through these pillars, I envision a society where collective action, individual responsibility, and traditional values come together to build a stronger, more prosperous nation. I am driven by a passion for creating positive change and empowering individuals to become the best versions of themselves. As I continue on this journey, I remain committed to my philosophy, working tirelessly to inspire and uplift those around me.”

Just like an onion, human beings are indeed composed of layers, each one revealing a new depth, complexity, and richness. This comparison highlights the multifaceted nature of individuals, and how we can continue to grow, learn, and discover new aspects of ourselves.


The onion’s layers can also symbolizes:
– Complexity: Each layer adds depth and nuance to our personalities, experiences, and emotions.
– Growth: Just as onions grow in layers, we too can develop and mature over time.
– Resilience: Onions can be peeled back, but they still remain intact; similarly, we can face challenges and setbacks, yet continue to thrive.

title.rendered: A Heartfelt Commendation to the Orunto Baalufe

content.rendered:
On behalf of HRH Oba Joshua Olusegun Phillips Ogunsola, the Orunda of Olorunda, and the entire Olorunda community, we extend our warmest commendations to the esteemed Chief Abiodun Lasile, the Orunto Baalufe of Owu Kingdom. Your tireless efforts in preserving and promoting the rich cultural heritage of Olorunda kingdom have not gone unnoticed.
Your dedication to tradition and innovation is truly inspiring, and we are all proud to witness your impactful leadership. The digital platform “Orunto Owu Abeokuta” is a groundbreaking initiative that showcases the history, customs, and traditions of the Owu Kingdom to the world. This pioneering effort ensures that our cultural legacy is not only preserved but also made accessible to future generations and the global community.
Your coronation on September 22nd, 2023, marked the beginning of a new era in the Owu Kingdom’s cultural narrative. As a proud son of Olorunda Kingdom, your contributions to the preservation of our cultural heritage are invaluable.

Please accept our sincerest appreciation for your dedication to the Owu Kingdom’s rich cultural legacy. We are honored to have you as a custodian of our cultural heritage, and we look forward to seeing the continued impact of your work. Omo Olowu Oduru, Ajifepesere! Indeed, we are all proud of you, Chief Abiodun Lasile, and eagerly anticipate your future endeavors.
AbdulAzeez Mubashir Adekunle,
Akinwunmi village.
PS. I Appreciate

title.rendered: Reading Together

content.rendered:
In a faraway land, nestled between majestic mountains and a wide, serene Abedopa river, there was a town known for its solitary way of life. The people there valued independence above all, believing that the strongest among them were those who could fend for themselves. Each person built their home in isolation, separated by tall stone walls that symbolized their self-sufficiency. Though the town was peaceful, there was an unspoken emptiness that hung in the air, for while they were strong in their solitude, they were fragile in their isolation.
One day, an old traveler arrived, weary from his journey. He carried with him only a small, battered book, its cover worn from years of use. Curious about this stranger, a few townspeople cautiously approached him. The traveler, seeing their interest, smiled kindly and began to read aloud from his book. It was a story of a distant kingdom where people lived and learned together, sharing knowledge and building a society rooted in wisdom and mutual support.
At first, the townspeople listened with mild interest, but as the traveler read on, they became captivated by the tale. The story spoke of a time when the kingdom had faced great challenges—famine, war, and uncertainty. But instead of crumbling under the weight of these trials, the people had come together, pooling their knowledge and experiences. The farmers taught one another better methods of planting, the healers shared new remedies, and the scholars opened their minds to new ideas. Through their shared pursuit of knowledge, they not only survived but thrived, building a society that was stronger than any one person could have imagined.
As the traveler’s voice wove through the air, the townspeople found themselves drawn to the idea that perhaps they, too, had something to gain from one another. For the first time, they considered that the knowledge they each held—skills passed down through generations, personal experiences, insights—was incomplete on its own. They began to wonder if they, like the people in the traveler’s story, could become something greater by uniting their wisdom.
Intrigued, a small group of townspeople invited the traveler to stay. They gathered each evening in the town square, where he would read to them from his book, and in turn, they would share their own stories. The farmer told of the changing seasons and the secrets of the earth; the blacksmith spoke of the strength hidden within iron and fire; the weaver shared the delicate art of spinning thread into cloth. As they shared, they began to teach one another, their individual knowledge intertwining into a tapestry of collective wisdom.
Weeks turned into months, and soon the walls that once separated them began to crumble—not by force, but by choice. The townspeople realized that their true strength did not lie in their ability to stand alone but in their willingness to learn from one another. The solitary town transformed into a thriving community where knowledge flowed freely, from one heart to the next.
Together, they built stronger homes, crafted better tools, and nurtured healthier crops. But more than that, they found that the support they gave each other went beyond practical skills—it extended into the realm of the spirit. When one was weary, the others would lend their strength. When one faltered, the others would lift them up. The collective wisdom they had fostered through their shared pursuit of knowledge became a wellspring of resilience and hope.
And so, the town flourished, not because any single person had all the answers, but because they had learned to seek answers together. Their bond, forged through the stories they had shared and the wisdom they had cultivated, became the foundation of a new kind of strength—one that empowered them not only to survive but to thrive, uplifted and supported by one another.

The old traveler, having witnessed the transformation of the town, smiled to himself and continued on his journey, leaving behind his well-worn book. It was no longer needed, for the town had discovered the secret within its pages: that through the shared pursuit of knowledge, people are united, and in their unity, they find a strength that empowers them to uplift one another, far beyond anything they could achieve alone.
And so it was, the town that once stood in isolation became a beacon of wisdom and strength, where the people, bound together by their shared learning, became stronger for one another, forever united in their pursuit of knowledge.

title.rendered: Reading Can Build Confidence

content.rendered:
Here are some ways:

1. Knowledge acquisition: Reading exposes you to new ideas, information, and perspectives, making you more knowledgeable and informed. This increased understanding can boost your confidence in discussions and decision-making.
2. Personal growth: Reading self-help, motivational, or personal development books can provide strategies and insights to overcome challenges, helping you develop a more confident mindset.
3. Empathy and connection: Reading about characters or individuals who face similar struggles can help you feel less isolated and more empowered to tackle your own challenges.
4. Improved critical thinking: Reading critically can enhance your analytical skills, enabling you to evaluate information more effectively and make more informed decisions.
5. Vocabulary expansion: Reading widely can improve your communication skills, allowing you to express yourself more clearly and confidently.
6. Escape and relaxation: Reading can provide a healthy escape from stress and anxiety, helping you feel more centered and confident.

By broadening your knowledge, fostering personal growth, and enhancing your skills, reading can be a powerful tool for building confidence.

title.rendered: Olowu Hosts Minister of Women Affairs for Launch of Olowu Hope Initiative – Women Empowerment Fund

content.rendered:
Towards the launch of the Olowu Hope Initiative – Women Empowerment Fund, Alayeluwa Oba Saka Adelola Matemilola, the Olowu of Owu Kingdom, hosted the Honorable Minister of Women Affairs, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, in a grand ceremony that highlighted the kingdom’s commitment to women’s empowerment and community development.
This initiative is designed to support women with no-interest capital and provide skills acquisition programmes to help them start or grow their businesses. It also focuses on equipping women with tools for education, digital literacy, vocational training, and income growth, ensuring sustainable empowerment and economic inclusion.
In Kabiesi Royal’s address, he stressed the vital role women play in building resilient communities, noting that empowering women translates to uplifting families and strengthening society as a whole.
In her remarks, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim commended the Olowu for his visionary leadership and reaffirmed the Federal Government’s dedication to initiatives that advance women’s participation in economic and social development. She emphasized the alignment of the initiative with national goals of broadening access to education, digital innovation, and entrepreneurship opportunities for women across the country.

With the launch of the Olowu Hope Initiative, Women Empowerment Fund, Owu Kingdom has positioned itself as a model for grassroots-driven empowerment, where traditional leadership collaborates with government to create lasting impact.

title.rendered: Overcome Corruption by Promoting Integrity and Transparency

content.rendered:
The Path to Integrity

In the quest to vanquish corruption and foster a culture of integrity and transparency, societies must embark on a multifaceted journey. This odyssey requires a comprehensive approach, one that weaves together various strategies to create a fabric of accountability and trust.

Pillars of Strength

At the heart of this endeavour lies the need to strengthen institutions. Independent judiciaries, anti-corruption agencies, and robust legislative frameworks form the bedrock of a just society. These institutions must be nurtured and supported, allowing them to function without fear or favour.

The Light of Transparency

Transparency is the beacon that illuminates the darkest corners of corruption. Open data initiatives, public disclosure of government information, and accessible records of public officials’ activities are essential in promoting transparency. By shedding light on the actions of those in power, societies can prevent the shadows in which corruption thrives.

A Culture of Integrity

Fostering a culture of integrity is a crucial step in this journey. Education and awareness campaigns can instill the values of ethics and integrity in the hearts and minds of citizens. By promoting ethical leadership and integrating ethics into school curricula and professional training programs, societies can create a new generation of leaders who prioritise integrity over personal gain.

The Sword of Accountability

Accountability is the sword that strikes fear into the hearts of corrupt officials. Mechanisms like audits, oversight bodies, and public scrutiny must be employed to hold public officials and institutions accountable for their actions. Consequences for corrupt behaviour and rewards for integrity will serve as a deterrent to those who would seek to abuse power.

The Voice of Whistleblowers

Whistleblowers are the unsung heroes in the fight against corruption. Protecting and supporting those who report wrongdoing is essential in creating a culture of accountability. Safe and confidential channels for reporting must be established, and whistleblowers must be shielded from retaliation.

The Power of Civic Engagement

Civic engagement is the lifeblood of a healthy society. By engaging citizens in the fight against corruption through participatory governance, public consultations, and active civil society involvement, societies can create a sense of ownership and responsibility among citizens. Citizens must be encouraged to demand accountability and transparency from their leaders.

The Shield of Anti-Corruption Measures

Robust anti-corruption laws, regulations, and policies are the shield that protects societies from the ravages of corruption. Conflict-of-interest regulations, asset disclosure requirements, and anti-bribery laws must be developed and enforced to prevent corruption.

The Watchdog of Media Freedom

A free and independent media is the watchdog that keeps power in check. By ensuring that the media can investigate and report on corruption without fear of censorship or reprisal, societies can create a culture of transparency and accountability.

The Sword of Technology

Technology is the sword that can cut through the red tape of bureaucracy. Digital platforms for reporting corruption, online portals for public information, and digital tools for tracking government spending can enhance transparency and accountability.

The Bond of International Cooperation

Finally, international cooperation is the bond that unites societies in their quest for integrity and transparency. By collaborating with international organisations and other countries, societies can share best practices, support global anti-corruption initiatives, and create a global culture of integrity.

By implementing these strategies, societies can work towards overcoming corruption and promoting a culture of integrity and transparency. The journey may be long and arduous, but with determination and perseverance, a brighter future can be forged.

Let’s unite to build a better Nigeria! By overcoming corruption and promoting integrity and transparency, we can unlock our nation’s true potential. The choice is ours, and it starts with our leaders. Together, we can create a brighter future for Nigeria.

-Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative.

title.rendered: Overcome Corruption by Promoting Integrity and Transparency

content.rendered:
The Path to Integrity
In the quest to vanquish corruption and foster a culture of integrity and transparency, societies must embark on a multifaceted journey. This odyssey requires a comprehensive approach, one that weaves together various strategies to create a fabric of accountability and trust.
Pillars of Strength
At the heart of this endeavour lies the need to strengthen institutions. Independent judiciaries, anti-corruption agencies, and robust legislative frameworks form the bedrock of a just society. These institutions must be nurtured and supported, allowing them to function without fear or favour.
The Light of Transparency
Transparency is the beacon that illuminates the darkest corners of corruption. Open data initiatives, public disclosure of government information, and accessible records of public officials’ activities are essential in promoting transparency. By shedding light on the actions of those in power, societies can prevent the shadows in which corruption thrives.
A Culture of Integrity
Fostering a culture of integrity is a crucial step in this journey. Education and awareness campaigns can instill the values of ethics and integrity in the hearts and minds of citizens. By promoting ethical leadership and integrating ethics into school curricula and professional training programs, societies can create a new generation of leaders who prioritise integrity over personal gain.
The Sword of Accountability
Accountability is the sword that strikes fear into the hearts of corrupt officials. Mechanisms like audits, oversight bodies, and public scrutiny must be employed to hold public officials and institutions accountable for their actions. Consequences for corrupt behaviour and rewards for integrity will serve as a deterrent to those who would seek to abuse power.
The Voice of Whistleblowers
Whistleblowers are the unsung heroes in the fight against corruption. Protecting and supporting those who report wrongdoing is essential in creating a culture of accountability. Safe and confidential channels for reporting must be established, and whistleblowers must be shielded from retaliation.
The Power of Civic Engagement
Civic engagement is the lifeblood of a healthy society. By engaging citizens in the fight against corruption through participatory governance, public consultations, and active civil society involvement, societies can create a sense of ownership and responsibility among citizens. Citizens must be encouraged to demand accountability and transparency from their leaders.
The Shield of Anti-Corruption Measures
Robust anti-corruption laws, regulations, and policies are the shield that protects societies from the ravages of corruption. Conflict-of-interest regulations, asset disclosure requirements, and anti-bribery laws must be developed and enforced to prevent corruption.
The Watchdog of Media Freedom
A free and independent media is the watchdog that keeps power in check. By ensuring that the media can investigate and report on corruption without fear of censorship or reprisal, societies can create a culture of transparency and accountability.
The Sword of Technology
Technology is the sword that can cut through the red tape of bureaucracy. Digital platforms for reporting corruption, online portals for public information, and digital tools for tracking government spending can enhance transparency and accountability.
The Bond of International Cooperation
Finally, international cooperation is the bond that unites societies in their quest for integrity and transparency. By collaborating with international organisations and other countries, societies can share best practices, support global anti-corruption initiatives, and create a global culture of integrity.
By implementing these strategies, societies can work towards overcoming corruption and promoting a culture of integrity and transparency. The journey may be long and arduous, but with determination and perseverance, a brighter future can be forged.
Let’s unite to build a better Nigeria! By overcoming corruption and promoting integrity and transparency, we can unlock our nation’s true potential. The choice is ours, and it starts with our leaders. Together, we can create a brighter future for Nigeria.

title.rendered: I Am an Author and Writer

content.rendered:
As an author and writer, you have the power to craft compelling stories, convey important messages, and inspire others through your words.
I write Children stories and fictional reality books. Writing for children and exploring fictional realities can be so much fun and incredibly rewarding.
Children’s stories can spark imagination, teach valuable lessons, and create lifelong readers. Fictional reality books can transport readers to new worlds, challenge their perspectives, and explore complex themes in an engaging way.
I have six published books to my credit under the Sixth Sense Series Publications with many manuscripts. I’m working on traditional narratives and cultural literatures.

I congratulate myself on having six published books! That’s a significant achievement for me, especially in the realm of traditional narratives and literatures.
My work likely preserves cultural heritage, shares timeless stories, and inspires readers. Traditional narratives often carry valuable lessons, morals, and historical significance.
I hugely promote reading culture and human capacity development with passion
Promoting reading culture and human capacity development is crucial for individual and societal growth. Through literature, we can:
1. Foster critical thinking and empathy
2. Preserve cultural heritage and traditions
3. Develop emotional intelligence and self-awareness
4. Enhance creativity and imagination
5. Build knowledge and understanding of the world
My work as an author and writer contributes significantly to these goals above. Let’s make our children read, again!

-Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR 
Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta 
Founder Coordinator The SixthSense Initiative and Sixth Sense Series Publications.

title.rendered: The Power of Collective Responsibility: A Blueprint for Nation-Building

content.rendered:
As I ponder the fabric of our society, I am reminded of the profound impact of collective responsibility on nation-building. When individuals, communities, and institutions converge towards a shared vision, the outcome is nothing short of transformative. This synergy yields shared progress, increased accountability, improved social cohesion, and more effective problem-solving.
By acknowledging our individual roles in contributing to the greater good, we cultivate a sense of ownership and responsibility that propels positive change and development. This collective ethos is the bedrock upon which a stronger, more equitable, and prosperous nation is built.
The Pillars of Collective Responsibility
1. Civic Engagement: Active participation in democratic processes, community service, and volunteerism ignites the flame of citizenship and civic duty.
2. Social Cohesion: Fostering unity, tolerance, and understanding among diverse groups weaves a tapestry of inclusivity and social harmony.
3. Economic Empowerment: Supporting local businesses, entrepreneurship, and education unlocks the potential for economic growth and self-sufficiency.
4. Environmental Stewardship: Protecting natural resources and promoting sustainability ensures a healthy and thriving planet for future generations.
5. Accountability: Holding leaders and institutions accountable for their actions promotes transparency, trust, and good governance.
6. Education and Awareness: Promoting critical thinking, media literacy, and civic education empowers citizens to make informed decisions and demand their rights.
7. Community Development: Investing in initiatives that benefit marginalised or underprivileged groups bridges the gap between different segments of society, fostering a more equitable and just nation.
By embracing these pillars of collective responsibility, we can collectively contribute to building a nation that is stronger, more resilient, and more prosperous for all.

-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative.

title.rendered: SixthSense SmartWords…Value Beyond Monetary

content.rendered:
In a world where the value of everything is often measured by its price tag, it’s easy to get caught up in the idea that every action, every service, and every gesture must be compensated. However, there’s a profound truth that lies beyond this transactional mindset – the joy and fulfillment that come from selfless giving. As according to Chief Dr Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Let me illustrate with this story of a buddy. I still remember a moment that changed my perspective on giving forever. I was volunteering at a local soup kitchen, serving meals to those in need. As I handed a warm bowl of soup to a frail elderly man, he looked up at me with tears in his eyes and said, “Thank you, young one. This means more to me than you’ll ever know.” In that moment, something shifted within me. I realised that the value of my service wasn’t in the monetary compensation I might have received, but in the smile on his face, the warmth in his eyes, and the knowledge that I had made a difference in his life.
From that day forward, I made a conscious decision to prioritise kindness and generosity in my life. I began to look for opportunities to give without expectation of reward – whether it was volunteering my time, offering a listening ear to a friend in need, or simply holding the door open for a stranger. And with each act of selfless giving, I felt a sense of joy and fulfillment that I had never experienced before.
It was as if I had developed a sixth sense – a sense that guided me to prioritise kindness and generosity, even when it didn’t make logical sense. I began to see the world in a different light, as a place where every interaction was an opportunity to make a positive impact. And I discovered that the more I gave, the more I received in return – not in monetary terms, but in the form of meaningful relationships, a sense of purpose, and a deeper connection to the world around me.
One day, I had the opportunity to participate in a community project that brought clean water to a rural village. The villagers had been struggling to access clean water for years, and the project was entirely funded by donations. As I worked alongside the villagers, I saw the impact that our collective efforts had on their lives. I saw children playing in the clean water, laughing and splashing without the worry of getting sick. I saw mothers who no longer had to worry about the health of their families. And I saw a community that was transformed by the simple act of kindness.
In that moment, I realised that selfless giving wasn’t just about the recipient – it was also about the giver. It was about the kind of person I wanted to be, the kind of world I wanted to live in, and the kind of impact I wanted to make. And I knew that I would continue to prioritise kindness and generosity, not just because it felt good, but because it was a fundamental part of who I was.
As I reflect on my journey, I am reminded that the true value of giving lies not in what we receive in return, but in the positive impact we have on the world around us. When we give without expectation of reward, we open ourselves up to a world of possibilities – possibilities for growth, for connection, and for making a difference in the lives of others. And it’s in these moments of selfless giving that we discover our truest selves, and the world discovers its true potential.

title.rendered: Failure and Refusal an Impetus

content.rendered:
The wisdom encapsulated in the phrase “Failure and refusal counting is just a challenge not an end but an impetus to continue” is a profound reminder that our response to adversity defines our trajectory. When we encounter setbacks and failures, we have a choice: we can let them defeat us, or we can use them as stepping stones for growth and progress.

This mindset is a powerful catalyst for success. By viewing failures and setbacks as challenges rather than endpoints, we open ourselves up to a world of possibility. Every obstacle becomes an opportunity to learn, to grow, and to refine our approach. We recognize that setbacks are a natural part of the journey, and that every challenge can be overcome with determination, perseverance, and resilience.
As we navigate the twists and turns of life, we discover that growth happens through iteration. By embracing challenges and learning from our failures, we can develop new skills, refine our approach, and ultimately achieve our goals. This process of iteration is not just about overcoming obstacles, but about becoming better versions of ourselves.
The benefits of this mindset are multifaceted. As we face challenges head-on and persevere through difficulties, we build confidence and develop a sense of self-assurance in our abilities. We cultivate our critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and we learn to approach problems with creativity and innovation. Perhaps most importantly, we stay motivated, even in the face of adversity, by focusing on the potential for growth and progress.
In the end, it is not the absence of failures that defines our success, but our response to them. Every successful person has faced setbacks and failures along the way, but it is how they respond to those challenges that ultimately determines their success. By adopting the mindset that failure is not an end, but an impetus to continue, we can unlock our full potential and achieve greatness.

title.rendered: Communication in Leadership

content.rendered:
The art of communication is the lifeblood of any successful endeavour, be it leadership, teamwork, or relationships. To communicate effectively is to weave a delicate balance of clarity, empathy, and understanding. It begins with clear articulation, where one expresses their vision, goals, and expectations with precision and simplicity, ensuring that the message is conveyed without ambiguity.

But effective communication is not just about speaking; it is equally about listening. Active listening is the cornerstone of meaningful interaction, where one pays attention not just to the words, but to the underlying emotions and intentions. It involves asking clarifying questions, restating what has been understood, and ensuring that both parties are on the same page.

Beyond words, nonverbal communication plays a pivotal role. The subtleties of body language, the tone of voice, and the nuances of facial expressions can convey just as much information as the spoken word. Being aware of these nonverbal cues can make all the difference in how a message is received.
Adaptability is also key in effective communication. Different audiences require different approaches, and being able to adjust one’s communication style to suit the needs, preferences, and level of understanding of others is crucial. This flexibility ensures that the message is not only delivered but also understood and acted upon.
Feedback is another vital component of effective communication. Encouraging open and honest feedback creates a culture of transparency and trust, where individuals feel valued and heard. Being receptive to constructive criticism allows for growth and improvement, both personally and professionally.
Certain techniques can enhance the effectiveness of communication. Using “I” statements instead of accusatory language helps to avoid blame and defensiveness, fostering a more open and collaborative environment. Asking open-ended questions encourages discussion and exploration, while paraphrasing ensures clarity and shows that one is actively engaged in the conversation. Avoiding jargon and technical terms that might confuse others ensures that the message is accessible to all.
When communication is effective, the benefits are manifold. Trust is built, misunderstandings are avoided, collaboration is fostered, and results are driven. Clear communication of goals and expectations motivates others to work towards achieving them, creating a sense of purpose and direction.
In essence, effective communication is the foundation upon which successful relationships, teams, and organisations are built. It requires a combination of clarity, empathy, adaptability, and a willingness to listen and learn. By mastering the art of communication, one can unlock the full potential of their relationships and endeavours, leading to greater understanding, collaboration, and success.

title.rendered: Key Features of Olumo Rock

content.rendered:
Tourist Attractions
 – Climbing the Rock: Visitors can climb to the top via stairs or elevator (though elevators may not always be functional).
 – Ancient Caves: Explore the caves where Egba warriors hid during wars.
– Art Gallery: Discover local artwork and purchase souvenirs.
– Lisabi Garden: A tribute to the legendary warrior Lisabi Agbongbo Akala, featuring three majestic trees.

 Visiting Information:
– Location: Olumo Rock is situated near Itoku Market in Abeokuta.
– Opening Hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM, daily.
– Getting There: Accessible by car or public transport, with options for motorcycle taxis (okada) or tricycles (keke) within Abeokuta.
– Tips:
– Visit early in the morning to avoid heat.
– Wear comfortable shoes for climbing.
– Engage with local guides for a more immersive experience

title.rendered: The Unyielding Spirit of Abiodun Lasile: A Tale of Dedication and Perseverance

content.rendered:
In a world where dreams are often suffocated by the weight of mediocrity, Abiodun Lasile, DL MnbR, stood tall as a beacon of hope and determination. His mantra, “Ready to Work, Ready to be Tired,” was more than just a phrase – it was a way of life, a testament to his unwavering dedication and unrelenting passion for greatness.

Abiodun’s journey was not one of overnight success, but rather a testament to the power of persistence and hard work. He had always been driven by a fierce desire to push beyond his limits, to test his mettle, and to emerge victorious in the face of adversity. And so, he embarked on a path that would take him to the pinnacle of success, fueled by his mantra and guided by his unyielding spirit.

As Abiodun navigated the challenges of his journey, he encountered numerous obstacles that threatened to derail his progress. There were times when the road ahead seemed uncertain, when the weight of his responsibilities felt crushing, and when the voices of doubt whispered in his ear. But Abiodun refused to be deterred. With every step forward, he drew strength from his mantra, reminding himself that he was ready to work, ready to be tired, and ready to emerge triumphant.

The phrase “Ready to Work” was more than just a declaration of intent – it was a battle cry, a call to arms that summoned Abiodun to push beyond his limits and to strive for excellence. It was a reminder that success is not a destination, but a journey, one that requires dedication, perseverance, and a willingness to learn and grow.

And when the exhaustion crept in, when the body and mind screamed for respite, Abiodun would draw comfort from the second part of his mantra – “Ready to be Tired.” He knew that the physical and mental exhaustion that came with hard work was a temporary state, one that would give way to a sense of accomplishment and pride. He knew that the tiredness was not a sign of weakness, but a badge of honor, a testament to his unwavering commitment to his craft.

As Abiodun’s journey progressed, his mantra became a source of inspiration for those around him. His unwavering dedication and unrelenting passion inspired others to push beyond their own limits, to strive for greatness, and to never give up in the face of adversity. And Abiodun’s story served as a powerful reminder that success is within reach, that anything is possible with persistence, determination, and a willingness to push through challenges.

Years later, Abiodun’s name would become synonymous with greatness, his mantra a rallying cry for those who dared to dream big and push beyond their limits. And though the journey had been long and arduous, Abiodun knew that it was worth it, for he had discovered that the greatest reward was not the destination, but the journey itself – the journey of self-discovery, growth, and transformation.

In the end, Abiodun’s story would serve as a testament to the power of the human spirit, a reminder that with dedication, perseverance, and a willingness to push beyond our limits, we can achieve greatness, no matter what challenges we may face. And his mantra, “Ready to Work, Ready to be Tired,” would live on, inspiring generations to come, a powerful reminder of the importance of hard work, determination, and the unyielding spirit that drives us to achieve our dreams.

title.rendered: Hardworking Leader Cum Back-Looking Followers

content.rendered:
When a hardworking leader is paired with followers who are backward-looking, it can create a challenging dynamic. The leader’s drive for progress and innovation may be met with resistance from followers who prefer to maintain the status quo. This resistance can hinder the implementation of new ideas and approaches, making it difficult for the leader to achieve their goals.

Furthermore, the lack of motivation among followers can be a significant obstacle for the hardworking leader. If followers are not inspired to work towards a common goal, the leader may struggle to motivate them to achieve more. The leader’s focus on progress and improvement may clash with the followers’ priorities, leading to conflicts and misunderstandings.
The difficulty in implementing the leader’s plans and initiatives can also be a major challenge. If followers are not willing to adapt or change their ways of working, it can be hard for the leader to drive progress and achieve their objectives.
To overcome these challenges, the leader needs to communicate effectively with their followers. By clearly explaining the vision, goals, and benefits of change, the leader can help followers understand the rationale behind new initiatives. Building trust is also crucial, and the leader can achieve this by demonstrating empathy, transparency, and fairness in decision-making.
Empowering followers to take ownership of specific tasks or projects can also be an effective strategy. By involving them in the decision-making process, the leader can encourage followers to take a more active role in driving progress. Leading by example is also essential, as the leader’s behaviour and work ethic can inspire and motivate followers to achieve more.
By adopting these strategies, the hardworking leader can bridge the gap between their own work ethic and the followers’ more traditional approach. Ultimately, this can help to drive progress and achieve shared goals, leading to a more successful and productive team.
The SixthSense says “Experience is the best teacher”

title.rendered: The Tale of Two Warriors: Stubbornness and Courage

content.rendered:
In a land of ancient wisdom called Orunto, two warriors, Stubbornness and Courage, roamed the realm. Both were known for their strength and conviction, but their paths diverged like two distinct rivers.
Stubbornness was like a boulder, unmoving and unyielding. He would resist change and cling to his views, even when faced with overwhelming evidence to the contrary. Stubbornness was driven by a desire to prove himself right, rather than seeking truth or wisdom.
Courage, on the other hand, was like a lion, fearless and noble. She would stand tall in the face of adversity, driven by a sense of justice and conviction. Courage was not afraid to challenge the status quo, but she was also willing to listen and learn from others.
One day, a young apprentice approached Stubbornness and asked for his guidance. Stubbornness replied, “I’ve made up my mind, and I won’t budge. You’re either with me or against me.” The apprentice felt intimidated and frustrated, realizing that Stubbornness was not open to reason or alternative perspectives.
Meanwhile, another apprentice approached Courage and asked for her counsel. Courage replied, “I’m willing to take a stand, but I’m also open to hearing your thoughts and considering different perspectives. Let’s explore this together and find a path forward.” The apprentice felt inspired and empowered, recognising that Courage was driven by a desire to do what was right, rather than simply proving a point.
A wise elder, Baalufe observed the two warriors and their approaches. Baalufe explained, “Stubbornness is like a wall, built to protect one’s own views and interests. Courage is like a bridge, connecting people and ideas, and fostering growth and understanding. Stubbornness is driven by ego and pride, while courage is driven by conviction and a sense of justice.”
The apprentices nodded, beginning to understand the difference. Stubbornness was about resisting change and clinging to one’s own views, while courage was about standing up for what was right, even in the face of adversity. Stubbornness was like a rigid tree, unyielding and inflexible, while courage was like a flexible reed, bending but not breaking.
As the apprentices continued their journey, they learned to appreciate the value of courage in standing up for what was right, while avoiding the pitfalls of stubbornness. They recognised that courage was not about being inflexible, but about being principled and open to growth and learning. And they lived their lives with a deeper understanding of the difference between stubbornness and courage.
The tale of the two warriors spread throughout the land, reminding people that true courage is not about being rigid or unyielding, but about standing up for what is right, while remaining open to growth, learning, and the perspectives of others.

title.rendered: The Tale of Two Travellers: Lies and Untruths

content.rendered:
In a vast desert, two travelers, Lies and Untruths, journeyed through the dunes of deception. Both seemed to lead people astray, but their paths diverged like two distinct oases.
Lies was a cunning guide, intentionally misleading others for personal gain or malice. He would fabricate stories and present them as facts, knowing full well that they were false. Lies would manipulate and deceive, causing harm to those who trusted him.
Untruths, on the other hand, was a misguided traveller, often spreading false information without realising it. He might believe something to be true, only to discover later that it was not. Untruths would share his misconceptions, not out of malice, but out of ignorance or misunderstanding.
One day, a young traveller approached Lies and asked for directions to a nearby city. Lies pointed him in the wrong direction, laughing to himself as the traveller wandered further into the desert. The young traveller became lost and frustrated, realising too late that he had been deceived.
Meanwhile, another traveller approached Untruths and asked for information about the same city. Untruths shared what he thought was true, but it turned out to be an untruth. The traveller was misinformed, but Untruths apologised and corrected his mistake as soon as he realised the error.
A wise elder observed the two travellers and their interactions. He explained to the young travellers that Lies and Untruths were distinct, despite both leading people astray. “Lies are like a mirage created by a deceitful mind,” he said. “They are intentional and malicious, designed to manipulate and harm. Untruths, on the other hand, are like a mistaken map. They may lead people astray, but they are not necessarily malicious.”
The travellers nodded, beginning to understand the difference. Lies were about intentional deception, while untruths were about unintentional mistakes. Lies were a breach of trust, while untruths were an opportunity for correction and growth.
As the travellers continued their journey, they learned to discern between Lies and Untruths. They approached information with a critical eye, verifying facts and sources to avoid being misled. And they treated others with empathy, recognising that untruths can be corrected, while lies require vigilance and discernment.
The tale of the two travelers spread throughout the land, reminding people of the importance of critical thinking and empathy. And the travelers learned to navigate the complex landscape of truth and deception, guided by wisdom and discernment.

title.rendered: The Egbas Are Arguably The Most Civilized Tribe In Nigeria

content.rendered:
Abeokuta was a sovereign nation for 20 years and 11 months before the British amalgamated her with the rest of Nigeria. She had her own laws, Police Force, Civil Service and was well organized. The Alake was the head of the defunct government known as the Egba United Government (1 February 1893- 1 January 1914). The amalgamation with the rest of Nigeria did not go down well with the Egba people and this resulted in the Adubi War (1918). I have compiled some facts about this ancient and paramount city that seats as the capital of Ogun State and also the pride of Egbaland.
Abeokuta was founded in 1830, with Sodeke as her leader. The initial name of Abeokuta was “Oko Adagba” meaning “Adagba’s farmstead”-Adagba was an Itoko farmer. Sodeke who led the Egbas met him there.
Abeokuta means ‘under a rock’, signifying the protection which the Olumo Rock offered the Egbas during attacks.
Since the discovery of Olumo Rock, no one has fallen from it. Not even once.
Eastern side of the Olumo Rock in Ikija, Abeokuta.
The first church in Nigeria, St. Peter’s Anglican Church, is in Abeokuta.
The first Baptist Church in West Africa and the first local government in Nigeria (Abeokuta South) are in Abeokuta.
The first University in Nigeria should have been located in Abeokuta but due to infighting, it was established at Ibadan as the University of Ibadan in 1948.
The first secondary school in Nigeria was sited in Abeokuta before it was relocated to Lagos as CMS Grammar School due to unknown reasons.
The first hospital in Nigeria, Sacred Heart Hospital, is in Abeokuta. It is still functioning.
The first bridge in Nigeria (Sokori Bridge-1903) built by a Nigerian (Mr. John Adenekan) without European supervision is in Abeokuta.
The first Newspaper in Nigeria (Iwe Iroyin) was founded in Abeokuta in 1859.
The first president of the Nigeria Union of Teachers and the first woman to drive a car was from Abeokuta. They both married each other. They were also the first male and female admitted to Abeokuta Grammar School.
The first indigenous Chief Justice of Nigeria (Justice Adetokunbo Ademola) was from Abeokuta. He was the son of the longest reigning monarch (Alake) in Egbaland.
Okukenu Sagbua I, was the first Alake of Egbaland. He was enthroned on August 8, 1854. His descendant, Okukenu Sagbua IV is the current Alake of Egbaland.
Alake Gbadebo I, was the first monarch in Nigeria to visit England on a state visit.
He spent 20 days at sea-May 5-25, 1904.
The first time a white man came to Abeokuta on January 4, 1843, everybody (both young and old) left their homes and market places to catch a glimpse of Henry Townsend, the white man.
During the American Civil War (1861-1865) which interrupted the U.S cotton trade to Europe, Abeokuta exported cotton to England.
The most influential woman in the history of Egbaland and the first Iyalode of Egbaland was Madam Tinubu. Tinubu square in Lagos and Ita Iyalode in Abeokuta are named after her. She died in 1887.
In 1893, the Egba United Government was recognized as an independent nation by Britain. She had her own laws. Many developments were made until 1914, when she was amalgamated to form Nigeria. The Sokori Bridge was constructed in 1903 and Abeokuta Grammar School was founded on July 16, 1908.
Abeokuta has produced many outstanding persons in the nation: In Academics (Reverend Israel Oludotun Ransome-Kuti, Professor Saburi Biobaku), In Accountancy (Akintola Williams, Folorunso Oke, Bola Kuforiji-Olubi), In Law (Justice Adetokunbo Ademola – first indigenous Chief Justice of Nigeria, Olumuyiwa Jibowu, George Sodehinde Sowemimo, S. O. Lambo, Chief F.R.A. Williams, Prince Bola Ajibola), In Medicine (Moses Majekodunmi, Professor Thomas Lambo, Koye Ransome – Kuti)), In Military (Olusegun Obasanjo, Oluwole Rotimi, Enitan Ransome-Kuti), In Civil Service (Simeon Adebo), In Literature (Ajisafe, J.F Odunjo, Amos Tutuola, Wole Soyinka – of Egba mother), In Music (Josiah J. Ransome-Kuti, Fela Ransome-Kuti, Yusuf Olatunji, Femi Ransome-Kuti, Seun Kuti, Fela Sowande, Ebenezer Obey, Sina Peters, Adeola Akinsanya, Prince Adekunle, Ayinla Omowura and Sefiu Alao, among others. In Journalism (Olusegun Osoba, Reuben Abati), In Women Rights and Entrepreneurship (Iyalode Tinubu, Eniola Soyinka, Elizabeth Adekogbe, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti and Iyalode Bisoye Tejuoso and Simbiat Abiola. In Politics (Olusegun Obasanjo, Ernest Adegunle Sonekan, M.K.O. Abiola, Moses Majekodunmi, Dimeji Bankole, Ayotunde Rosiji, Olusegun Osoba, Ibikunle Amosun) and others countless to mention.
In 1925, Josiah Jesse Ransome-Kuti (1855-1930) Fela’s grandfather, became the first Nigerian to release a record album after he recorded several Yoruba language hymns in gramophone through Zonophone Records.
The most enlightened clan among the Yoruba tribe are the Egbas. Her chiefs had been interacting with the Queen of England as far back as 1868 which continued till a century later. English and Egba monarchs did exchange gifts.
The First South Westerners ever to rule Nigeria are from Abeokuta (Olusegun Obasanjo and Ernest Shonekan).
It is widely believed that Egba women are more independent than any other Yoruba tribe in the country e.g Eniola Soyinka, Elizabeth Adekogbe and Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti.
Popular Egba Song:
Egba ile, ibe ni ‘gbagbo ti bere;
Egba ile, ibe l’olaju ti bere;
Omo Egba won m’aye je.;
Baba mi se die loro mi emi l’omo Lakesin.
Bo ni male ma wi ni mosalasi, won a ni ka ma ro’ko;
Bo ni ‘gbagbo ma wi ni Soosi, won a ni ka ma s’agbe.
Eni yo s’ore agbe, a jinyan koko, a senu kabata;
Ewele wekun ewele,
A ko ma f’oju sunkun ara wa;
E e wele wekun e wele.
PROUDLY EGBA INDIGENE.
COMRADE EBENEZER ADEBAYO AYOADE.

She had her own laws, Police Force, Civil Service and was well organized. The Alake was the head of the defunct government known as the Egba United Government (1 February 1893- 1 January 1914).

title.rendered: Hon Chief Olugbolahan Bamidele Oketade Ijaola Onroko Erunmu, Owu, Abeokuta

content.rendered:
Died 2nd August, 2017
My Encounter with Onroko Ijaola…
Chief Onroko Ijaola worked with the Nigeria Railways from 1953 at Ebute Metta, Lagos State, and retired as a Deputy Secretary on October 2, 1978. I often told him, “You’re one of the remaining brigade of truth, trusted, upright, and forthright – a library of Owu history and a rare breed of incorruptible elders.”
Onroko Ijaola represented the Lagos North East Constituency at the National Assembly from 1979-83 under the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN). He was a close associate of Chief Obafemi Awolowo and Chief Lateef Jakande. I discovered his philosophies and straightforwardness many years ago in the Owu Community of Abeokuta. Though he held tough stances, he was a respected figure.
Born on September 28, 1933, at Kano, Nigeria, Onroko claimed to have been born at 2:10 am. His father, a Senior Station Master at Ido, Lagos State, played a significant role in shaping his lineage and traditional title. Onroko was installed as the 8th Olu Aroko on September 30, 2000, and tenaciously protected the traditional stool until his passing.

One of his notable proverbs, “Olotito ki leni sugbon won ki o ku si apo ika,” translates to “The truth will always prevail no matter the circumstances.” I personally learned a lot from Onroko tiwa, a family man with many children. Adieu Onroko tiwa! Goodnight…
Emi ni tiyin nitoto,
Oloye Abiodun Lasile
Orunto Baalufe Owu Kingdom Abeokuta.

title.rendered: Volunteering: An Act of Giving

content.rendered:
The SixthSense Initiative is calling for volunteers to support their SixthSense Summer Children Reading Camp (SCRC) in Abeokuta, Ogun State. This annual event, now in its 8th edition, aims to promote reading culture, critical thinking, and moral grooming in children aged 8-15.

VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITIES:
– Facilitators: Guide children through interactive reading sessions, peer reviews, and book discussions
– Mentorship: Provide guidance and support to children during the camp
– Administrative Support: Assist with camp organization, registration, and logistics
CAMP DETAILS:
– Date: August 3-9, 2025
– Location: WOOTEN Hall, Baptist Girls College, Idi-Aba, Abeokuta, Ogun State.
– Expected Participants: Over 100 children
BENEFITS OF VOLUNTEERING:
– Gain valuable experience in teaching, mentoring, or administrative support
– Contribute to the development of young minds and promote reading culture
– Network with like-minded individuals and organiations
HOW TO GET INVOLVED:
– Contact: +234 803 717 1759, +234 802 719 1291
– Email: mails@sixthsenseinitiatives.org.ng

By volunteering, you’ll play a significant role in shaping the next generation of thinkers, leaders, and nation-builders. Join the SixthSense Initiative in promoting reading culture and empowering young Nigerians.
-Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative and Sixth Sense Series Publications.

title.rendered: SixthSense SmartWords…Leadership

content.rendered:
The sanctity of strong leadership and guidance stands as an immutable cornerstone of human endeavour, a luminous beacon illuminating the path to triumph and transcendence. The majestic metaphor of a ‘superior head’, graced by a ‘good pilot’ of unwavering sagacity and adorned with ‘sterling decision’ of unshakeable resolve, bespeaks an ardent yearning for wise and capable direction, a quest for illumination amidst the labyrinthine complexities of existence. This exalted approach, suffused with the essence of visionary leadership, shall prove beneficent across the vast tapestry of human experience, manifesting its virtues in the realms of:
– Leadership: wherein a strong and visionary leader, endowed with clairvoyant insight and sound decision-making acumen, shall inspire and guide the multitudes towards the radiant pinnacle of success.
– Personal Growth: wherein the seeker of wisdom shall find solace and guidance beneath the nurturing wings of mentors and role models, those luminous paragons of expertise and sagacity who shall illuminate the path to self-mastery and informed decision-making.
– Teamwork: wherein the synergy of collaborative endeavor, guided by a skilled and trustworthy ‘pilot’ of unwavering expertise, shall navigate the treacherous straits of complexity and emerge triumphant, achieving shared goals and celestial aspirations.
By surrendering to the sublime guidance of a ‘superior head’, blessed with a ‘good pilot’ of discerning wisdom and ‘sterling decision’ of unshakeable integrity, the aspirant shall unlock the gates of celestial success, bathing their existence in the aureate radiance of stability and triumph.
Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Founder/Coordinator, The SixthSense Initiative.

title.rendered: Cultural Participation as a Phenomenon

content.rendered:
Cultural participation is a vibrant and multifaceted phenomenon that encompasses the diverse ways individuals engage with and contribute to the rich tapestry of cultural activities. It is an expression of human creativity, diversity, and connection, manifesting in various forms that cater to different interests, passions, and communities.

At its core, cultural participation involves individuals immersing themselves in creative activities that allow them to express their unique perspectives and talents. This can take the form of art, music, writing, or other creative pursuits that bring joy, fulfillment, and a sense of accomplishment. By engaging in these activities, individuals not only cultivate their skills but also contribute to the cultural landscape, enriching it with their distinctive voices and visions.
Beyond personal creative endeavors, cultural participation also involves engaging with broader cultural events and practices. This can include attending concerts, festivals, theater performances, or visiting museums and heritage sites, where individuals can experience the richness of cultural heritage and connect with others who share similar interests. Online platforms have also emerged as vital spaces for cultural participation, enabling individuals to access, create, and share cultural content with a global audience.
Community involvement is another crucial aspect of cultural participation, where individuals engage in local cultural practices, traditions, and events that foster a sense of belonging and social connection. This can range from participating in traditional festivals to contributing to community arts projects, each offering opportunities for individuals to bond over shared cultural experiences and values.
Cultural participation can manifest in different ways, from passive consumption of cultural products like movies and music to active creation of cultural content through writing, painting, or playing music. It can also involve participatory culture, where individuals collaborate on cultural projects, share ideas, and build communities around shared interests.
The benefits of cultural participation are profound and far-reaching. By engaging with diverse cultures and perspectives, individuals can foster greater tolerance and trust, breaking down barriers and building bridges between communities. Cultural participation can also play a pivotal role in building inclusive societies, promoting social cohesion, and empowering individuals with a sense of purpose and fulfillment. Ultimately, cultural participation is a powerful tool for personal growth, community development, and social transformation, offering a platform for individuals to express themselves, connect with others, and contribute to the vibrant tapestry of human culture.

title.rendered: Osinbajo, Abiodun, Sanwo-Olu, Dangote, Osoba, Others Bid Awujale Farewell

content.rendered:
The late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona, who died on Sunday, July 13, 2025, has been laid to rest with the Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun describing him as a pride of Ijebuland, Ogun State and Nigeria as a whole.
Oba Adetona was crowned as the Awujale of Ijebuland in 1960 and was the longest reigning monarch in the country.
Speaking after the monarch was committed to mother earth at Ogbagba Court, Igbeba, Ijebu-Ode, the governor noted the enormous development Oba Adetona brought to Ijebuland in his 65 years on the throne, saying he was an enduring candour of dignity of the Ijebu ancestral heritage.
As a lover of education, according to the governor, the late monarch pioneered the institution of a professorial Chair on good governance and the upgrading of the Oba (Dr) Sikiru Kayode Adetona School of Governance Studies, Olabisi Onabanjo University into a full fledged campus of the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, Kuru.
He said: “This historic achievement not only honours the vision of Kabiyesi, but also positions Ogun State as a centre of policy innovation and elite public service training in Nigeria and across Sub-Saharan Africa.
“Baba’s commitment to human development was unmatched. He championed the Ijebu Development Board on Poverty and Education, and he was Chairman.”
According to Governor Abiodun, Oba Adetona was a philanthropist of immeasurable proportions, a generous giver, and a mentor to many people.
“Baba was a phenomenon, a monarch like no other. He betroyed colossus. His reign was not only defined by his longevity but by his towering influence, deep wisdom, enduring legacy of integrity, generosity, selflessness, progress and peace.

“Kabiyesi was a bundle of intellect, he was principled, he was forthright, he was courageous, he was a philosopher, a transparent and incorruptible monarch, equitable in judgement and deeply committed to the Nigerian state,” he said.
The governor, while noting that the late Awujale lived a fulfilled life, acknowledged the contribution of the late monarch to the successful passage of the laws governing traditional councils and monarchs in the state.
“The bill sought to review the laws governing traditional councils and monarchs in the state.
“This bill was passed into laws and that legislation now gives traditional rulers the freedom to be buried according to their wishes, not only was it passed into law, I signed that bill in Kabiyesi’s palace.
“His life was a rich tapestry of impact in tradition, national discourse, education, philanthropy and social harmony, a true champion, a remarkable conqueror, an exemplary servant of the people.
“Today, we salute this legend, this giant of history and enduring symbol of Ijebuland.  I felt it was a fitting tribute to a monarch who refined tradition,” he added.
He appreciated President Bola Tinubu for conferring on the monarch the prestigious national honour of the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON) noting that it is a testimony of the Awujale’s  contributions to national development.
Former governor of the state, Chief Olusegun Osoba, in his remarks, said the late Awujale was active and lively till the point of death, saying he must be proud for having his wish come to pass.
The President of Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote, said living up to 91 years was no mean achievements and revealed his level of closeness with the late monarch.
The event was attended by former Vice President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, the Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Alhaji Gboyega Oyetola, Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Mr. Bosun Tijani, former governors Gbenga Daniel, Ibikunle Amosun, James Ibori, among other dignitaries.

content.rendered:
The Olubadan throne boasts a distinctive succession system, marked by structure and predictability, facilitating smooth transitions of power. What sets it apart from many Nigerian traditional rulerships is its well-defined hierarchical framework, comprising two ruling lines: the Otun Olubadan (civil) and Balogun (military). Chiefs progress through ranks within these lines, ultimately reaching the esteemed positions of Otun Olubadan or Balogun of Ibadanland, thereby becoming eligible for the Olubadan throne.
The current Otun Olubadan, High Chief Rasidi Adewolu Ladoja, is the next in line from the civil line following Oba Olakulehin’s reign. This system, rooted in Ibadan’s history, minimises disputes and ensures that the most senior chief ascends the throne.
Forty-Three Olubadans have ruled the ancient city of Ibadan since Yoruba took over the territory in 1820.
1. (One year): Lagelu – 1820
2. (Six years): Baale Maye Okunade – 1820-1826
3. (Four years): Baale Oluyendun Labosinde – 1826-1830
4. (Five years): Baale Lakanle – 1830-1835
5. (15 Years): Basorun Oluyole Ojaba – 1835-1850
6. (One year): Baale Oderinlo Opeagbe Idiomo/Kure – 1850-1851
7. (13 Years): Baale Oyesile Olugbode Ita Baale – 1851-1864
8. (One year): Ba’ale Ibikunle – 1864-1865
9. (Two Years): Basorun Ogumola Mapo – 1865-1867
10. (Three Years): Balogun Beyioku Akere Onitamperin – 1867-1870
11. (One year): Baale Orowusi (Awarun) Kobomoje – 1870-1871
12. (14 Years): Aare Oadoke Latoosa Oke-Are – 1871-1885
13. (Eight Years): Balogun Ajayi Osungbekun Kobmoje  – 1885-1893
14. (Two Years): Baate Fijabi 1 (Omo Babalola) Oritamerin – 1893-1895
15. (Two Years): Baale Osuntoki Olusun Agbeni – 1895-1897
16. (Five Years): Badorun Fajimi (Yerombi) Oranyan – 1897-1902
17. (Two Years): Baale Mosaderin Sunlehinmi Oranyan – 1902-1904
18. (Three Years): Baale Dada Opadare Mapo – 1904-1907
19. (Three Years): Basorun Sumonu Apanpa Isale-Osi – 1907-1910
20.  (Two Years): Baale Akintayo Awanibaku Elenpe Bere, Aboke – 1910-1912
21. (Two Years): Baale Irefin (Omo Ogundeyi) Oke Ofa Babasale – 1912-1914
22. (11 Years): Baale Shitu (Omo Are Latosa) Oke Are 1914-1925   11
23. (Five Years): Baale Oyewole Aiyejenku Omo Foko Oke Foko – 1925-1930
24. (16 Years): Olubadan Okunola Abaasi Alesinloye Isale Ijebu – 1930-1946
25.  (Three Months): Olubadan Fagbinrin Akere II Oritamerin – 1946-1946
26. (Eight Months): Olubadan Oyetunde I Eleta – 1946-1946
27. (One year): Olubadan Akintunde Bioku Oleyo, Oranyan – 1947-1948
28. (Four Years): Olubadan Fijabi II Oritamerin – 1948-1952
29. (Four Months): Olubadan Memudu Alli Iwo Gbenla – 1952- 1952
30. (Three Months): Olubadan Igbintade Apete Oke Ofa – 1952-1955
31. (Nine Years): Oba Isaac Babalola Akinyele Alafara – 1955-1964
32. (Two Months): Oba Yesufu Kobiowu Oranyan – 1964-1964
33. (Six Years): Oba Salawu Akanbi Aminu Adeoyo – 1965-1971
34. (Five Years): Oba Shittu Akintola Oyetunde II Eleta – 1971- 1976
35. (One year): Oba Gbadamosi Akanbi Adebimpe Odinjo – 1976- 1977
36. (Five Years): Oba Daniel Tayo Akinbiyi Elekuro  – 1977-1982
37. (10 Years): Oba Yesufu Oloyede Asanike IdiAro – 1983- 1993
38. (Six Years): Oba Emmanuel Adegboyega Operinde Isale Ijebu – 1993-1999
39. (Eight Years): Oba Yinusa B. Ogundipe Arapasowu I Oranyan – 1999-2007
40. (Nine Years): Oba Samuel Odulana Olugade I- 2007–2016
41. (Six Years): Oba Saliu Akanmu Adetunji – 2016–2022
42. (Two Years): Oba Lekan Balogun – 2022–2024.
43. Oba Owolabi Olalere Olakulehin- 12 July 2024 – 7 July 2025.

title.rendered: Dipo Sodipo: The Maestro

content.rendered:
Dipo Sodipo, affectionately known by his stage name “Pope,” was a renowned Nigerian highlife musician, band leader, and entertainer, widely celebrated as the “Czar of the One Man Band” during the late 1980s and 1990s. His unique voice, commanding stage presence, and dynamic musical style made him a beloved figure within the Yoruba music scene and beyond.

Early Life and Background
Born in 1954 into the respected Sodipo family of the Igbein Ancestral Route in Abeokuta, Ogun State, Dipo Sodipo was raised in a culturally rich environment that shaped his love for music and performance from a young age. His deep-rooted heritage and exposure to Yoruba traditions would later influence his musical journey and artistic expression.
Musical Career and Style
Dipo Sodipo first rose to prominence as the lead singer of K12 Voices, a band that blended traditional Yoruba rhythms with highlife melodies. His baritone voice, laced with charisma and stage wit, quickly distinguished him in a crowded music scene.
He later forged his path as a solo artist, becoming a pioneer of the “One Man Band” style—a form of live performance where a single musician uses electronic instruments to create the sound of a full band. His innovation and mastery in this space earned him the title of “Czar of the One Man Band.”
His musical style was a fusion of highlife, Fuji, and Yoruba traditional music, performed with humor, social commentary, and deep cultural flair. He was admired for his ability to connect with audiences across generations, delivering music that was both entertaining and reflective of Nigerian society.
Influence and Recognition
Because of his pioneering work and leadership within the performance community, Dipo Sodipo was appointed President of the One Man Band Association, where he mentored younger musicians and helped shape the standards of live performance within the genre.
He was known not only for his musical talent but also for his jovial personality, humility, and lively spirit. His friendliness and down-to-earth nature earned him respect from fellow musicians and fans alike.
Legacy
Though no longer active on the music scene, Dipo Sodipo’s contributions remain significant in the history of Yoruba and Nigerian live music. His innovative work with the One Man Band format paved the way for a new era of live performance in Nigeria, influencing many who followed his lead.
Today, he is remembered as a trailblazer in highlife music, a vocal powerhouse, and a cultural figure whose creativity and leadership helped shape modern Yoruba musical expression.

title.rendered: My Vision for Value of Life in Our Nation

content.rendered:
In my country, Nigeria, I envision a society where life is cherished and respected, free from the shackles of neglect and disregard. Every individual deserves to live with dignity, unencumbered by limitations and excesses that stifle their potential. The inherent value of life should be recognised and protected, from the highest echelons of power to the humblest of homes.
This value of life encompasses decency, respect, and protection. It’s about creating an environment where the mentally ill are cared for, not left to wander the streets, and where human life is shielded from shame and indignity. It’s about ensuring that the deceased are treated with reverence, not left exposed on roadsides or decaying in waterways.
My dream for our nation includes:
– Well-maintained infrastructure, free from potholes and hazards that claim lives
– Safe roads, where accidents are minimized through genuine construction and maintenance
– Quality healthcare that prolongs life, with accessible hospital services and a ban on fake drugs
– Immediate medical facilities that provide timely care and attention
– Eradicate corruption that drains public resources and infringes on citizens’ rights.
In this envisioned society, life is valued, respected, and protected. Every individual has the opportunity to thrive, and our collective humanity is reflected in the way we care for one another. This is my dream for the value of life in our nation – a dream of dignity, decency, and compassion that guides our actions and decisions.

title.rendered: An Open Conscience to Man

content.rendered:
“With humility, I pour my heart into teaching one, that many may benefit, and in selflessness, I surrender personal accolades for the greater good.” -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Sometimes, protecting our collective humanity requires sacrificing personal advantages or positions to impart valuable lessons and accord others the dignity they deserve. True self-worth often emerges from self-denial, ultimately uplifting humanity. Not everyone can relinquish privilege to make a point, but those who do can teach profound lessons.
My SixthSense discovery reveals that self-denial can foster long-term self-esteem, particularly when lessons are learned and applied. This approach may be necessary to convey hard truths, even after repeated warnings. The adage “No pain, no gain” resonates here – someone must often pay the price for others to reap the benefits.
We must acknowledge and respect the sacrifices made by individuals who contribute to the greater good. While personal understanding is crucial, there’s also a need for recognition and protocol. Even small acts of sacrifice can have a significant impact, and it’s often the seemingly insignificant ones that can teach the greatest lessons.
Let’s honour our capacity for selflessness and recognise that even the few, the insignificant few, can make a profound difference of sacrifice.
After all, great achievers often do!

title.rendered: Tribute to Prince Bola Ajibola by Demola Oladosu

content.rendered:
I celebrate and pay glowing tributes, to a distinguished personality, foremost legal luminary, renowned Minister of Justice and one time judge at the international court of justice, Hague, Omooba Bola Ajibola, the founder of the popular Crescent University.

The tributes to the sweet memories of this legend, with enduring and enviable legacies is to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Crescent University.
Before the university, the great crown prince had established an institution to foster the teaching of Islam and Arabic, with a view to promoting understanding, tolerance and accommodation, for peaceful coexistence.
20 years ago, I was privileged to host Baba, on an NTA Abeokuta programme, ” Frankly Speaking”. It was quite stimulating, exciting and unforgettable.
He disclosed how the land, on which the university was built, was acquired manually many decades ago. He vouched to give all it would take to establish the university. In his words;
“If it means selling my underwears”. It was a strong determination, commitment and selfless sacrifice.
Today the citadel of learning is contributing to the development of Human resources and the nation.
A great humanist and philanthropist, Omooba Bola Ajibola also donated a multimillion naira trauma centre to the Federal Medical Centre, Abeokuta.
I celebrate the Crescent University at 20.
May Allah SWT continue to grant him Aljaana Firdaus.
Omooba Bola Ajibola was a rare breed.

title.rendered: Preparing for ‘Night of Tributes’ for late ‘Chairman’ Chukwu!

content.rendered:
Earlier today, I visited the Wall of Fame at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs, NIIA, Lagos.
The National monument is still looking as  beautiful as when it was erected two years ago for everlasting remembrance and recognition of the historic contribution of some forgotten sports heroes to Nigeria’s Sports Diplomacy.
Amongst the names written permanently on the marbled wall are those of the ‘Chairman’, Christian Chukwu, MFR, and Charles Bassey, MON, two members of Nigeria’s 1980 African Cup of Nations’ winning squad. Both of them  died a few hours apart, on the same day, a few weeks ago.
The body of Christian Chukwu, a former Captain and Coach of the national team of Nigeria, will be laid to rest in Enugu State on August 16, 2025.
That of Charles Bassey will be buried on August 9, 2025, in Akwa Ibom State.
Whilst details of both funerals will soon be made public, Special Organising committees have been set up by the respective families and State Governments of the two heroes to handle the arrangements for their funerals.
Those desirous to play a part in the arrangements, or want to support the families in any way to make the events befitting, should please do so. They need all the support the public can render NOW.
I shall publish the names and contact details of the persons that can be reached for that purpose, soon.
Meanwhile, I am also heading a small independent committee in Lagos, to organise a ‘Night of Tributes’ for friends and fans of Christian Chukwu that may not be able to attend the funeral in Enugu, but wish to be a part of the national event in Lagos.
The event of songs and tributes will take place by the famous wall at the NIIA, Victoria Island Lagos, in the evening of July 28th, 2025, the second anniversary of the decoration of the heroes as AirPeace Ambassadors.
Any individuals or groups interested in being a part of this small but special evening, in any way, can contact me through this platform, or directly, privately. Every contribution shall be acknowledged properly.
Meanwhile, I invite all to enjoy this short clip of the AirPeace-sponsored ‘NIIA Sports Diplomacy Wall of Fame’ waiting to receive family, fans and friends of ‘the Chairman’ in Lagos, soon.

title.rendered: The Obas Have No Right Or Legal Right To Change The Tradition They Have Voluntarily Come Into – Judge

content.rendered:
According to Punch, Justice Phillips Akinside of the Ogun State High Court has firmly stated that traditional rulers must accept the burial rites and customs of the institutions they voluntarily joined, arguing that once a person becomes an Oba through cultural processes, they relinquish the right to reject those traditions — even after death.
He said; “The Obas have no right or legal right to change the tradition they have voluntarily come into.”
The judge made this assertion on Wednesday while delivering the keynote address at the fifth Chief Kehinde Sofola Memorial Bar Lecture, organised by the Nigerian Bar Association, Sagamu branch. He explained that the same customs which guide the selection, nomination, and installation of an Oba should equally apply to their burial.
According to him, “One cannot become a traditional ruler in accordance with the customs of the land and later reject those same customs. Religious freedom exists under the 1999 Constitution, but once an individual chooses to enter a traditional institution, they cannot claim an infringement of that freedom when the rites of that institution apply.”
Justice Akinside argued that accepting the role of an Oba is a voluntary act, and by doing so, the individual implicitly agrees to uphold and be governed by the associated traditions, including burial rituals. He likened rejecting those customs later to attempting to “change the goalpost in the middle of the match.”
He also addressed the growing controversy surrounding coronet obas, noting that while the executive council may upgrade Bales or appoint chiefs as coronet obas, these minor chiefs lack prescribed authority and therefore do not possess the power to install other chiefs within their domains.
Meanwhile, the Chief Judge of Ogun State, Justice Mosunmola Dipeolu, represented by Justice Adetokunbo Jibodu, used the occasion to urge legal practitioners to always uphold the rule of law and prioritise fundamental human rights over rigid traditional practices.
She praised the lecture’s theme—“Obas and Chiefs Law of Ogun State: Chieftaincy Disputes, Their Effects on the Community and Legal Protection of Religious Freedom”—as timely and essential, given the delicate balance between preserving cultural identity and safeguarding individual liberty.
From Opera News
June 27, 2025.
