title.rendered: Poem: Wedding Party on Sokori River

content.rendered:
Chieftaincy installations are familiar sights,
But Orunto Baalufe’s of Owu kingdom stands out in might.
Its uniqueness leaves one in awe and wonder.
On Sokori River’s banks, you and your sweetheart hosted,
Two thousand guests, a grand and joyous crowd.
I salute you, excluding the countless unseen spirits,
Of notable Sokori River, in Ogun’s historical land.
Guests savored delicacies, ate till they were full,
Enjoyed varied drinks to complement the feast’s thrill.
Abbey and Gbem’s joy was contagious and lasting,
Their happiness echoed long after the celebration.
Fuji maestro Alao performed boldly and loudly,
Malaika sang with passion, his voice soaring proudly.
The crowd danced with abandon, their legs moving freely,
It was a truly unforgettable day.
The grand finale unfolded,
Drinkables flowed, smokables swirled.
Night’s veil lifted, dawn’s embrace,
On Sokori River’s banks, your chieftaincy’s sacred space.
You celebrated through the night,
Drinking, laughing, till morning’s first light.
Sokori River’s tranquil flow,
Witnessed your joy, on your chieftaincy’s glow.

title.rendered: Excerpt…..Adieu Oba Olufemi Ogunleye

content.rendered:
One of the Respected Royal fathers in Owu Kingdom in person of Towulade of Akinale joined his ancestors recently in a London Hospital, would you like to talk about his life and legacies?
“On late Oba OLUFEMI Ogunleye Towulade of Akinale, an enigma of huge stature. I referred to his transition as a “library burnt” because he was a reservoir of repository knowledge, document and tradition. 
He rose from the bottom of self help to traditional leadership, correspondence education to formal education at old age of 70years and the feat of starting a different profession from journalism and public relations to law. He studied first degree, masters and almost completed a doctorate degree in law at 79years. 
He died with great knowledge apart from the ones he authored, wrote and presented. He was one personality that knew my forebearers and often reminded me of the huge value of Orunto institution in the Owu Kingdom. 
I can’t remember him enough at once; a journalist of repute, foremost public relation personality, prolific writer, educated historian and traditionalist. Owu Kingdom Abeokuta will not quickly forget him in the annals of our history in terms of customs and traditions.”

title.rendered: SixthSense SmartWords…. Tradition, Custom and Culture

content.rendered:
In the tapestry of human experience, tradition, custom, and culture are the interconnected threads that weave together to form the rich fabric of our heritage. Like a mighty river, heritage flows from the past, through the present, and into the future, carrying with it the collective memories, values, and experiences of our ancestors.
Tradition, the guardian of our collective memory, passes down beliefs, practices, and rituals from one generation to the next, preserving the wisdom of our forebears. Custom, the fabric of our daily lives, is the habitual practice that gives texture and depth to our social norms. Culture, the very essence of our being, encompasses the shared values, beliefs, arts, customs, and behaviors that define us as a people.
Heritage, the sum total of our shared history, values, and experiences, is the foundation upon which we build our identities, both individual and collective. It is the soil in which our roots grow deep, the wind that shapes our growth, and the sun that nourishes our souls.
As we navigate the complexities of our heritage, we come to realise that tradition, custom, and culture are not separate entities, but interconnected aspects of our shared human experience. Like a symphony, they harmonise to create a rich cultural heritage that is both our legacy and our destiny.
By embracing this profound understanding, we can deepen our appreciation for the traditions that shape us, the customs that bind us, and the culture that defines us. We can honour our heritage, not as a relic of the past, but as a living, breathing entity that informs our present and shapes our future. As I always say, ‘Heritage is the foundation upon which we build our identities, and tradition, custom, and culture are the pillars that hold it strong.’ May we cherish and honor this sacred legacy.
Hence, let’s foster innovation within tradition while safeguarding the essence of heritage values.

title.rendered: Kemta Adire Kampala Festival 2025

content.rendered:
The Kemta Adire Kampala Festival was held on Saturday, January 25th, 2025, at the historic market place in the heart of Abeokuta. This vibrant celebration honored the rich cultural heritage of Adire, a traditional textile art form that has gained international recognition.
Adire, which translates to “tie and die,” is more than just a technique – it’s a concept that showcases the creativity and skill of Egbaland’s native artisans. Using ordinary textile materials, these talented individuals have elevated Adire to a globally acclaimed art form, putting Egbaland on the world map.
The Kemta market, situated on a historic land with a rich history of trade and commerce, welcomes visitors from across the globe, including The Gambia, Senegal, Mali, and beyond. The festival also acknowledges the significant contribution of Osogbo town in Osun State to the evolution of Adire.
On behalf of His Royal Majesty, Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE Otileta VII Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, we extend our warmest congratulations to all stakeholders in the Adire value chain. This festival celebrates not only our rich cultural heritage but also the people and trade that have made Adire a beloved part of our identity.
Congratulations to all Adire enthusiasts and stakeholders!

title.rendered: Idea HK Locks Creativity

content.rendered:
“Creative minds thrill me because I admire their passion, dedication, and ability to bring new ideas to life. Be a creative element!” -Abiodun Lasile DL MnbR
Renowned artist HK Locks recently visited the historic Olowu Palace in Oke Ago Owu, Abeokuta, to showcase his exceptional talent. In an impressive display of skill, he recreated the likeness of HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE Otileta VII, the revered Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, Ogun State.
This mesmerizing live painting was completed within a cumulative 70 minutes, a testament to HK Locks’ mastery and creative genius. I am thoroughly fascinated by the innovative mind of an artist like HK Locks, who constantly push boundaries and inspire us with their unique perspectives.
Kudos to HK Locks for this remarkable achievements in the world of arts!
It was a live painting experience with a difference, an engagement with interaction and a royalty re-creation.
This is an engagement of time for our youths who are currently looking for ways to excel and make impart.

title.rendered: Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, Mourns the Passing of Akogun Chief Isola Akinsipo

content.rendered:
It is with deep sorrow that we announce the passing of our esteemed Chief Raobil Isola Akinsipo, the Akogun of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, at the age of 69 on Tuesday, October 15, 2024. In keeping with Islamic traditions, Chief Akinsipo was laid to rest the same day.
On behalf of Alayeluwa, Oba Prof. Saka Matemilola, Oluyalo Otileta VII, Olowu of Owu Kingdom, we extend our heartfelt tribute to Chief Akinsipo’s remarkable life and enduring legacy. As a distinguished leader, he embodied exceptional service and dedication to humanity.
Chief Akinsipo served the Owu Kingdom in various capacities, including as the Head of Iwarefa Owu. He was a seasoned broadcast practitioner, a Yoruba language specialist, an insurance consultant, and a traditionalist.
His unwavering commitment to service, profound wisdom, and significant contributions to the Owu Kingdom have left an irreplaceable void in our community.
We pray that his soul rests in perfect peace and that Chief Akinsipo’s legacy continues to inspire generations. May his memory be forever blessed.

title.rendered: Congratulations on Your Birthday and Happy New Month!

content.rendered:
Dear Orunto Abiodun Lasile,
 
It is with great delight that I write to celebrate your birthday and extend my warmest wishes for the new month. Today, as we mark another remarkable year of your life, we reflect on the invaluable contributions you continue to make to society through your leadership, vision, and selfless service.
 
Your work with the SixthSense Initiative has been a beacon of hope and transformation for many. As the Orunto of Owu Kingdom, your influence and dedication to the betterment of your community are inspiring. Your unwavering commitment to excellence is a testament to the strength of your character.
 
Allow me also to express my heartfelt gratitude for the immense support you extended throughout the outgone year. Your guidance, encouragement, and partnership have been invaluable, and I look forward to even greater collaboration in the days ahead.
 
May this new year bring you renewed strength, boundless blessings, and the fulfillment of all your aspirations. I pray that you continue to prosper in good health, wisdom, and peace as you lead and inspire.
 
Once again, happy birthday and happy new month! May 2025 be filled with remarkable achievements for you.
 
With warm regards,
Adejola Adeyemi Crown
Tropic Reporters

title.rendered: Surprise! Surprise!! Surprise!!!

content.rendered:
I am deeply humbled and grateful to have received an award of excellence from Methodist Primary Nursery School, Ago Oko, Abeokuta, in recognition of my selfless contributions. 
 
The surprise honour was bestowed upon me during a ceremony where I was initially invited as a guest. It serves as a reminder that even the smallest acts of kindness can make a significant impact. I am thankful for the acknowledgement and will continue to strive for positive change in my community.
 
Non Governmental Organisation Award of the Year.
 
The SixthSense Initiative is a registered nonprofit outfit hugely promoting children reading culture and human capacity development.

title.rendered: Adieu, Iya Oba!

content.rendered:
We give all thanks to God, the merciful and magnificent. The mother of our monarch slept in the Lord at 81years, after a brief illness.

We the Owu people all over the world condole HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola FNSE, Oluyalo Otileta VII Olowu of Owu Kingdom Abeokuta, on the transition to his dear mother, iya Oba and matriarch of Bolaji family.
Alhaja Aliratu Adunni Matemilola was born 1943 in Abiola Village, to Chief Kasali Bolaji Abiola of Ago-Ika, Gbágùrá in Abeokuta and Mrs Raliat Bolaji of Labuta Compound, Oke Egunya, Owu Abeokuta. Her father was Baale of Abiola village, Gbalefa, in current Ado Odo/Ota Local Government of Ogun State.
Her father Chief Kasali Bolaji, who was the third Baale of Abiola village, which was founded by his own father, Chief Abiola, shortly after the Ẹgba United Forces roundly defeated the Dahomey forces in the mid 1800s.
Throughout her life, Alhaja Matemilola was a shining example of kindness, compassion, and strength. As a successful trader, loving mother, and dutiful wife, she touched countless lives with her warmth and generosity. Her commitment to transparency and truthfulness inspired all who knew her.
She was survived by several children, grandchildren, great grandchildren, sister, brothers, in-laws and families.
We extend our deepest condolences to HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola and the entire Bolaji, and Matemilola families during this difficult time. May Allah grant Alhaja Matemilola’s soul eternal peace and admit her into Aljannah Firdaus. Aamiin.
Chief Dr Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile
Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta

title.rendered: Chief Simeon Isabade Lasile (Orunto Owu and Baala Egba)

content.rendered:
Chief  S. I. Lashile was born July 24, 1914 to Pa Saalu and Mama Amoke Lasile of Orunto village in Olorunda, Abeokuta North Local Government. The last born of four children by his mother, young Isabade left his illiterate farmer father to live with his most senior brother who was a very successful farmer, trader and produce merchant.  
At about the age of thirteen, Isabade met another village boy and inquired as to what the other boy was carrying on his head. The other boy explained that they are books, and from books one could learn to count objects and write down what one knows. With his imagination fired! Isabade went to ask his mother to appeal to his brother to allow him to go to schooll. Relunctantly his brother agreed, on the condition that Isabade would perform his farm duties upon return from school everyday.
From Baptist Day School in Olorunda, Isabade gained admission to the prestigious Baptist Boys High School in 1933, and led his class in academics for five years. He earned for himself the nickname “THE GREAT” for his outstanding performances in athletics and in football. He sculpted with ease and won laurels in various competitions during his school days  
After undergoing Teacher Training at Iwo, he came back to BBBS. As a Teacher, he rose to the position of Senior Boarding Housemaster. Among the notables who passed through his hands are Chief Bayo Kehinde (SAN) Chief Kehinde Sofola (SAN and former Attorney General of the Federation).  
In 1947, he married Late Mrs. Felicia Adejoke Abike Lasile, (nee Adewusi) of Igbore. The marriage produced seven children. Adegoke (deceased), Olabisi (deceased), Olatoyese (deceased). Tayelolu. Kehinde (deceased). Fumilola (deceased) and Tokunbo.  
Chief Lasile left BBHS and went to Ibadan to engage in produce buying and selling. He later joined the Cooperative Supply Association of the then Western Region and within a few years, Papa had distinguished himself so well that he was sent in 1957 to Loughborough College in Britain. When in 196/2 he was not given the position he felt he was entitled to, he quit CSA and joined the National Bank of Nigeria. Within eleven months of joining the bank as a clerk, he passed all the banking intermediate exams and became a manager. First at Grade Eleven branch and rose up to the Grade Two branch in Ibadan.
S.I., as he was later fondly called, left paid employment and went into food supply business in Ibadan till he retired in 1981. In 1970 he occupied his family stool as Orunto of Owu. The title of the kingmakers of Owu Kingdom. He bagged the title of Baala Egba in 1977.
In calling Chief Lasile the modern day “Baba Owu’ one can say without fear of contradiction from any quarters that Papa was sent by the Almighty God to hold together Owu Kingdom from disintegration by forces both from within and outside Owu. As the youngest and one of the very well educated kingmakers, he always stood by the truth and never allowed the rich and powerful in Owu to stray him from the path of righteousness. As the older kingmakers died one by one, Papa was kept alive by God and this prevented non-Owu people from getting the chance to act as Regent in Owu,  a situation which our distrators would have used to scatter us for good. No amount of cash inducement, no position could deter Papa from always telling the truth and standing firm. In an unprecedented situation in Yorubaland, Papa became the first kingsmaker to install a king alone when in 1993 the Lord blessed Owu with the HRM Oba Dr. Olawale Odeleye (Lagbedu I), Olowu of Owu, Abeokuta.  
Chief Simeon Isabade Lasile, Orunto Owu, Baale Egba will be forever remembered in Owu and by all those who came his way as a man of great wisdom and a ready mediator. His wise sayings were legendary and will be missed by all who were close to him.  
May his great soul rest in perfect peace. Amen!

title.rendered: Brief of Chief George Ogunpola (aka “Honest Man”)

content.rendered:
Chief George Akinola Ogunpola, fondly known as “Honest Man,” was born on September 11, 1932, in Ajegunle Village, Ewekoro Local Government of Ogun State.
His father, Elder Julius Ibikunle Ogunpola, was a respected member of Olusomi Compound, Totoro Road, Owu, Abeokuta, while his mother, Chief (Mrs.) Marian Adekanla Ogunpola (née Ojediran), was the Late Seriki of Owu Christians and an authentic member of Onsa-Isale Compound, Erunmu, Owu, Abeokuta.
George began his primary education in 1940, enrolling at Abalabi Central School in January 1941. He later transferred to Owu African Central School in 1946, where he completed his elementary education in December 1949. He distinguished himself by graduating first in his class of 72, earning the nicknames “Ever First George” and “First Among Equals.”
In January 1952, he completed a two-year Teachers’ Certificate Grade Il course at the African Church Teacher Training College in Ifako, Agege. He returned to the same college to complete the Teachers’ Certificate Grade Il course and subsequently taught there. A dedicated student, George studied privately to pass his General Certificate fo Education (GCE) Examinations, achieving his “O” Level ni 1957 and “A” Level ni 1959.
Chief Ogunpola’s carer in the Western Region Civil Service as an Executive Officer spanned from 1959 to 1961, after which he enrolled at the University College, Ibadan, where he studied Economics. He graduated in 1965 with a B.Sc. (Hons) in Economics. Following his undergraduate studies, he served as an assistant lecturer at the University of Ibadan from September 1, 1967, to September 30, 1968. He further pursued his academic interests by earning an M.Sc. in Economics from the University of Ibadan ni 1968 and an MA. in Economics from Manchester University, England, in 1970.
Chief Ogunpola had a distinguished academic career, marked by numerous accolades, including the Faculty of Social Sciences prize and the Sir James Robertson’s prize and medal for Economics at the University of Ibadan in 1964. He was also a recipient of the University of Ibadan postgraduate scholarship award (1965-1967), the UNESCO Fellowship Award ni 1966, and the Ford Foundation £50,000 Competitive Award for Research in International Economic Order (1975) with Drs. O. Ojo and Janet Farooq. He received commendations from the University of Ife’s Faculty of Social Sciences and the Appointments and Promotions Committee in 1976 and 1977, respectively. He was a Senior Lecturer at the University of Ife (now Obafemi Awolowo University) from 1967 to 1979.
He participated actively in the affairs of the University as an Assistant Secretary, Association of Ife University Teacher (AIUT) 1974-75, Vice President, AIUT (1975-76), National Secretary, Academic Staff Union of Nigerian Universities, 1977 and a member of the Nigerian Economic Society.
In September 1979, Chief Ogunpola was appointed as the Ogun State Commissioner for Education by Governor Olabisi Onabanjo. During his tenure, he successfully implemented the Free-at-all-Levels education programme of the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) government, a significant achievement in the state’s educational development. He continued his academic career at the Olabisi Onabanjo University from 1984 until his retirement in 1991. Chief Ogunpola is celebrated as the founding father of Ogun State University, Department of Economics and an icon in the service of Ogun State and Nigeria.
Chief George Akinola Ogunpola was married to Hannah Olabisi Ogunpola (née Ogunmuyiwa) in 1958 and later to lyabode Feyisayo Ogunpola (née Elegbede) in 1982. He is survived by twelve children-Olugbenga, Olufunmilayo, Olusola, Olubukola, Olufunmilola, Olubola, Akinsola, Oyinlola, Akindamilola, Akinfolarin, Folasayo, and Mojisola-as well as many grandchildren, great grandchildren, siblings, and extended family members.
Throughout his life, Chief Ogunpola was honoured with numerous accolades and chieftaincy titles, including the prestigious title of Baba ljo of the African Church. His legacy as an educator, civil servant, and community leader remains a source of inspiration to many. May his soul rest in peace, and may God continue to bless his family and all who knew him. Amen.
(September 11, 1932-June 15, 2020)
Omo Olowu Oduru, ajifepe s’ere. Sun ree

title.rendered: History Re-Asserted As Onipopo Enters Ipebi In Orangun’s Palace

content.rendered:
This week, an event of epic historical  importance played out within the Orangun’s palace in Ila. The newly installed Onipopo of Grand Popo in Republique du Benin, Sa Majeste Oba Adeshina Fagbemi Alahoussan Hélékétché entered Ìpèbí right within the palace of the Orangun of Ila. 
The new Onipopo by this act has wrestled back the direction of history, re-emphasised  and re-asserted his root and blood, earlier disrupted by the Europeans who haphazardly delineated and parcelled out Africa, an act that emptied out a significant space in a people’s history  and robbed people of their true identity and self consciousness. 
The most credible Yoruba history has it that Oduduwa had seven grandchildren who were in order of their ages, Olowu, Alaketu, Oba of Benin, Orangun, Onisabe, Olupopo and Oranyan (Alaafin). 
The Olowu kingdom no longer exists in its original single, organic  monarchical evolution but now has several metastatic kingdoms of which the Owu in Egba, Orile Owu and Owu Kuta in Osun are offspring. The Alaketu is now in Benin Republic and the Oba of Benin now identifies as Edo, leaving the Orangun as the eldest sibling to be the most appropriate host for the new Onisabe. 
The new Ipebi has a touch of artistic elegance and is enveloped in total sobriety and sacrosanctity. That is commendable given that Ipebi is  where a man communes with his ancestors,transits to a king, disrobed of his past identity and immersed in a new power, second only to that of the gods’. All thanks to Oba Wahab Kayode Oyedotun, the Orangun of Ila who led the effort to bring the new Ipebi about within a very short time.
Once out of Ipebi after tomorrow, the new Onipopo plans to visit the the Ooni at the cradle of Yoruba race and a few other Obas before returning to Benin Republic. Long may he reign.
Dotun Oyeniyi.

title.rendered: Orunto Descendants Meeting 2025: A New Chapter Unfolds

content.rendered:
We successfully convened our maiden meeting of the year, setting the tone for a promising 2025. The gathering commenced with heartfelt prayers (Christian and Moslem), comprehensive reports, and joyful celebrations, paving the way for a unified agenda.
As we build upon our accomplishments, we reaffirm our commitment to positivity, truth, and love – core leadership principles guiding our journey. This dedication remains unwavering, unshaken by distractions.
Awa lomo Orunto Baalufe Descendants, Omo Enlonka. 
Awa lomo Orunto Baalufe, Omo Enlonka! (We are the children of Orunto Baalufe, descendants of Enlonka!)
Together, we forge ahead, strengthened by our shared heritage and united purpose. No distractions!
Abiodun Lasile DL, MnbR 
Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta
(January, 2025)

title.rendered: Ibogun Olaogun Day 2023 Anniversary Celebration

content.rendered:
On Tuesday, December 26, 2023, a momentous occasion unfolded as His Royal Majesty Oba Prof Saka Adelola Adisa Matemilola FNSE Otileta VII Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom Abeokuta, graced the 2023 Ibogun Day celebration and extended his felicitations to Olu Ibogun of Ibogunland on the colorful anniversary. 
The Anniversary served as a platform for cultural enrichment and historical reflection of Ibogun Olaogunland.

title.rendered: A Legacy of Transformation: Palace Branding Revitalized

content.rendered:
A pivotal initiative spearheaded by Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile, prior to his ascension as Orunto Owu Kingdom Abeokuta, has left an indelible mark on the palace’s identity.
Recognising the absence of palace branding as a significant oversight before 2022, Abiodun took decisive action, transforming this deficit into a triumph.
Today, this project stands as a testament to his vision and dedication. To God be the glory for this remarkable achievement!

title.rendered: Meet Ali Baba, Nigeria’s King of Comedy!

content.rendered:
It is very creative of him to have shortened his name to Ali Baba because only his family members would have been privileged to be calling him by name. You asked me why?
Try calling this name, “Atunyota Alleluya Akpobome” He couldn’t have been relatable and accessible to his audience. In my mind…
He is professional Nigerian stand-up comedian, master of ceremonies and actor. 
Indeed, a great man in the Nigerian entertainment industry!

title.rendered: Olowu Of Owu In Abeokuta

content.rendered:
– Oba Pawu (1855-1867) (OTILETA I)
– Oba Adefowote (1867-1872) (OTILETA II)
– Oba Aderinmoye (1873-1890) (OTILETA III)
– Oba Adepegba (1893-1905) (AYOLOYE I)
– Oba Owokokade (1906-1918) (OTILETA IV)
– Oba Adesunmbo Dosunmu (1918-1924) (AMORORO I)
– Oba Adesina Aderinoye (1924-1936) (OTILETA V)
– Oba Adelani Gbogboade (March 1938- August 15, 1946) (OTILETA VI)
– Oba Salami Gbadela Adewunmi Ajibola (1949-1972) (AYOLOYE II)
– Oba Adebowale Oyegbade (1975-1980) (AKINJOBI I)
– Oba Michael Ayinde Oyelekan (April 29, 1987 – May 8, 1987) (AKINOSO I)
– Oba Olawale Adisa Odeleye (October 30, 1993 – June 11, 2003) (LAGBEDU I)
– Oba Adegboyega Dosunmu (July 14, 2005 – December 12, 2021) (AMORORO II)
– Oba Prof. Saka Adelola Matemilola Oluyalo (July 27, 2022 – present) (OTILETA VII)

title.rendered: A Memorable Encounter: Celebrating Life, Legacy, and Leadership

content.rendered:
Today, July 3, 2024, was a day of triple significance. It marked the 40th birthday of Prince Adedayo Tejuoso, a joyous occasion that brought warmth to our hearts. Concurrently, I had the privilege of visiting HRM Oba Dr. Adedapo Tejuoso, the revered Osile of Oke Ona Egba, to discuss the forthcoming “Kongi at 90” programme, particularly his tribute to the legendary Nobel Laureate.
As fate would have it, the rainy day transformed into a poignant moment of reflection, as I listened intently to the remarkable stories of late Chief Simeon Isabade Lasile (1914-2000), Orunto Owu and Baala Egbaland. This encounter not only deepened my understanding of our rich cultural heritage but also granted me valuable insights into the complexities of Egba history.
The highlight of my visit was receiving three thought-provoking books: “Ripples on So Far So Memorable (Egba History in Focus)”, “So Far So Memorable”, and “The Ultimate Honour”. These literary treasures have enriched my knowledge, offering a unique perspective on the intricacies of our collective past.
My time with HRM Oba Dr. Adedapo Tejuoso was, as always, a rewarding experience. Engaging with elderly leaders is akin to attending a revered school of life, where wisdom, experience, and firsthand accounts converge to broaden one’s understanding of the world.
Long live HRM Oba Dr. Adedapo Tejuoso, a shining exemplar of leadership, wisdom, and cultural stewardship.
Kabiyesi!

title.rendered: Sweet Memories: A Year of Leadership

content.rendered:
September 22, 2024 marks the one-year anniversary of my installation as Chief Dr. Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile, Orunto Baalufe of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta.
I vividly recall the traditional processes, meticulously followed to ensure a seamless transition. The official presentation to His Royal Majesty, Oba Prof. Saka Adelola Adisa Matemilola FNSE, Otileta VII, Olowu Oluyalo of Owu Kingdom, Abeokuta, remains an unforgettable experience.
365 days have passed, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to serve. Here’s to many more years of growth, progress, and service to the Owu Kingdom.

title.rendered: Fila: The Traditional Soft cap of the Yoruba People

content.rendered:
The Fila Gobi is a distinctive, soft hat steeped in tradition and cultural significance, worn by the Yoruba people of Western Africa. This iconic headpiece is expertly crafted from an array of luxurious materials, including:
– Hand-woven Aso Oke fabric
– Cotton
– Velvet
– Damask
Typically, the Fila Gobi or Abietiaja is lined with cotton for added comfort and durability. However, for special occasions or one-time events, it can be crafted without a lining, showcasing the artisan’s skill and attention to detail.
Fila completes a formal dressing of a chief.
This revered cap is an integral part of Yoruba attire, reflecting the rich cultural heritage and traditions of the Yoruba people.
One of the symbols of Omoluabi appearance in a cultural society, speaks about identity and customs.

title.rendered: The Installation of Chief Oladimeji Abiodun Lasile as the Orunto of Owu Kingdom: A Year of Transformative Leadership. -Adejola Adeyemi Crown

content.rendered:
On Friday, September 22, 2023, Chief Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile was installed as the Orunto of Owu Kingdom during a grand ceremony in Abeokuta, Ogun State. This is momentous event was marked by the presence of esteemed royal fathers, captains of industry, and professionals from various sectors, all coming together to witness the elevation of a leader who has made a significant impact within the community. As we reflect on the past year since this historic installation, it is essential to delve into the planning, execution, and outcomes of this event, as well as the achievements of Chief Lasile during his first year in office.
The Making of Orunto Abiodun Lasile…
The journey to becoming the Orunto of Owu Kingdom was not just a personal triumph for Chief Lasile but a testament to meticulous planning and execution. From the moment he received the title, he engaged in extensive preparations to ensure that the installation would be memorable. 
Planning is our forte at SixthSense, he stated, emphasizing the importance of strategic planning in event management. Lasile aimed to create a ceremony that would be remembered for a decade, a reference point for excellence in event planning. This goal was reflected in his rigorous approach to every aspect of the installation.
Strategic Planning and Execution…
The planning for the installation began in earnest after Chief Lasile received the official title from the family. He meticulously calculated the budget and allocated resources accordingly, with a clear focus on pre-event activities that would set the tone for the occasion. This foresight proved crucial, as it laid the foundation for a successful event.
Lasile shared insights into his planning process, revealing that he approached the event with a clear vision. I postulated that I would spend a certain amount and concentrated on the pre-event, which is the bedrock of acclaimed success, he remarked. He understood that goal-setting was central to effective planning. By defining specific objectives, such as the type of publicity and outreach, he was able to create a strong buzz around the installation.
A Grand Ceremony…
The installation ceremony itself was nothing short of spectacular. The venue was carefully chosen for its accessibility and traditional significance, which underscored the cultural heritage of the Owu Kingdom. The event attracted an impressive array of attendees, including royal fathers, dignitaries, and community members, all eager to witness the installation of the new Orunto of Owu Kingdom.
To ensure widespread awareness of the event, Lasile employed a comprehensive marketing strategy, utilising billboards and social media to promote the installation. Between 30 and 40 days before the installation, I filled all entrances of Abeokuta with promotional materials, he explained. This extensive campaign created anticipation and excitement in the community.
The ceremony was designed to be inclusive, reflecting Chief Lasiles commitment to engaging all segments of society. He envisioned the reception as a “Carnival Party,” aimed at celebrating not only the new title but also the community at large. By inviting 2,000 people, including those often overlooked, Lasile aimed to foster a sense of belonging and unity within the Owu Kingdom.
A Focus on Security and Logistics…
Recognising the importance of security at such a large event, Chief Lasile took proactive measures to ensure the safety of all attendees. He coordinated with security forces from Lagos to provide adequate protection and maintain order throughout the ceremony. Additionally, he engaged local community members, creating a sense of involvement and ownership among the attendees.
The meticulous attention to detail extended beyond security. Lasile ensured that the event was not only memorable but also well-coordinated. His commitment to quality was evident in every aspect, from the decor to the entertainment. I like quality but hidden beauty, he noted, emphasising his desire to create an aesthetically pleasing atmosphere that resonated with the rich cultural heritage of the Owu Kingdom.
Legacy of the Installation…
One year after his installation, Chief Lasile reflects on the impact of his leadership within the Owu Kingdom. He has embraced his role with fervor, dedicating himself to representing the Olowu of Owu, Oba (Prof.) Adelola Saka Matemilola, Otileta VII and serving the community. His year in office has been characterised by numerous achievements, initiatives, and a commitment to preserving the cultural heritage of the Owu people.
In a recent interview, Chief Lasile expressed his gratitude for the support and prayers he has received from the community. I’ve never been prayed for as much as I have experienced in the last year, he stated, underscoring the deep connection he has established with the people.
Contributions to the Owu Kingdom and Strengthening Community Ties….
Since his emergence as Orunto, Chief Lasile has focused on reinforcing community ties and fostering unity among the people of Owu. He has actively participated in various cultural and social events, representing the Olowu and advocating for the needs and interests of the community. 
One of his significant contributions has been the establishment of an interactive platform connecting Orunto families and settlements across the Southwest. During a meeting with the Ooni of Ife, Oba Enitan Ogunwusi, Lasile discussed the importance of preserving the history and cultural significance of the Orunto dynasty. This initiative aims to create a network of Orunto families, fostering collaboration and mutual support among members of the community.
Cultural Preservation and Advocacy…
Chief Lasile is deeply committed to documenting and preserving the history and traditions of the Orunto dynasty. His vision includes integrating ancient values with modern realities while discarding harmful practices. He aims to promote cultural awareness and appreciation within the community, ensuring that future generations understand their heritage.
My goal is to document our history, relationships, genealogy, cultural interactions, and traditions, Lasile emphasized. By focusing on cultural preservation, he seeks to honor the legacy of his ancestors and promote a sense of identity among the Owu people.
Infrastructure and Community Development
Under the leadership of Olowu of Owu Kingdom, Oba Prof. Saka Adelola Matemilola, several projects aimed at improving the living conditions of the Owu people have been initiated. The focus on community development includes the provision of essential services such as clean water, solar lighting, and vocational training programs.
“Within the two years of his coronation, is like ten years of development, he stated in reference to the achievements of HRM Oba Prof Saka Adelola Matemilola, the Olowu of Owu Kingdom. Lasile highlighted the importance of infrastructure and personal development training in empowering the community and fostering economic growth.
In the past year, he has spearheaded initiatives that have provided resources and support for small-scale businesses, encouraging entrepreneurship among the youth. By offering training and mentorship programmes, Lasile aims to equip the next generation with the skills needed to thrive in a competitive environment.
A Tribute to Legacy…
As Chief Lasile reflects on the past year, he also acknowledges the contributions of those who came before him. The recent passing of Oba Olufemi Ogunleye, Towulade of Akinale, has left a profound impact on the Owu community. Lasile described him as a library burnt, emphasizing the depth of knowledge and tradition he embodied.
Lasile expressed his commitment to continuing the legacy of cultural preservation and advocacy established by the late Towulade. He has pledged to honour his memory by furthering initiatives that promote peace, understanding, and collaboration within the Owu Kingdom.
Addressing Modern Challenges (Youth Engagement and Empowerment)…
Recognising the importance of youth engagement, Chief Lasile has prioritised initiatives aimed at empowering young people within the Owu Kingdom with the leadership of Oba Prof. Saka Adelola Matemilola, the Olowu of Owu Kingdom. The palace has launched programs that promote education, skill acquisition, and leadership development, ensuring that the youth are equipped to take on future challenges.
Investing in our youth is crucial for the future of our community, he stated. Lasile’s efforts to create mentorship programs and partnerships with educational institutions aim to provide opportunities for personal and professional growth.
Health Initiatives…
Chief Lasile, under the owu palace has also focused on health initiatives to improve the overall well-being of the Owu community. By coordinating health fairs and awareness campaigns, he aims to address pressing health issues and promote preventive care. His leadership in establishing health insurance projects has yielded positive results, providing much-needed support to community members.
My commitment to the health and well-being of our people is unwavering, he asserted. Lasile believes that access to quality healthcare is fundamental to the prosperity of the Owu Kingdom.
Environmental Sustainability…
In addition to social and health initiatives, Chief Lasile is committed to promoting environmental sustainability within the Owu community through the provisions of the Olowu and Owu palace. Recognizing the importance of preserving natural resources, he has advocated for sustainable practices and community-led environmental programs. 
By raising awareness about the importance of environmental conservation, Lasile seeks to foster a culture of stewardship among the Owu people, ensuring that future generations inherit a healthy and sustainable environment.
Looking Ahead…
As Chief Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile enters his second year as Orunto Baalufe of Owu Kingdom, he remains focused on the future and the challenges that lie ahead. His leadership philosophy centers on inclusivity, community engagement, and cultural preservation. 
In his discussions with the Ooni of Ife and other leaders, he is exploring avenues for collaboration and support that will strengthen the Orunto dynasty and enhance the welfare of the Owu people. Lasiles commitment to fostering innovation within tradition positions him as a forward-thinking leader who seeks to bridge the gap between the past and the future.
Final Thoughts…
The installation of Chief Abiodun Oladimeji Lasile as the Orunto of Owu Kingdom was not merely an event; it marked the beginning of a transformative journey for the community. Over the past year, Lasile has demonstrated exceptional leadership, dedication, and a commitment to the values of the Owu people.
As he continues to navigate the complexities of leadership, Chief Lasile remains focused on his vision of fostering unity, preserving heritage, and empowering the community. His journey as the Orunto is a testament to the power of planning, execution, and unwavering dedication to the betterment of the Owu Kingdom.
– Adejola Adeyemi Crown
Journalist and Publisher of tropic Reporters
